items.name: Chinese audiophile
items.lineage: Chinese audiophile repertoire brings Chinese-language songs and familiar melodies into carefully produced listening recordings. Labels such as Harmony connect Mandarin repertoire with jazz-influenced arrangements and an emphasis on recorded detail.
items.description: An exposed vocal line may sit over acoustic guitar and piano, with space for instrumental phrasing and subtle dynamic changes. The field emphasizes recorded clarity and presentation rather than a single mandatory ensemble.
exemplars: Jacintha — Love Flows Like A River (Harmony Records), Mandarin vocal/guitar/piano core

items.name: Chinese experimental
items.lineage: Chinese experimental music includes sound art and composition crossing acoustic instruments, electronics and recorded environments. Artists such as Li Yilei connect migration, memory and everyday surroundings with exploratory listening.
items.description: Synthesizer textures, strings, vocal samples and field recordings can form fragmented soundscapes. Changes in timbre, space and duration can organize a piece as strongly as melody or a regular beat.
exemplars: Li Yilei — 之 / OF (2021), synth/violin/guqin core

items.name: Chinese new year
items.lineage: Chinese New Year music accompanies Spring Festival celebrations across Chinese communities. Familiar festive repertoire appears in public performances, recordings and arrangements ranging from larger ensembles to solo piano.
items.description: Bright melodies and celebratory rhythmic gestures mark the seasonal setting. Piano transcriptions offer an instrumental route through the repertoire, while songs and ensemble versions serve other festive occasions.
exemplars: Lang Lang — Happy Chinese New Year (2014), piano arrangement branch

items.name: Chinese worship
items.lineage: Chinese worship music connects Chinese-language Christian congregations through original songs, ministry recordings and live worship. Stream of Praise has developed this repertoire for Chinese churches internationally since the 1990s.
items.description: Sung praise and congregational participation lie alongside instrumental devotional arrangements. Piano can carry hymn and worship-song melodies with chordal support, while worship bands provide fuller settings.
exemplars: Stream of Praise — With All My Love, Piano Series 2 (2008), instrumental piano core

items.name: Chip hop
items.lineage: Chip hop brings video-game music and chip-derived sounds into hip-hop production. Artists such as Mode 7 connect game-music sampling with rap and beat-making.
items.description: Rapped verses and looped beats meet melodic fragments and recognizable textures from game soundtracks. Chopped samples and layered sequences provide a production route alongside synthesized chip sounds.

items.name: Choro contemporâneo
items.lineage: Contemporary choro develops the Brazilian instrumental tradition through new compositions, interpretations and concert repertoire. Maurício Carrilho’s works and Paula Borghi’s performances illustrate its continuing dialogue with guitar music.
items.description: Melodic movement and rhythmic phrasing carry through solo guitar as well as ensemble settings. Fingerpicked guitar can combine an independent melody with bass movement and harmonic accompaniment.
exemplars: Paula Borghi — ten solo-guitar works of Maurício Carrilho

items.name: Christchurch indie
items.lineage: Christchurch indie draws on the independent bands and recording activity of the New Zealand city. Groups such as PATIENTS connect local songwriting with alternative and indie rock.
items.description: Electric guitars, bass and drums support sung melodies and contrasting vocal parts. Guitar-led arrangements range from direct hooks to rougher, more atmospheric rock textures.

items.name: Christelijk
items.lineage: Christelijk encompasses Dutch Christian music associated with worship, devotion and church life. Projects such as Psalmen voor Nu bring Psalm texts into contemporary Dutch-language song.
items.description: Clear sung melodies and chordal accompaniment support devotional texts and communal participation. Voice and acoustic guitar offer an intimate setting alongside fuller church and recording ensembles.
exemplars: Psalmen voor Nu — Licht, kom tevoorschijn (2013), published guitar-score realization

items.name: Christian a cappella
items.lineage: Christian a cappella uses unaccompanied voices for Christian song and worship. Congregations, quartets and vocal groups maintain harmony traditions through live singing, recordings and teaching.
items.description: Interlocking vocal parts carry melody, harmony and rhythmic support without instrumental accompaniment. Four-part arrangements are a prominent teaching and performance practice, with larger groups extending the same vocal texture.
exemplars: Acappella Ministries — Praise & Harmony training-disc quartet

items.name: Christian indie
items.lineage: Christian indie connects independent songwriting and alternative music with Christian texts and devotional themes. Artists such as Thief to King work across acoustic song, worship and band-based recording.
items.description: Sung melodies sit over guitars, bass and drums, with piano and organ adding harmonic color. Intimate acoustic passages and fuller band textures give the repertoire a range of dynamics.
exemplars: Thief to King — Your Decrees Are Very Sure (Psalm 93), Hail the King (2025)

items.name: Christian lo-fi
items.lineage: Christian lo-fi brings devotional music and hymn repertoire into intimate, deliberately modest recording practices. Home performances and simple recordings can preserve the immediacy of personal or congregational music-making.
items.description: Soft keyboard melodies and restrained arrangements support reflective listening. Audible room character and limited recording fidelity can become part of the presentation, alongside contemporary beat-based approaches to devotional repertoire.
exemplars: Tyler James Cook — My Wonderful Lord, The Lo-Fi Hymnal (2020)

items.name: Christian music
items.lineage: Christian music encompasses songs and instrumental works shaped by Christian belief, worship and devotional life. Historical hymn texts continue to receive new melodies and arrangements from contemporary songwriters such as Rachel Wilhelm.
items.description: Voice-centered settings range from intimate acoustic accompaniment to larger groups. Guitar, piano and sustained strings can frame hymn melodies with gentle rhythmic motion and layered harmony.
exemplars: Rachel Wilhelm — O Love With Heights Unknown (2016)

items.name: Christian uplift
items.lineage: Christian uplift gathers faith-centered repertoire associated with encouragement, consolation and hope. Hymn interpretations and contemporary devotional songwriting connect inherited texts with personal musical expression.
items.description: Clear vocal melodies and supportive accompaniment foreground the words. Fingerpicked nylon-string guitar provides an intimate folk-influenced setting, while other arrangements build a fuller sense of communal affirmation.
exemplars: Wilder Adkins — Nothing But the Blood, Oak & Apple (2011)

items.name: Christmas instrumental
items.lineage: Christmas instrumental music recasts seasonal songs, carols and associated screen repertoire without sung text. Solo arrangements and ensemble performances bring familiar melodies into settings ranging from home listening to concerts.
items.description: Instrumental melody carries the tune while accompaniment supplies harmony and rhythmic character. Solo piano can combine both roles, drawing on jazz voicings, classical phrasing and familiar seasonal themes.
exemplars: Steve T Hunter — Christmas Solo Piano (2020)

items.name: Cincinnati indie
items.lineage: Cincinnati indie grows from the city’s independent bands, songwriters and live music activity. Groups such as Old City combine local songwriting with alternative and indie-rock performance.
items.description: Guitar, bass and drums frame vocal hooks and introspective lyrics. Contrasting voices and shifts between restrained passages and a fuller band sound give the music its dynamic shape.

items.name: Clap and tap
items.lineage: Clap and tap is a South African choral practice connecting group singing with rhythmic hand percussion. Student and community ensembles maintain the practice through shared performance and cultural participation.
items.description: Blended vocal harmony combines with coordinated clapping and hand tapping. The voices carry the melodic texture while the hand rhythm gives the ensemble a clear collective pulse.
exemplars: Nelson Mandela University — Clap and Tap Student Society

items.name: Clarinet ensemble
items.lineage: Clarinet ensembles bring several players of the clarinet family together in chamber performance. Repertoire includes composed works and contemporary experimental pieces, as illustrated by John McCowen’s clarinet quartets.
items.description: Related reed timbres blend into layered melodic and harmonic textures. Independent lines, sustained tones and changes of register create contrast within an ensemble centered on one instrument family.

items.name: Classic Praise
items.lineage: Classic praise draws on widely circulated congregational Christian songs associated with modern praise and worship. Songs such as Henry Smith’s Give Thanks, popularized by Don Moen, continue through church singing and published arrangements.
items.description: Accessible melodies and chordal support invite participation. Voice with piano provides a clear, intimate setting, while other performances use fuller worship ensembles.
exemplars: Don Moen / Henry Smith — Give Thanks, published easy-piano arrangement MN0069487

items.name: Classic Schlager
items.lineage: Classic Schlager revisits the melodic German-language popular-song repertoire associated with singers such as Vicky Leandros. Songs from the 1960s and 1970s continue through recordings, stage performances and published arrangements.
items.description: Prominent vocal melodies, memorable refrains and clear chordal support carry emotional storytelling. Piano-and-voice arrangements expose the melody and harmonic movement of repertoire also heard in fuller pop settings.
exemplars: Ich Liebe Das Leben — ND-Verlag piano-and-voice arrangement 7070739

items.name: Classify
items.lineage: Classify gathers instrumental reinterpretations of familiar popular songs, including piano covers by artists such as Susan Tahmoosh. The repertoire brings widely known melodies into a more intimate instrumental setting.
items.description: A solo keyboard can carry the vocal melody above chordal or patterned accompaniment. Changes in touch, register and spacing reshape songs originally associated with more elaborate production.

items.name: Clean Comedy
items.lineage: Clean comedy presents humorous storytelling and stand-up material with restrained explicit language and content. Performers such as Dave Ross adapt stage material for this repertoire while retaining a conversational relationship with listeners.
items.description: Spoken delivery, timing, pauses and shifts of emphasis shape the performance. The comedian’s voice carries the material, with audience responses forming part of the live setting.

items.name: Cleveland Indie
items.lineage: Cleveland indie connects the city’s independent bands and DIY recording culture. Groups such as Biitchseat bring indie rock, jangle pop and emo influences into local songwriting and performance.
items.description: Interacting guitars and contrasting vocal parts sit over bass and drums. Melodic hooks and dynamic changes balance direct pop phrasing with a rougher band texture.

items.name: Cocuk Masallari
items.lineage: Çocuk masalları comprises Turkish-language tales told and recorded for children. Published readings connect local storytelling with translated literary tales, including works by Hans Christian Andersen.
items.description: A narrator carries the story through pacing, pauses and changes of vocal emphasis. Speech and characterful delivery guide young listeners through the narrative without requiring a fixed instrumental accompaniment.

items.name: Cocuk Sarkilari
items.lineage: Çocuk şarkıları includes Turkish songs composed and shared for children, alongside familiar lullabies. The repertoire circulates through family singing, educational settings and concert interpretations.
items.description: Clear sung melodies and supportive accompaniment foreground the text. Voice-and-piano recitals present one chamber setting for children’s songs, including works by Turkish composers.
exemplars: Şebnem Ünal and Verda Karaçil Cerit — Çocuk Şarkıları ve Ninniler, March2019

items.name: College A Cappella
items.lineage: College a cappella developed through student singing groups and campus musical traditions. Ensembles such as Yale’s Whiffenpoofs, founded in 1909, carry institutional songs, jazz standards and popular repertoire into touring performance.
items.description: Layered vocal parts supply melody, harmony and rhythmic support without instruments. Group blend and contrasting lead lines allow familiar songs to be reshaped for an all-vocal ensemble.

items.name: Cologne Indie
items.lineage: Cologne indie connects independent bands and recordings associated with the German city. Artists such as Blarg bring guitar-based songwriting into a local alternative-music network.
items.description: Sung lines and electric-guitar figures sit over bass and drums. Compact band textures allow melodic hooks and rhythmic changes to shape the songs.
exemplars: Blarg — Don't Stop Alice, Cologne Flashback Mix (2025)

items.name: Colombian Indie
items.lineage: Colombian indie draws on independent songwriting and band culture across Colombia. Bogotá groups such as Figueroa connect the field with alternative rock, garage and punk influences.
items.description: Electric guitars, bass and drums support melodic hooks and contrasting vocal parts. Direct rhythmic playing and rougher guitar textures can carry expressive, socially engaged songs.

items.name: Color Noise
items.lineage: Color noise organizes sound around broad noise spectra rather than conventional melodies. Different spectral balances and layered noise textures form sustained listening environments.
items.description: Continuous noise layers can vary in brightness, depth and density. A steady sound bed may develop through subtle spectral changes instead of a regular beat or pitched harmonic progression.

items.name: Columbus Ohio Indie
items.lineage: Columbus, Ohio indie connects independent bands, recording spaces and local songwriting. Groups such as The Kyle Sowashes bring a melodic, guitar-based approach to the city’s indie-rock practice.
items.description: Lead and supporting vocals sit over electric guitars, bass and drums. Direct hooks and changes in band intensity balance a rougher rock texture with tuneful songwriting.
exemplars: The Kyle Sowashes — The Least That You Can Do (2022)

items.name: Comedia
items.lineage: Comedia gathers Spanish-language comic performance, including stand-up and humorous storytelling. Performers such as Bobby Comedia connect personal observations with shared social experience.
items.description: Spoken delivery, pauses and changes of emphasis shape the rhythm of the jokes. A solo performer addresses listeners directly, with audience reactions providing the live performance context.
exemplars: Bobby Comedia — Los Espermatozoides Son Fascinantes (2017)

items.name: Comedienne
items.lineage: Comedienne highlights women’s comic performance across stand-up, storytelling and recorded comedy. Performers such as Giulia Rozzi bring personal experience and social observation into live and recorded routines.
items.description: Timing, conversational inflection and deliberate pauses carry the material. A single spoken voice can shift between narration and characterful delivery, drawing responses from the audience.
exemplars: Giulia Rozzi — True Love / An Embarrassing Story About Spring Break

items.name: Comic
items.lineage: Comic music uses song, theatrical delivery and musical parody to create humor. Songwriters such as Tom Lehrer connect witty lyrics with recognizable musical forms and piano-led performance.
items.description: Clear text delivery and sharply placed musical phrases support the joke. Voice and piano allow rapid shifts between storytelling, melodic emphasis and exaggerated stylistic gestures.
exemplars: Tom Lehrer — The Masochism Tango, voice-and-piano version

items.name: Commons
items.lineage: Commons gathers music shared through open licensing and reuse communities. Songwriters such as Josh Woodward circulate recordings and instrumental resources under Creative Commons licenses.
items.description: The repertoire spans musical styles rather than prescribing one sound. An acoustic songwriter branch combines sung melodies with guitar figures and chordal support, leaving space for lyrics and instrumental detail.
exemplars: Josh Woodward — Memorized, Creative Commons song branch

items.name: Comptine africaine
items.lineage: Comptine africaine brings together children’s songs, games and lullabies from African communities. Moussa Koita’s Burkina Faso repertoire draws on childhood memories of Bobo-Dioulasso and singing in Bambara.
items.description: Short refrains and exchanges between lead and supporting voices encourage participation. Acoustic guitar, hand drums, shakers and clapping can animate the songs, while gentler pieces support quiet listening.
exemplars: Moussa Koita — Setou Setou, Burkina Faso children’s repertoire

items.name: Concepción indie
items.lineage: Concepción indie connects independent Chilean bands working across garage rock, post-punk and melodic alternative music. Groups such as Sujetos Ficticios participate in the city’s recording and performance scene.
items.description: Electric guitars, bass and drums support lead vocals and backing responses. Direct song structures and melodic hooks meet rougher guitar textures and the energy of a small rock band.

items.name: Concertina
items.lineage: Concertina repertoire joins traditional tunes and newly composed instrumental music around the compact bellows-driven free-reed instrument. Rob Harbron’s English-concertina work develops this practice through solo settings and original tunes.
items.description: Bellows shape the attack and length of the notes, while button patterns carry melodies and accompanying figures. Dance tunes and slower pieces give the instrument space for rhythmic articulation and sustained phrasing.
exemplars: Rob Harbron — Meanders, solo English concertina

items.name: Connecticut indie
items.lineage: Connecticut indie spans locally rooted independent bands and songwriters. Acts such as zanders connect piano-led art-pop with the state’s alternative and indie-rock practice.
items.description: Sung melodies can move between conversational verses and more intense refrains. Piano and electric guitar share harmonic space over bass and drums, with ensemble dynamics shaping the songs.

items.name: Contrabass
items.lineage: Contrabass music places the double bass in a foreground role across composed and improvised performance. Solo work such as Carl Baugher’s bowed improvisations explores the instrument beyond its familiar supporting bass function.
items.description: Sustained bow strokes, resonant low tones and changes in pressure or articulation create an exposed instrumental texture. In solo improvisation, phrases and timbral contrasts can organize the music without a fixed accompaniment.

Production and instrumentation change across generations: solo voices and vocal groups appear over rhythm sections, keyboards and programmed accompaniment. Successive generations renew its close relationship with youth audiences and changing pop fashions.

items.lineage: Contemporary British alternative pop — melodic songwriting shaped by indie, electronic and art-pop production.
items.description: British alternative pop combines accessible vocal hooks with the less conventional textures and arrangements of indie and electronic music. Piano songs, guitar-led bands and programmed productions coexist within the field; intimate singing can sit beside layered keyboards, bass and percussion. Contrasts between familiar song forms and exploratory production are a recurring feature.

items.name: UK pop
items.lineage: British popular song — contemporary vocal pop drawing on a long interaction with rock, soul, R&B and electronic dance music.
items.description: UK pop is the broad contemporary British popular-song field, encompassing solo singers, groups, ballads and dance-oriented productions. Clear vocal melodies and memorable refrains commonly lead arrangements built from keyboards, guitars, bass, drums and electronic production. Acoustic songs and piano-led ballads sit alongside fuller band arrangements.

items.name: Ukrainian folk pop

Vocals carry the connection to folk repertoire while keyboards, guitars, bass and drums provide contemporary accompaniment; flute and other instrumental colors appear in some ensembles. Arrangements can draw on funk, jazz or electronic production as well as folk-rock.

items.name: Ukrainian pop
items.lineage: Ukrainian popular music — contemporary vocal songwriting across band, electronic and art-pop production.

Guitar bands, synthesizers and rhythm sections support a range from direct mainstream songs to more experimental art-pop. Regional groups such as Sumy’s Tvaryny illustrate one creative strand within the wider national field.

items.description: Jamtronica joins the extended interplay of jam bands with electronic rhythms, repeating grooves and synthesizer textures. Guitar, bass, drums and keyboards often operate as a live rhythm-and-texture ensemble, sometimes with vocals. Repetition provides a framework for evolving solos, transitions and collective improvisation.

items.description: Jugendchor denotes a youth choir, encompassing school and community ensembles with varied vocal combinations. Repertoire includes folk-song arrangements, composed choral works and contemporary songs, performed unaccompanied or with instruments. Blended ensemble tone and coordinated phrasing are important, while vocal distribution depends on the particular group.

items.name: Kabarett
items.lineage: German-language Kabarett — theatrical satire, political commentary and comic performance.
items.description: Kabarett uses wit, argument, character and theatrical timing to examine public life and social behavior. Spoken monologues and small-stage performance form an important strand, alongside musical and ensemble approaches. Political satire distinguishes much of its repertoire, while individual performers vary in tone from understated observation to confrontational comedy.

items.name: Future Ambient
items.lineage: Experimental ambient music built around evolving drones, transformed recordings and small digital details. Akumu exemplifies its use of environmental sound as musical material.
items.description: Slowly changing textures and spatial detail take precedence over a regular dance beat. Fragmented samples, layered atmospheres and sustained sound create a sense of depth and gradual transformation.

items.name: Chill House
items.lineage: A relaxed strand of house combining a steady dance pulse with soft synthesizer textures and spacious production. It overlaps deep house and lounge-oriented electronic music.
items.description: Rounded electronic drums support sustained chords and an unhurried harmonic atmosphere. Soft synthesizer textures and spacious production retain the steady pulse of house while reducing its harder edges.

items.name: Experimental House
items.lineage: House-derived electronic music that treats the dance groove as a framework for unusual sound design, modulation and compositional experiments. A_A connects floor-oriented rhythms with graphic-score and improvised electronic practices.
items.description: A regular electronic pulse can coexist with unstable timbres, noise, sparse passages and changing structures. Modulation and unusual sound design expand the expressive range of house rhythm.

items.name: French Tech House
items.lineage: The French producer and club network within tech house, combining house grooves with lean electronic percussion, bass-led hooks and loop-based production. Shiba San brings hip-hop-informed sampling and synthesis into this field.
items.description: Programmed percussion, repeating bass figures and short sampled phrases emphasize movement and rhythmic space. French tech house overlaps the international tech-house circuit while remaining distinct from the filter-heavy associations of French house.

items.name: Italian Tech House
items.lineage: Italy’s tech-house producer and club scene, represented by Stefano Noferini and related dance-floor networks. Its music connects house grooves with minimal, percussive and techno-oriented approaches.
items.description: Looped electronic drums and bass figures leave space for detailed percussion and gradual variation. Minimal arrangements and more forceful techno-oriented passages coexist within the regional club scene.

items.name: Japanese Progressive House
items.lineage: Japanese progressive house combines melodic electronic composition with the gradual development and sustained pulse of progressive house. Shingo Nakamura represents its connection to international melodic-house labels and audiences.
items.description: Layered synthesizer chords, repeating melodic figures and steady electronic drums build spacious, flowing arrangements. Melodic development and gradual changes connect home listening with the dance floor.

items.name: Mexican Tech House
items.lineage: Mexico’s tech-house scene connects local producers and club communities with the international house circuit. Andruss exemplifies its rhythm-focused electronic production and DJ culture.
items.description: A firm electronic pulse, repeating bass hooks and syncopated percussion create a compact dance-floor groove. Samples and vocal fragments add contrast within rhythm-focused arrangements.

items.name: Norwegian House
items.lineage: Norwegian house developed alongside the country’s disco and electronic club networks. Todd Terje and Lindstrøm exemplify its melodic synthesizers, dance grooves and overlap with nu-disco.
items.description: Electronic drums and layered synthesizers support buoyant rhythms and extended melodic development. House, disco and electronic pop meet in arrangements that balance repetition with expressive harmonic color.

items.name: Austrian Techno
items.lineage: Austria’s techno field includes electronic production and live approaches that translate repetitive dance structures into instrumental performance. Vienna trio Elektro Guzzi exemplifies the latter with interlocking guitar, bass and drums.
items.description: Repetition, precise rhythmic interaction and evolving timbre create a continuous dance pulse. Electronic production and live instrumental approaches coexist within the broader Austrian scene.

items.name: Dark Techno
items.lineage: A shadowy, forceful strand of techno emphasizing low-register weight, insistent repetition and abrasive or ominous electronic textures. Florian Meindl’s hybrid production and performance practice provides one example.
items.description: Drum synthesis, samples and modulated synthesizer layers support a driving pulse and gradual timbral changes. Dark atmosphere is a production tendency rather than a requirement for one particular rig, venue or tempo.

items.name: Greek Techno
items.lineage: The Greek techno scene encompasses club production and exploratory live electronics. Modular performance is one strand, alongside the wider dance-music community.
items.description: Repeated electronic rhythms and evolving synthesis create a dance-oriented framework. Regular grooves and improvised textures connect club production with exploratory live performance.

items.name: Hungarian Techno
items.lineage: Hungarian techno includes club-oriented production and experimental live electronic performance. Mári and Rozi Mákó connect improvised synthesis with noisy, industrial-leaning rhythms.
items.description: Drum voices and patched synthesizers produce insistent patterns, shifting textures and contrasting density. Industrial timbres and improvised structures form one strand within the wider scene.

items.name: Indian Techno
items.lineage: India’s techno community brings international club forms into local producer and live-performance networks. Mumbai-based Monophonik exemplifies its use of analog and modular synthesis.
items.description: Electronic drum patterns anchor layered synthesis, repetition and gradual timbral change. Studio production and live electronic performance connect local communities with the international techno circuit.

items.name: Irish Techno
items.lineage: Irish techno includes dance-floor production and experimental electronic work that draws on sampling, sound design and repetition. Lakker connects the scene with an exploratory approach to rhythm and recorded sound.
items.description: Programmed drums, synthesizer modulation and transformed samples support both driving passages and spacious textures. Experimental sound design and dance-floor repetition coexist within the regional field.

items.name: Scottish Techno
items.lineage: Scottish techno connects club culture with adventurous electronic production, including broken rhythms, bass pressure and sampling. Neil Landstrumm exemplifies its hardware-based, cross-style approach.
items.description: Drum synthesis, synthesizer voices and sampled material create dense, rhythmically varied arrangements. Broken beats, bass pressure and hardware improvisation extend beyond a single four-on-the-floor approach.

items.name: Techno Kayo
items.lineage: Techno kayō joins Japanese popular song and idol-pop traditions with electronic instrumentation, drawing on the influence of Yellow Magic Orchestra and early synthesizer pop.
items.description: Sung melodies and concise pop arrangements sit over electronic drums and synthesizer hooks. Idol-pop songwriting and electronic instrumental repertoire overlap within the field.

items.name: Deep DnB
items.lineage: A deeper strand of drum and bass emphasizing atmospheric space, restrained detail and low-end movement. It overlaps several drum-and-bass approaches without being synonymous with liquid, ragga or darkside styles.
items.description: Sampled drum patterns and synthesizer bass are shaped through spacious textures and carefully placed rhythmic details. Restraint and depth concern the arrangement and sound design rather than one fixed level of energy.

items.name: Minimal DnB
items.lineage: A stripped-back strand of drum and bass in which sparse percussion and bass movement carry the rhythmic structure. It overlaps deeper and experimental DnB without being synonymous with liquid or halftime styles.
items.description: Short drum phrases, space between attacks and focused bass movement provide the rhythmic foundation. Snare placement and density vary; sparse arrangement can reveal small changes in timbre and timing.

items.name: NZ DnB
items.lineage: New Zealand drum and bass connects electronic club production with an established live-band culture. Shapeshifter exemplifies the meeting of sung hooks, synthesizers, sampling and a rhythm section.
items.description: Fast broken rhythms, low-end drive and melodic vocal or instrumental passages support club tracks and live performance. Singing, rhythm-section instruments, synthesis and sampling connect electronic production with band performance.

items.name: Birmingham grime
items.lineage: Birmingham grime is the West Midlands city’s MC and producer scene within the wider UK grime tradition. Artists such as Mayday connect local identity with rhythmic verbal performance and electronic beats.
items.description: Rhythmic verses sit over sparse, syncopated programmed percussion and bass-heavy electronic material. Local language, MC exchanges and producer collaborations contribute to Birmingham’s place within UK grime.

items.name: Alabama rap
items.lineage: Alabama rap belongs to the wider Southern US hip-hop field, with local voices spanning rhythmic MC delivery, melodic hooks and varied production approaches. CHIKA is one prominent example.
items.description: Rap and singing combine with programmed beats, samples or live musicians. Melodic hooks, rhythmic storytelling and varied production connect Alabama artists with the wider Southern hip-hop field.

items.name: Austin hip hop
items.lineage: Austin’s hip-hop community includes producer-led rap and live-band approaches rooted in the city’s music scene. Magna Carda exemplifies the combination of MC delivery with an instrumental ensemble.
items.description: Rhythmic vocals interact with electronic production and live instrumental arrangements. The city scene overlaps broader Texas hip-hop while retaining its own artists, venues and collaborations.

items.name: Taraneem
items.lineage: Arabic Christian hymn and devotional-song traditions, practiced in church communities and contemporary recordings. Singing communicates sacred texts through both inherited melodies and newer arrangements.
items.description: Solo and group voices communicate sacred texts through inherited melodies and newer compositions. Accompaniment ranges from restrained chordal support to ensembles with keyboards, strings, plucked instruments and regional flutes.

items.name: Thai worship
items.lineage: Thai-language Christian worship music joins congregational praise with contemporary song forms and local church and recording communities. It is distinct from Thai Buddhist devotional traditions.
items.description: Lead and group singing are supported by chordal instruments and a rhythm section, with strings sometimes adding fuller textures. Congregational participation and devotional lyrics remain central across different arrangements.

items.name: Tibetan Mantra
items.lineage: Tibetan Buddhist mantra practice centres on repeated sacred syllables, including Om Mani Padme Hum. It extends from devotional recitation and chant to contemporary meditative musical arrangements.
items.description: Repeated sacred syllables and focused vocal delivery are central to contemplative recitation and chant. Solo and communal practices coexist, with accompaniment and melodic treatment varying by setting.

items.name: Tone
items.lineage: Tone-based listening music foregrounds sustained pitches, overtones and subtle changes in sound. Electronic tone recordings provide one approach within ambient and experimental listening.
items.description: Long tones and gentle variations invite attention to pitch, beating and timbre rather than song form or a drum groove. Listening may focus on a fixed frequency, changing overtones or subtle interactions between sustained sounds.

items.name: Transpop
items.lineage: A cross-style pop field connecting songwriting, performance and trans cultural visibility. Its repertoire encompasses acoustic song, rock and electronic pop rather than a single production technique.
items.description: Melody, lyrics and individual expression link acoustic song, rock and electronic-pop arrangements. The field crosses production styles rather than requiring one characteristic timbre or instrument.

items.name: Triangle Indie
items.lineage: Independent rock and pop associated with North Carolina’s Triangle region, including Raleigh, Durham and Chapel Hill. Local artists connect guitar-band traditions with keyboards and electronic production.
items.description: Song-centred arrangements range from spare guitar textures to layered pop and rock ensembles. Keyboards, electronic production and varied rhythmic approaches extend the region’s guitar-band traditions.

items.name: Tribute
items.lineage: Music made in homage to another artist, repertoire or musical legacy. Tribute projects cross genres and may closely recall their source or reshape it through a different instrumental and interpretive approach.
items.description: The purpose of homage links close stylistic recreations with substantial reinterpretations. Solo, vocal, band and orchestral approaches can all celebrate another artist or repertoire while bringing a new perspective.

items.name: Trio Batak
items.lineage: Batak vocal-trio music joins three-part singing with popular-song accompaniment. Groups such as Trio Golden Heart helped circulate the style through recordings and community listening.
items.description: Three-part vocal interaction, memorable melodies and chordal accompaniment give the trio format its identity. Acoustic guitars are prominent in early recording practice, alongside later expanded popular arrangements.

items.name: Trombone Brasileiro
items.lineage: Brazilian trombone performance spans popular repertoire, arranged ensemble music and concert practice. Trombone groups bring Brazilian melodies and rhythmic traditions into a distinctive brass sound.
items.description: Melodic playing, rhythmic articulation and ensemble voicing connect Brazilian repertoire with the trombone’s expressive range. Soloists and groups work with varied accompaniment, from small ensembles to larger concert settings.

items.name: Tropical
items.lineage: A broad Afro-Latin popular and dance-music field encompassing multiple regional rhythms and ensemble traditions. Contemporary groups such as QUITAPENAS combine voice, electric instruments and layered percussion.
items.description: Interlocking percussion, bass movement and sung hooks support social dancing and song. The umbrella encompasses multiple Afro-Latin traditions and contemporary combinations, broader than any single cumbia or salsa branch.

items.name: Tropical Alternativo
items.lineage: Alternative tropical music combines Afro-Caribbean and Latin American rhythmic traditions with independent rock, psychedelic textures and electronic production. Combo Chimbita exemplifies this cross-style approach.
items.description: Vocals, electric rhythm-section instruments, synthesizer color and traditional percussion create layered dance-song textures. Psychedelic and independent-music approaches transform Afro-Caribbean and Latin American rhythmic roots.

items.name: Tropical Tecladista
items.lineage: Keyboard-fronted tropical dance music, represented by performers such as Nelson Kanzela. The keyboardist’s lead role links cumbia and related dance repertoire with flexible electronic and live accompaniment.
items.description: Singing and keyboard-led melodic or chordal parts combine with bass and dance percussion. Ensemble size varies, with guitar, saxophone and other colors extending the keyboardist’s central role.

items.name: Trova Mexicana
items.lineage: Mexican trova places poetic songwriting and the singer’s interpretation at the centre of the music. Alejandro Filio and Fernando Delgadillo exemplify its connection between voice, guitar and lyrical expression.
items.description: Acoustic accompaniment supports the text, melodic phrasing and exchange between performers. Intimate solo and collaborative performances coexist with fuller arrangements.

items.name: Turin Indie
items.lineage: Turin’s independent-music scene includes guitar-led songwriting, experimental arrangements and small ensembles that expand their sound through effects. Giulia’s Mother exemplifies one inventive acoustic-band approach.
items.description: Voices, guitars and percussion can move between intimate song and layered amplified textures. Local artists share a regional independent context rather than a single instrumentation or sound.

items.name: Turkish Experimental
items.lineage: Turkish experimental music connects sound exploration, composition and improvisation across acoustic and electronic practices. Cevdet Erek’s percussion work is one example within this broad field.
items.description: Unusual timbres, changing structures and attention to the physical production of sound can take precedence over conventional song forms. Instruments, recordings and electronic processes support different approaches without a fixed ensemble.

items.name: Tzadik
items.lineage: The international experimental-music community associated with the Tzadik label connects composed music, improvisation and unconventional instrumental approaches. Its catalogue crosses genre and national boundaries.
items.description: Solo work and ensembles explore extended gestures, unusual structures and varied musical lineages. Marc Ribot’s solo guitar music represents one composed instrumental branch within the label’s diverse output.

items.name: UAE Indie
items.lineage: Independent music in the United Arab Emirates includes local, resident and visiting musicians working across song, rock, jazz and experimental settings. Dubai’s performance spaces connect these varied practices.
items.description: The field is regional and cross-style rather than a single sound. Tarek Yamani’s improvisational piano practice illustrates its links with jazz and Arabic musical ideas alongside the wider independent scene.

items.name: Ukrainian Indie
items.lineage: Ukraine’s independent-music field spans guitar-led rock, pop and experimental songwriting. Shoegaze and other alternative-rock approaches form one strand alongside quieter and more electronic work.
items.description: Vocals and a rhythm section support layered guitar textures, melodic writing and varied production. Bowed strings can add contrast without defining the instrumentation of the whole scene.

items.name: Ukulele Cover
items.lineage: Adaptations of existing songs for ukulele, ranging from vocal accompaniment to instrumental interpretation. Performers such as Cynthia Lin connect cover performance with accessible teaching and arrangement practice.
items.description: Chord patterns, fingerpicking and the instrument’s compact range reshape familiar melodies. Solo singing with ukulele is a common approach, while ensemble and instrumental covers broaden the possibilities.

items.name: Umeå Indie
items.lineage: Independent music from Umeå in northern Sweden encompasses several rock and pop approaches. Maha Sohona exemplifies a heavy psychedelic strand, with fuzz guitar and expansive space-rock passages.
items.description: Guitar riffs and a rhythm section can alternate between direct song structures and longer instrumental development. The regional scene remains broader than stoner or psychedelic rock alone.

items.name: Urbano mexicano
items.lineage: Mexican urban popular music connects rap, perreo, electronic production and melodic pop. Artists such as Kenia Os and Leon Leiden move between these overlapping song and dance communities.
items.description: Rhythmic vocals, sung hooks and produced accompaniment support varied arrangements, from beat-led tracks to songs with guitars and keyboards. The field overlaps Mexican reggaeton without being limited to it.

items.name: Uruguayan indie
items.lineage: Uruguay’s independent-music scene brings together rock and pop songwriting with local rhythmic and folk influences. Montevideo artists work across small bands and more richly arranged ensembles.
items.description: Vocals, guitars and rhythm-section instruments can combine with keyboards, strings and brass. Milonga and other regional ideas enter varied arrangements without making the entire independent field a traditional style.

items.name: USBM (United States black metal)
items.lineage: United States black metal brings together American bands working within and beyond the international black-metal tradition. Atmospheric writing, abrasive textures and varied local approaches coexist within the national scene.
items.description: Distorted guitars, bass, intense drum patterns and forceful vocals form a common foundation. Synthesizers can add sustained atmosphere, while arrangements range from raw directness to more expansive development.

items.name: Uwielbienie
items.lineage: Polish Christian praise and worship repertoire connects devotional singing with church communities and contemporary song production. Traditional sacred texts and newer compositions coexist across denominational and stylistic settings.
items.description: Lead and communal singing are supported by chordal accompaniment and, in contemporary arrangements, a rhythm section. Larger productions may add strings, brass or other colors, but no single album’s guest ensemble defines the practice.

items.name: Vaikiškos dainos (Lithuanian children’s songs)
items.lineage: Lithuanian children’s-song repertoire includes traditional and contemporary compositions for learning, play and performance. Lithuanian composers also cultivate accompanied songs for young singers.
items.description: Clear melodic phrases and accessible texts support singing, with piano or other accompaniment varying by setting. Composed voice-and-piano repertoire forms one concert and educational branch within this broader field.

items.name: Vallenato moderno
items.lineage: Modern vallenato extends Colombian accordion-centred song into contemporary commercial production. Silvestre Dangond and Juancho de la Espriella exemplify its connection between recognizable vallenato melody and expanded popular arrangements.
items.description: Accordion and singing remain prominent alongside electric instruments, layered percussion and studio production. Backing vocals, keyboards and programming can broaden the texture beyond the traditional small ensemble.

items.name: VBS (Vacation Bible School music)
items.lineage: Vacation Bible School music supports children’s Christian teaching, participation and praise. Repertoire emphasizes memorable songs that can be learned and sung together in church and educational settings.
items.description: Group singing and clear accompaniment help communicate stories and devotional themes. Piano and chordal guitar offer a simple foundation, while movement, ensemble size and additional instruments vary by programme.

items.name: Veena
items.lineage: Veena repertoire centres on the expressive possibilities of Indian plucked zithers and lutes. The Saraswati veena is especially associated with Carnatic raga and tala practice.
items.description: Ornamented melodic lines, plucked resonance and rhythmic articulation support composition and improvisation. Solo performance, accompaniment and layered contemporary work all contribute to the instrument’s recorded repertoire.

items.name: Vegas indie
items.lineage: Las Vegas independent music includes locally rooted rock and pop beyond the city’s large entertainment productions. Bands connect guitar-driven songwriting with punk, folk and other influences.
items.description: Vocals, guitar and a rhythm section may be joined by keyboards and other colors. Direct songs and varied arrangements reflect a local independent community rather than a single casino-show or commercial sound.

items.name: Venezuelan indie
items.lineage: Venezuela’s independent-music scene encompasses indie pop, folk-oriented songwriting, rock and related cross-style work. Caracas artists such as Aida Rojas connect personal songs with collaborative production.
items.description: Voice, guitars, bass, keyboards and percussion can create intimate or fuller arrangements. The field overlaps national rock and popular music without being confined to either.

items.name: Veracruz indie
items.lineage: Independent music from Veracruz state includes guitar-led pop and rock as well as experimental and progressive approaches. Xalapa-based artists such as Aqueronte contribute to this regional network.
items.description: Vocals and a rhythm section can combine with keyboards, changing rhythmic patterns and exploratory arrangements. The scene is distinct from traditional son jarocho while sharing the broader cultural life of the state.

items.name: VGM instrumental
items.lineage: Instrumental performance and reinterpretation of video-game music spans acoustic, electronic and amplified ensemble approaches. Familiar game melodies are adapted for listening and live performance beyond their original interactive setting.
items.description: Rock and metal arrangements often use guitar, bass, drums and keyboards, while other performers choose very different instrumentation. The absence of lyrics distinguishes instrumental adaptations without prescribing one production method.

items.name: VGM remix
items.lineage: Reworking and rearrangement of video-game music and sound, ranging from electronic dance remixes to experimental sample manipulation. Game themes and effects become material for new musical structures.
items.description: Sampling, editing and transformation can reshape melody, percussion, bass and sound effects. The field includes both recognisable reinterpretations and more radical treatments, distinct from composing an original interactive game score.

items.name: VIA (Soviet vocal-instrumental ensembles)
items.lineage: The Soviet vocal-instrumental ensemble tradition joined group singing with self-contained amplified bands. Ensembles such as Pesnyary developed distinctive repertoires and continued beyond the Soviet period.
items.description: Vocal harmony, guitars, keyboards and a rhythm section support popular songs, often drawing on folk material and varied arrangements. The band-centred format overlaps estrada while retaining its ensemble identity.

items.name: Victoria BC indie
items.lineage: Independent rock and pop from Victoria, British Columbia, grows through local bands, recordings and performance communities. It is part of the wider Canadian independent field while remaining distinct from Vancouver’s scene.
items.description: Vocals, guitars and rhythm-section instruments support direct songs and layered arrangements. Keyboards, percussion and guest contributions expand the sound beyond a fixed band format.

items.name: Vlaamse kinderliedje
items.lineage: Flemish children’s songs include family-oriented pop and entertainment-franchise repertoire associated with performers such as K3. Singing and memorable melodies connect recorded songs, shows and everyday participation.
items.description: Clear lyrics, recurring choruses and lively accompaniment make the music accessible to children and families. Electronic pop, band arrangements and simpler acoustic versions coexist within this repertoire.

items.name: Vocal ensemble
items.lineage: Music performed by a group of voices, spanning written repertoire, arranged songs and collective improvisation. Ensemble singing can be accompanied or unaccompanied and is not limited to one tradition.
items.description: Blended sound, contrasting vocal roles and interaction between singers shape the texture. Contemporary ensembles also explore breath, speech and freely changing pitches alongside conventional singing.

items.name: Voidgaze
items.lineage: An experimental extreme-metal field connecting dense, abrasive sound with atmospheric or more consonant passages. Aterrima exemplifies its overlap with avant-garde and blackened death-metal approaches.
items.description: Distorted guitars, bass, drums and forceful voices can alternate between turbulent density and more spacious writing. The field overlaps other atmospheric metal practices without implying one universal tempo or tuning.

items.name: Wagnerian singing
items.lineage: Singing associated with Richard Wagner’s operatic and concert repertoire, cultivated by specialist performers across different voice types. Waltraud Meier is one prominent interpreter.
items.description: Sustained phrasing, textual expression and a projected classical vocal tone support long dramatic lines. Orchestral performance, piano rehearsal and song recital provide different settings for the repertoire.

items.name: Washboard
items.lineage: Music foregrounding the washboard as a rhythmic instrument, found in small popular ensembles and several regional traditions. Its scraped and struck patterns can support singing and interact with melodic instruments.
items.description: The instrument contributes a bright, percussive texture through varied implements and attachments. Guitar and a bass-role brass instrument form one ensemble approach associated with the New Orleans group Tin Men.

items.name: Washington indie
items.lineage: Washington state’s independent-music scene includes Seattle and other local networks working across rock, punk, pop and experimental approaches. Bad Optics represents an art-punk strand within this wider field.
items.description: Guitars, vocals and rhythm-section instruments can be joined by synthesizers, tuned percussion or horns. Energetic songs and exploratory arrangements coexist across the state’s independent communities.

items.name: Wellington indie
items.lineage: Wellington’s independent rock and pop scene connects local bands with the broader New Zealand music community. Guitar-led and post-punk approaches are among its many strands.
items.description: Interacting guitars, vocals and a rhythm section support direct songs and varied amplified textures. The regional field is distinct from Dunedin or other city scenes without requiring a single characteristic lineup.

items.name: Welsh indie
items.lineage: Wales’s independent-music scene includes guitar-led rock, pop and other locally rooted approaches. South Wales bands such as Bedford Falls connect melodic songwriting with fuzzy amplified textures.
items.description: Vocals and interlocking guitars sit over a rhythm section, with arrangements ranging from direct songs to more layered rock. The independent scene overlaps Welsh rock without being limited to a single band or language.

items.name: West Virginia indie
items.lineage: Independent rock and pop from West Virginia draws on local bands, recordings and venue networks, including Morgantown’s music community.
items.description: Guitars, vocals and a rhythm section support varied song-based arrangements. The regional field is part of wider US indie music while remaining geographically distinct from Virginia.

items.name: West Yorkshire indie
items.lineage: West Yorkshire’s independent-music field connects Leeds and neighbouring communities through rock, pop and experimental songwriting.
items.description: Guitar-led songs can incorporate piano, keyboards and vocal harmonies alongside a rhythm section. Local scenes overlap within the wider regional network rather than sharing one fixed instrumentation.

items.name: Western Mass indie
items.lineage: Western Massachusetts has an independent-music community spanning rock, pop and cross-style songwriting. Northampton-area artists connect guitar-band practice with soul, art-rock and other influences.
items.description: Voice, guitars, bass and drums provide a flexible foundation for direct songs and exploratory arrangements. The regional scene is broader than one town or one stylistic formula.

items.name: Whale song
items.lineage: Recorded whale vocalizations offer a listening field distinct from recordings of ocean water or human music. Early recordings by Frank Watlington and Roger and Katharine Payne helped bring these sounds to a wider audience.
items.description: Long calls, changing contours and recurring sound patterns can be heard within an underwater acoustic environment. Recordings may present individual or overlapping calls, with no human singer or musical accompaniment required.

items.name: White noise
items.lineage: White noise is a continuous random signal with equal power per unit frequency across the represented bandwidth. It is distinct from pink and brown noise, which distribute energy differently.
items.description: Its broadband hiss has no fixed melody, meter or pitched instrumental role. Software generation and recorded playback are common ways to produce it; listening uses do not establish medical benefits.

items.name: Wind quintet
items.lineage: The standard woodwind quintet brings together flute, oboe, clarinet, horn and bassoon in a chamber ensemble. Composers explore the contrast and blend of these five instrumental colors.
items.description: Interlocking lines, changing registers and individual instrumental characters support a wide range of composed repertoire. Some works use doubling instruments, but the core formation remains a five-player ensemble.

items.name: Windsor ON indie
items.lineage: Windsor, Ontario’s independent scene includes alternative rock, grunge-influenced bands and other guitar-led music. Local performers connect Canadian indie practice with their own recordings and venues.
items.description: Singing, interacting guitars and a rhythm section support melodic songs and heavier textures. The city field is distinct from neighbouring scenes without requiring a unique instrument lineup.

items.name: Wisconsin indie
items.lineage: Wisconsin’s independent-music community spans Madison, Milwaukee and other local scenes. Indie pop, guitar rock and piano-led songwriting are among its intersecting approaches.
items.description: Vocals and a rhythm section may combine with guitars, piano and tuned percussion. Jazz-influenced harmony and varied arrangements form one strand within the broader regional field.

items.name: Women's music
items.lineage: Women’s Music names a feminist musical movement and its artist, label and audience communities, not simply all music performed by women. Songwriters including Margie Adam, Meg Christian and Cris Williamson helped shape its repertoire and institutions.
items.description: Lyrics, personal expression and collective participation connect acoustic song, piano-led writing and fuller arrangements. The movement encompasses varied musical styles while retaining its social and cultural history.

items.name: Worcester MA indie
items.lineage: Worcester, Massachusetts has an independent rock community connecting local bands, recordings and performance spaces. Evil Felipe exemplifies its guitar-driven indie and alternative-rock strand.
items.description: Melodic singing, interlocking guitars, bass and drums support direct songs and rougher amplified textures. The regional field encompasses varied independent approaches rather than a single band’s sound.

items.name: World devotional
items.lineage: World devotional brings sacred song and chant from different religious and cultural traditions into a transnational listening field. Yogananda-inspired chanting is one strand alongside other devotional repertoires.
items.description: Repeated melodic phrases, sung texts and instrumental accompaniment support contemplation and participation. Voice, harmonium, cymbals and tabla form one familiar chant ensemble; the wider field is not limited to Indian instrumentation.

items.name: World fusion
items.lineage: World fusion brings musical traditions into direct interaction through composition, arrangement and improvisation. Jazz musicians and cross-cultural ensembles have helped shape its varied instrumental and rhythmic language.
items.description: Voices, winds, bass and percussion can combine contrasting timbres and rhythmic practices. Improvised exchange and collectively developed textures are one approach within a field that also includes carefully arranged compositions.

items.name: Wrestling
items.lineage: Professional wrestling uses entrance themes and event music to establish character, anticipation and spectacle. Rock and metal are prominent approaches alongside hip-hop, electronic and orchestral music.
items.description: Recognizable hooks, emphatic rhythms and contrasting sections accompany entrances and promotion. Distorted guitar, electric bass and drums provide a common instrumental foundation.

items.name: Writing
items.lineage: Music programmed for writing is a functional listening field that draws on classical, ambient and other instrumental repertoires. Publishers and listeners often favor sustained concentration and a consistent atmosphere.
items.description: Piano-led arrangements can combine flowing melody, moderate dynamic contrast and an uncluttered texture. The listening purpose does not prescribe one composer, instrument or tempo, or establish a measurable cognitive benefit.

items.name: Wrock
items.lineage: Wrock, or wizard rock, is a fan-song movement inspired by the characters and stories of Harry Potter. Artists connect original songwriting with a shared literary audience and participatory fan culture.
items.description: Sung narratives and character-based lyrics appear in rock, pop and acoustic arrangements. Electric guitars, bass and drums support the amplified band strand of the movement.

items.name: Wuhan indie
items.lineage: Wuhan’s independent-music community includes alternative rock, indie pop and locally produced guitar music. Bands such as Flip Side connect the city’s scene with wider Chinese independent networks.
items.description: Vocal melodies, interacting guitars and a rhythm section support both amplified and acoustic arrangements. Varied textures and song structures coexist within the regional field.

items.name: Wyoming indie
items.lineage: Wyoming’s independent-music scene includes melodic guitar bands and other locally rooted approaches. Laramie musicians such as Wynona contribute to its regional recording and performance culture.
items.description: Singing, layered guitars and a rhythm section carry melodic songs and contrasting rock textures. Harmony vocals and energetic ensemble playing are common possibilities rather than a fixed roster.

items.name: Wyoming roots
items.lineage: Wyoming roots music connects regional songwriting with folk, blues, country and other American roots traditions. Jackson Hole artists such as Benyaro combine acoustic song with broader band arrangements.
items.description: Acoustic guitar, harmonica, piano, upright bass and percussion provide varied support for lead and harmony singing. Narrative lyrics and song-centered arrangements link intimate performances with fuller ensemble settings.

items.name: Xhosa
items.lineage: Xhosa musical traditions include communal song, personal and narrative singing, musical bows and other forms of vocal and instrumental expression in South Africa’s Eastern Cape. Nofinishi Dywili was an important bearer of the Ngqoko bow-song tradition.
items.description: Sung text, recurring phrases and resonant bow accompaniment create an intimate song texture. Collective dance-song and other vocal practices belong to the wider field; bow singing does not require overtone vocal technique.

items.name: Yemeni Traditional
items.lineage: Yemeni traditional music encompasses regional lyric-song and instrumental practices, including unaccompanied strophic singing in the north and lute-accompanied urban repertoires. Poetry and social gatherings are central contexts for many of these traditions.
items.description: A solo singer can shape verses through melodic contour, ornament and flexible pacing. Accompaniment varies by locality and occasion; the unaccompanied northern branch differs from, but does not replace, Sanaani song.

items.name: Yoga
items.lineage: Music for yoga draws on ambient, acoustic, devotional and other repertoires used alongside movement, breathing and quiet attention. Contemporary electronic composers have developed slowly evolving instrumental approaches for this setting.
items.description: Sustained tones, gentle changes in texture and environmental recordings can support an unhurried listening space. Musical choices vary with the practice; no single instrument or claimed health effect defines the category.

items.name: Yogyakarta indie
items.lineage: Yogyakarta’s independent-music scene connects Indonesian guitar pop, alternative rock and experimental songwriting. Grrrl Gang exemplifies its melodic guitar-band strand and international independent-label connections.
items.description: Lead and harmony singing, guitars, bass and drums may be expanded with keyboards and synthesizer layers. Direct songs and varied textures coexist within the city’s broad independent field.

items.name: York indie
items.lineage: York’s independent rock scene brings local bands and audiences into the wider British indie network. The Receivers exemplify its melodic guitar-band approach.
items.description: Vocal melodies and interacting guitars ride over bass and drums, combining direct song structures with amplified energy. Different bands emphasize pop immediacy, heavier textures or more exploratory arrangements.

items.name: Yugoslav New Wave
items.lineage: Yugoslav new wave emerged around the late 1970s and early 1980s through punk, post-punk and adventurous pop across the former Yugoslavia. Bands such as Haustor brought local songwriting into dialogue with international rhythmic and production ideas.
items.description: Electric guitars, active bass lines and drums support sung or declaimed vocals, with keyboards and saxophone adding contrasting colors. The historical scene includes varied approaches rather than a single national successor style.

items.name: Yunnan Traditional
items.lineage: Yunnan’s traditional music encompasses diverse regional and ethnic song traditions in southwest China. Folk-song repertoires circulate through local performance, collecting and later concert arrangements.
items.description: Melodic text-setting, repetition and vocal expression are central to many songs. Instruments and ensemble forms differ widely across communities; modern piano arrangements are one later presentation rather than a common requirement.

items.name: Yuri
items.lineage: Music associated with yuri anime and related franchises includes theme songs, character songs and live performances by their casts. Its connection to stories of relationships between female characters is a cultural and media context, not a single musical style.
items.description: Melodic pop singing, bright instrumental hooks and contrasting verse and chorus sections support many character songs. Acoustic performances and other arrangements coexist with electric and electronic pop production.

items.name: ZCC
items.lineage: The Zion Christian Church’s musical culture includes communal singing, choirs, bands and distinctive dance practices. Mokhukhu at Moria combines collective song and prayer with forceful, coordinated boot stamping.
items.description: Interlocking voices and repeated rhythmic movement support participation and worship. The song-and-stamp formation is one important branch alongside the church’s other vocal and instrumental ensembles.

items.name: Zespol Dziecięcy
items.lineage: Polish children’s ensembles and children’s-song repertoire connect group singing, family concerts and recorded entertainment. Both young singers and adult performers contribute to the field.
items.description: Clear melodies, recurring refrains and accessible accompaniment encourage listening and participation. Small keyboard-led ensembles and fuller instrumental arrangements offer different settings for the songs.

items.name: Zhenskiy Rep
items.lineage: Zhenskiy rep brings women’s voices into Russian-language rap and adjacent regional hip-hop communities. Artists such as AIGEL connect rhythmic poetry with electronic production, while individual repertoires may cross languages and incorporate singing.
items.description: Forward vocal delivery, repeated beats and bass-led electronic textures support personal narratives and contrasting flows. The field is diverse in production and vocal style rather than defined by one duo’s equipment.

items.name: Zillertal
items.lineage: Zillertal music connects the Tyrolean valley’s folk traditions with contemporary Alpine folk-pop. Dance tunes, communal singing and accordion-led ensembles remain prominent in its regional identity.
items.description: Steirische harmonika and accordion supply melody and rhythmic chords alongside guitar, bass and keyboards. Polka and Ländler rhythms coexist with modern song arrangements.

items.name: Zolo
items.lineage: Zolo groups eccentric art-pop, new-wave and progressive approaches marked by playful contrasts and unconventional songwriting. Sparks exemplify its theatrical vocal and keyboard-centered strand.
items.description: Angular hooks, shifting textures and tightly arranged contrasts can combine voice, keyboards, electric guitar and a rhythm section. Intimate reductions and elaborate band arrangements both occur within the wider field.

items.name: Zürich Indie
items.lineage: Zürich’s independent-music field includes experimental guitar rock, indie pop and cross-style songwriting. Artists such as Disco Doom connect the city with Swiss and international independent networks.
items.description: Voices, guitars, bass and drums can interact with piano and synthesizer textures. Repetition, melodic contrast and exploratory arrangements are among the scene’s varied approaches.

items.name: Funky Tech House
items.lineage: Funky tech house combines the lean rhythmic structure of tech house with syncopated hooks and funk-informed movement. Producers and DJs such as Simon Field connect it with contemporary club practice.
items.description: Electronic drums and repeated bass figures leave room for detailed percussion, short samples and melodic accents. Groove and rhythmic variation distinguish it without excluding overlap with funky house.

items.name: Saxophone House
items.lineage: Saxophone house foregrounds saxophone melody and improvisatory phrasing within house-music grooves. Live saxophone with a DJ and studio-produced tracks are both prominent formats.
items.description: Saxophone lines move over steady electronic drums, bass patterns and repeating harmonic material. Vocals may also appear, while instrumental versions give the wind instrument a central melodic role.

items.name: South African Deep House
items.lineage: South African deep house grows through local clubs, producers and DJ communities, connecting house rhythm with warm harmony and varied regional influences. Jazzuelle exemplifies its deeper electronic production strand.
items.description: Layered chords, bass movement and electronic drums support spacious, groove-led arrangements. Vocal, jazz-influenced and more stripped-back approaches coexist within the regional field.

items.name: Swedish House
items.lineage: Swedish house encompasses varied producer and label communities, including Stockholm’s eclectic Studio Barnhus network. Its scope reaches beyond any single commercial group or festival sound.
items.description: Synthesizer melodies, sample-based ideas and electronic drums support dance rhythms with changing mood and texture. Playful and understated arrangements coexist with more expansive club tracks.

items.name: Vapor House
items.lineage: Vapor house sits within online electronic and club-music culture, bringing house-related material into edited, cross-style arrangements. Artists such as Ben Aqua connect the field with experimental club mixing and digital production.
items.description: Sample fragments, repeating phrases and abrupt changes in texture or tempo create contrasting sections. Its relationship to house does not make every track conventional four-on-the-floor dance music or synonymous with vaporwave.

items.name: Australian Techno
items.lineage: Australian techno develops through local producer, club and live-electronic networks, including Melbourne’s scene. DJs and live performers connect repetitive dance structures with varied electronic sound design.
items.description: Electronic drums, repeating sequences and slowly changing synthesis provide a flexible framework. Hardware, software and hybrid approaches coexist rather than one performance controller defining the field.

items.name: Hard Industrial Techno
items.lineage: Hard industrial techno combines forceful techno rhythms with distorted, metallic and noise-rich electronic sound. Its production emphasizes pressure, repetition and abrasive contrast.
items.description: Heavy electronic percussion interacts with modulated synthesis, sampled impacts and dense transitions. Arrangements can alternate stripped rhythmic passages with sustained noise and layered textures.

items.name: Israeli Techno
items.lineage: Israeli techno connects regional producers and clubs with international electronic-music networks. Nadav Dagon’s drum-and-sampler performance illustrates one live approach within the scene.
items.description: Repetition and evolving electronic textures create a dance-oriented framework. Live percussion, samples and other electronic sources may interact, while conventional studio production and DJ practice also belong to the field.

items.name: Mexican Techno
items.lineage: Mexican techno includes club production and exploratory electronics that overlap ambient, dub and experimental sound. Murcof exemplifies its attention to texture, space and transformed recorded material.
items.description: Electronic percussion, evolving synthesis and processed samples support repetitive structures with changing density. Sparse atmospheric passages and more insistent rhythmic sections coexist within the broader scene.

items.name: Raw Techno
items.lineage: Raw techno emphasizes direct electronic rhythm, exposed timbre and less polished or more forceful production textures. Live hardware and modular performance are among its approaches.
items.description: Repeated percussion and evolving synthesizer patterns foreground physical pulse and timbral friction. Sound can change through performance and modulation without requiring a single fixed rig.

items.name: Somatik Techno
items.lineage: Somatik techno is associated with the experimental electronic community around Somatik Sound System. Its practice connects recorded-source construction, electroacoustic textures and techno-related repetition.
items.description: Edited sounds, layered recordings and contrasting density can produce rhythmic or more acousmatic passages. The field is not limited to a conventional club beat or a single sample collection.

items.name: South African Techno
items.lineage: South African techno connects electronic producers, live acts and dance communities with international club forms. Projects such as Atelier illustrate its overlap with house, song and instrumental performance.
items.description: Electronic drums and synthesizer sequences provide a rhythmic foundation, while some acts add singing, guitar or recorded phrases. Live and studio approaches coexist across the scene.
