items.name: Trance brasileiro
items.lineage: Brazilian trance connects progressive and psychedelic trance with the country’s festival, club and producer communities. Artists such as Vegas combine international trance structures with local musical references.
items.description: Electronic drums, pulsing bass and repeating synthesizer patterns build momentum through extended sections and releases. Melodic, textured and more percussive approaches coexist within the regional scene.

items.name: Trance mexicano
items.lineage: Mexican trance connects local producers, audiences and festivals with international psychedelic and progressive trance. Mandragora exemplifies a cross-style approach within this regional electronic field.
items.description: Pulsing electronic drums and repeated synthesizer figures build sustained dance momentum. Bass patterns, melodic hooks and textural changes can move between psychedelic, progressive and other club influences.

items.name: French DnB
items.lineage: French drum and bass develops through local producers, labels and events, including Toulouse’s scene. Artists such as Monty connect its detailed bass production with international DnB networks.
items.description: Fast broken drum patterns, low-end movement and contrasting electronic textures support varied forms of dance music. Sparse, heavy and more atmospheric approaches coexist within the regional field.

items.name: German DnB
items.lineage: Germany’s drum-and-bass scene includes established producers and club communities connected with the international genre. Current Value exemplifies its technically detailed and sound-design-focused strand.
items.description: Broken rhythmic patterns and substantial bass interact with precisely shaped electronic timbres. Dense, forceful arrangements and more spacious passages form different approaches within the scene.

items.name: Modern jungle
items.lineage: Modern jungle renews and recombines jungle’s breakbeat and bass language through contemporary producers, labels and club communities. Networks such as Rupture and Future Retro connect new records with the genre’s earlier repertoire.
items.description: Chopped breaks, sampled bass tones and rapidly changing rhythmic detail support fluid, syncopated movement. Fresh compositions and new versions of older material coexist with hardcore- and techno-influenced hybrids.

items.name: Russian DnB
items.lineage: Russian drum and bass grows through producers, labels, radio and event communities. GVOZD’s work with Pirate Station and Respect Records illustrates the scene’s local institutions and international connections.
items.description: Fast broken beats, bass weight and electronic sound design provide a shared foundation. Individual producers range from atmospheric and melodic material to more forceful and technically dense tracks.

items.name: South African DnB
items.lineage: South African drum and bass develops through local DJs, producers and club networks, including Cape Town’s It Came From The Jungle community. Niskerone helped connect this scene with national broadcasting and international repertoire.
items.description: Fast syncopated drums and bass-led electronic arrangements underpin dance-oriented tracks. The regional field includes varied moods and production styles rather than one fixed club programme.

items.name: Bass trip
items.lineage: Bass trip connects jazz, funk and beat-oriented improvisation within a cross-style discovery field. Groups such as BRZZVLL bring live instrumental interaction into dance-oriented grooves.
items.description: Active bass and drums support saxophone, guitar and keyboard interplay. Repeated figures, collective improvisation and changing textures connect the music with jazz fusion, Afro-funk and rare groove.

items.name: Experimental dubstep
items.lineage: Experimental dubstep stretches dubstep’s bass-weighted rhythmic language through sound design and cross-style production. Acts such as Symbiz Sound connect it with dancehall, hip-hop and other bass-music approaches.
items.description: Electronic drums, low-frequency synthesis and transformed sounds can interact with live MC delivery. Broken patterns, timbral contrast and flexible arrangements need not follow a single conventional dubstep formula.

items.name: Grime brasileiro
items.lineage: Brazilian grime develops through local MCs, DJs and producers adapting grime’s rhythmic language to Brazilian scenes and languages. Brasil Grime Show helped establish a platform for performances and exchanges.
items.description: Rhythmic verse and freestyle delivery move over sparse, forceful electronic beats. Repeating patterns and bass-led production leave space for individual flows and exchanges between MCs.

items.name: Hard bass
items.lineage: Hard bass, or hardbass, is a dance style associated with pumping and bumping house and the Saint Petersburg scene’s links with Dutch club music. Its identity involves a distinctive rhythmic and bass-sound vocabulary rather than loud bass alone.
items.description: A firm four-beat pulse and short, resonant synthesized bass figures create a bouncing drive. Repeated hooks and direct contrasts organize the arrangement for dancing.

items.name: Kawaii future bass
items.lineage: Kawaii future bass joins colorful electronic production with Japanese pop, anime-adjacent aesthetics and dance-music influences. Producers such as Moe Shop connect bright melodic writing with bass-led club sounds.
items.description: Playful samples, short vocal fragments, buoyant bass and layered synthesizers create a polished, animated texture. Chord changes, melodic hooks and detailed transitions balance sweetness with rhythmic weight.

items.name: Russian grime
items.lineage: Russian grime adapts grime’s electronic rhythmic language to Russian-language MC performance and local rap communities. Recorded tracks, live exchanges and unaccompanied verses provide different settings for the same vocal practice.
items.description: Rhythmic speech and sharply articulated flows ride sparse, syncopated electronic beats. Producers and MCs use bass pressure, repeated figures and space between sounds to emphasize the delivery.

items.name: Afghan rap
items.lineage: Afghan rap develops within Afghanistan and its diaspora, bringing hip-hop forms to experiences of migration, conflict and everyday life. Artists such as Ali ATH and Zartosht connect local languages and concerns with international rap culture.
items.description: Rhythmic verses, sampled or programmed beats and occasional sung hooks support direct storytelling and commentary. Solo performances and exchanges between MCs coexist with both accompanied and unaccompanied formats.

items.name: Albanian hip hop
items.lineage: Albanian hip-hop spans Albania, Kosovo and diaspora communities, linking local language and identity with international rap production. Diaspora performers such as Dardan also work across languages and national scenes.
items.description: Rhythmic verses and melodic hooks interact with programmed drums, bass and sampled or synthesized phrases. Production ranges from spare rap arrangements to more layered pop and trap approaches.

items.name: Arkansas hip hop
items.lineage: Arkansas hip-hop connects regional MCs, producers and live performers with wider Southern rap traditions. Little Rock artists such as Big Piph illustrate the scene’s links between rhythmic verse, community storytelling and band performance.
items.description: Rap delivery, hooks and beat-driven arrangements support varied lyrical approaches. Electronic production and live rhythm sections offer different ways to shape the groove.

items.name: Aussie drill
items.lineage: Australian drill developed through local rap communities drawing on British and American drill while expressing Australian neighbourhood experience. Mount Druitt group ONEFOUR became an important reference point.
items.description: Forceful rhythmic verses move over sparse electronic percussion and sliding bass. Group exchanges, hooks and occasional live-band treatments extend the basic beat-led format.

items.name: Bangladeshi hip hop

items.name: Bulgarian Trap

items.name: Japanese Chill Rap

items.name: Old School UK Hip Hop

items.name: Perth Hip Hop
items.lineage: Perth hip-hop develops through Western Australian MCs, producers and independent performance networks. Freestyle and recorded rap provide complementary outlets within this regional community.
items.description: Rhythmic verses and repeated beat patterns foreground vocal flow and local expression. Sampled or programmed drums and bass support varied melodic and lyrical approaches.

items.name: Peruvian Hip Hop
items.lineage: Peruvian hip-hop connects local MCs and producers through independent releases and performance communities, including Lima’s rap networks. Artists such as Mseco work within a national field broader than any single trap or boom-bap style.

items.name: Pinoy Hip Hop

items.description: Rap verses and sung hooks interact with programmed beats, samples or live rhythm sections. Multilingual delivery and flexible instrumental arrangements allow both direct MC tracks and more expansive band performances.

items.name: Polish Hip Hop
items.lineage: Polish hip-hop includes national MC, producer and DJ communities, with independent and mainstream branches. Artists such as Jakub Jan Bryndal connect rap with electronic production and live instrumental experimentation.
items.description: Rhythmic verse sits over sampled phrases, electronic percussion and bass. Keys, live drums and other instrumental colors can broaden the arrangement while preserving the emphasis on flow and language.

items.name: Rap Alagoano

items.description: Rhythmic verses and vocal hooks interact with beat production or guitar-led rhythm sections. Soul, reggae and other influences can enrich the groove without defining a fixed ensemble for the entire scene.

items.name: V-pop
items.lineage: V-pop denotes Vietnamese popular music and its recording, performance and fan communities. Artists such as Sơn Tùng M-TP connect local songwriting and language with contemporary international pop production.
items.description: Sung hooks and melodic verses interact with keyboards, programmed drums and chordal accompaniment. Dance-oriented songs, lyrical ballads and acoustic versions give the field a wide range of rhythmic and textural contrasts.

items.name: Yemeni Pop
items.lineage: Yemeni pop adapts Yemeni song and poetic traditions within contemporary regional and diaspora music. Artists such as SHIRAN combine inherited melodies and expression with electronic and band-based popular production.
items.description: Ornamented singing and plucked-string phrases interact with bass, percussion and keyboard textures. Repeated grooves and melodic refrains connect intimate song expression with dance-oriented arrangements.

items.name: Acid IDM
items.lineage: Acid IDM connects the resonant bass sequences of acid music with experimental electronic rhythm and arrangement. Performers such as Surreal Pneuma work across live machine performance, hypnotic repetition and fragmented structures.
items.description: Squelching bass patterns interact with drum-machine pulses, edited rhythmic layers and changing electronic textures. Repetition provides a frame for variations in phrasing, modulation and the density of programmed events.

items.name: Arab Electronic
items.lineage: Arab electronic music develops through producers, singers, DJs and experimental musicians across Arab countries and diaspora networks. Contemporary club scenes bring Arabic vocal and melodic expression into house, techno and other electronic approaches.
items.description: Synthesized bass, programmed drums and layered electronic phrases support both dance-oriented tracks and exploratory work. Singing, sampled voices and regional instrumental colors enter in different combinations across artists.

items.name: Bosnian Electronic
items.lineage: Bosnian electronic music grows through local producers, club nights, labels and international DJ networks. Mladen Tomic and Sinisa Tamamovic connect Banja Luka’s scene with house and techno production and performance.
items.description: Repeating electronic drums and bass figures support gradual changes in percussion, synth patterns and arrangement. DJ sets and studio productions share an emphasis on sustained groove while leaving room for more varied electronic approaches.

items.name: Vietnamese electronic
items.lineage: Vietnamese electronic music connects club production with experimental sound art and electroacoustic composition. Artists such as Sound Awakener explore recorded environments and processed acoustic sources alongside other forms of electronic practice.
items.description: Environmental recordings, transformed instrumental sounds and layered textures create an exploratory listening space. Dance-oriented work belongs to the broader scene, while its sound-art branches emphasize timbre, space and changing sonic relationships.

items.name: Tulum
items.lineage: Tulum music centers the double-chanter bagpipe traditions of the eastern Black Sea region. Hemşin, Laz and related communities use its sustained, ornamented sound in dance, wedding and other local repertoires.
items.description: Continuous bag pressure supports paired reed lines and closely articulated melodic figures. Driving horon passages contrast with freer song airs, while repeated patterns and variations connect the instrument to communal movement and celebration.

items.name: Turkish Alternative
items.lineage: Turkish alternative music connects independent songwriting, guitar bands and electronic experimentation across a varied national scene. Artists such as Taner Öngür and Tuğçe Şenoğul illustrate exchanges among rock, psychedelic textures and contemporary song production.
items.description: Voices, electric guitars, bass and drums provide one common band setting, while electronic collaborations broaden the palette. Repeated riffs, melodic lines and changing dynamics support both sung songs and instrumental work.

items.name: Turkish Soundtrack
items.lineage: Turkish soundtrack music serves film and television storytelling through composed instrumental cues and songs. Composers such as Ahmet Kenan Bilgiç and Gökhan Kırdar draw on acoustic instruments, electronic production and diverse local musical references.
items.description: Recurring motifs, harmonic support and changes in timbre connect music with dramatic pacing. Guitar, piano and synthesized textures can create intimate or expansive settings, with ensembles and voices varying according to the production.

items.name: UK Worship
items.lineage: UK worship music develops through churches, congregations and songwriters such as Graham Kendrick. Contemporary hymn writing and band-led worship connect biblical texts and communal singing with changing popular-song styles.
items.description: Accessible melodies and repeated refrains encourage participation. Voices are supported by guitar, piano, bass and drums, while smaller acoustic or choral settings offer quieter forms of shared devotion.

items.name: Ukrainian Experimental
items.lineage: Ukrainian experimental music brings composition, improvisation and unconventional sound practices into dialogue. Artists such as Ihor Tsymbrovsky connect poetry and exploratory singing with minimal keyboard forms, alongside other electronic and instrumental approaches.
items.description: Voice, piano and organ can create spare, evolving textures in which repetition and variation shape the music. Other branches foreground processed sound, ensemble interaction or less conventional musical structures.

items.name: Vinahouse
items.lineage: Vinahouse is a Vietnamese club-music practice shaped through local DJs, remixes and electronic production. Vietnamese popular and folk-derived vocal material is often reworked into energetic dance arrangements.
items.description: Programmed drums, insistent bass and bright synth phrases support recurring vocal hooks and rapid textural changes. Repetition and layered rhythmic production keep the music oriented toward sustained dancing.

items.name: Mexican classic rock
items.lineage: Mexican classic rock gathers foundational rock repertoire and the countercultural scenes that developed around it. Bands such as Toncho Pilatos, Los Dug Dug’s and El Ritual connect blues and psychedelic influences with local expression.
items.description: Electric guitar riffs and melodic leads interact with bass, drums and direct singing. Harmonica and other colors can reinforce blues-derived phrasing, while Mexican rhythmic and melodic references reshape the band sound.
exemplars: Toncho Pilatos — Segunda Vez, complete1980 ten-track album

items.name: Rock Nacional Feminino
items.lineage: Rock nacional feminino highlights women-fronted projects across Brazil’s rock and underground scenes. Collections such as A Cena é Delas bring together bands working in varied rock, punk and metal approaches.
items.description: Vocals, distorted guitars, bass and drums form a flexible amplified core. Strong riffs and dynamic contrast support many kinds of singing and heavier delivery, rather than a single style determined by the performers’ gender.

items.name: Eritrean pop
items.lineage: Eritrean pop brings several languages and regional rhythmic traditions into modern popular song. Groups such as Asmara All Stars connect local dance approaches, including gwaila, with amplified band arrangements.
items.description: Lead singing, guitar, bass and keyboards interact with drums and hand percussion. Saxophone lines and group clapping can add contrasting accents around recurring melodies and grooves.

items.name: Garhwali pop
items.lineage: Garhwali pop connects regional language, melody and cultural identity with contemporary songwriting and recording in Uttarakhand and its diaspora. Singers may also move into Hindi and other popular repertoires.
items.description: Melodic verses and refrains are supported by guitar and other chordal accompaniment, with electronic and fuller band arrangements offering alternatives. Solo and duet singing connect lyrical expression with regional musical memory.

items.name: Himachali pop
items.lineage: Himachali pop brings regional song and identity into contemporary popular recording and performance. Artists range across acoustic, electronic and amplified-band settings; Moksh illustrates a rock-based reinterpretation of inherited repertoire.
items.description: Voices and memorable melodic figures interact with guitars, bass and rhythmic accompaniment. Traditional material may be reworked through contemporary production, with intensity and instrumentation varying widely across artists.

items.name: J-pop girl group
items.lineage: Japanese girl-group pop develops through vocal ensembles, entertainment production and fan communities. Groups such as Perfume connect coordinated singing and performance with electronic pop, while other acts draw on varied band and idol traditions.
items.description: Group hooks, repeated melodic lines and layered vocals interact with electronic drums and keyboard textures. Dance-oriented arrangements and ballads offer different settings for ensemble identity and individual voices.

items.name: K-pop reality show
items.lineage: K-pop reality-show repertoire emerges from televised auditions, competition projects and the careers they launch. Groups such as I.O.I and Wanna One connect these production institutions with the wider Korean pop industry.
items.description: Coordinated group vocals, prominent hooks and rhythmic electronic accompaniment support stage performance. Melodic singing, rap passages, ballads and dance-pop arrangements vary across projects and releases.

items.name: Malagasy pop
items.lineage: Malagasy pop connects Malagasy-language expression and Madagascar’s musical cultures with contemporary recording and diaspora collaboration. Local and international influences meet in acoustic songs, amplified bands and electronic productions.
items.description: Voices, interlocking instrumental figures and recurring refrains support varied popular-song forms. Guitar, bass, keyboards and percussion can provide a flexible band texture around melodic and rhythmic regional influences.

items.name: Pop argentino
items.lineage: Argentine pop connects national songwriting, recording and performance communities across band-based and electronic styles. Artists range from independent groups such as Komo Yamarte to major pop performers including Lali and Diego Torres.
items.description: Sung melodies and memorable refrains interact with guitar, bass, keyboards and drums. Dance-oriented production, lyrical ballads and rock-inflected arrangements overlap within this varied popular repertoire.

items.name: Pop costarricense
items.lineage: Costa Rican pop develops through national performers and international recording networks. Artists such as Debi Nova connect personal songwriting and piano-led performance with broader Latin popular-music approaches.
items.description: Lead singing and melodic hooks sit over chordal support and a flexible rhythm section. Intimate acoustic passages contrast with fuller band arrangements and dance-oriented production.

items.name: Pop peruano
items.lineage: Peruvian pop connects national songwriting and performance with wider Spanish-language popular music. Singers such as Gian Marco work across lyrical acoustic songs, band arrangements and contemporary recording styles.
items.description: Vocal melody, chord progressions and recurring refrains organize the songs. Guitar and keyboards provide harmonic support, with bass and drums adding rhythmic weight in fuller arrangements.

items.name: Pop virale italiano
items.lineage: Italian viral pop circulates through social platforms, streaming and established popular-song institutions. Artists such as Olly connect melodic Italian songwriting with online discovery and fan-made audiovisual sharing.
items.description: Memorable vocal hooks and recurring accompaniment figures make songs recognizable across changing listening contexts. Acoustic instruments, keyboards and electronic rhythm tracks support both ballads and more energetic pop.

items.name: Réunion pop
items.lineage: Réunion pop connects the island’s contemporary songwriting with soul, jazz, hip-hop and other popular styles. Groups such as DRÉO belong to a varied scene that overlaps local musical traditions without being confined to one dance or ancestral repertoire.
items.description: Lead vocals and chordal keyboards interact with bass and drums in one common band setting. Changes in rhythm, vocal phrasing and arrangement allow intimate songs and more groove-centered passages to coexist.

items.name: Russian alt pop
items.lineage: Russian alternative pop connects distinctive songwriting and vocal expression with independent production and performance communities. Artists such as OQJAV move between keyboard-led intimacy, electronic arrangements and other contemporary song forms.
items.description: Voice and recurring melodic or harmonic figures remain central while textures change around them. Piano, synthesized layers and rhythmic production can alternate with sparse passages and improvised links.

items.name: Samoan pop
items.lineage: Samoan pop connects island song, local and diaspora identity with contemporary popular music. Artists such as Bobby Alu bring ukulele, rhythm and soul influences into both acoustic and amplified settings.
items.description: Sung melodies and harmonies ride over strummed strings, bass and percussion. Repeating chordal figures and flexible grooves support relaxed song delivery as well as more rhythmic public performances.

items.name: South Sudanese pop
items.lineage: South Sudanese pop connects regional languages and song traditions with contemporary band and recording practices. Musicians such as Gordon Koang bring Nuer rhythmic and melodic expression into local and diaspora popular music.
items.description: Lead singing and repeated melodic figures interact with bass, keyboards and percussion. The thom and other regional instruments can retain a distinct place within amplified ensembles, alongside varied acoustic and electronic approaches.

items.name: Spanish noise pop
items.lineage: Spanish noise pop combines melodic songwriting with distorted guitar textures and independent-band culture. Groups such as Alborotador Gomasio connect 1990s noise-pop and shoegaze influences with punk-pop energy.
items.description: Sung hooks and repeated guitar figures move against bass and driving drums. Fuzz, dynamic contrasts and layered textures give accessible melodies a rougher surface, while acoustic and keyboard colors broaden some arrangements.

items.name: Taiwan idol pop
items.lineage: Taiwan idol pop develops through performers whose music, screen appearances and fan communities are closely connected. Groups such as F4 illustrate the relationship between television drama, vocal-group careers and popular-song repertoire.
items.description: Group and solo vocals carry memorable melodies over keyboard-led and rhythmic pop arrangements. Ballads and dance-oriented songs offer contrasting settings for shared group identity and individual performers.

items.name: Tunisian pop
items.lineage: Tunisian pop connects national and diaspora songwriting with a range of contemporary popular styles. Artists such as Jawhar and Saber Rebai span intimate folk-influenced work and broader mainstream recording networks.
items.description: Expressive singing sits over chordal and rhythmic accompaniment. Guitar, keyboards, bass and percussion support melodic refrains, while acoustic, electric-piano and electronic textures vary across projects.

items.name: Ukrainian viral pop
items.lineage: Ukrainian viral pop circulates through social platforms, streaming and contemporary song communities. Acts such as Tember Blanche connect memorable melodies and acoustic songwriting with internet-led discovery.
items.description: Vocal hooks and repeated accompaniment patterns make songs recognizable in short-form media and fuller performances. Guitar-led duets coexist with band arrangements and electronic production across the repertoire.

items.name: Xitsonga Pop
items.lineage: Popular music in Xitsonga connects Tsonga-language expression with contemporary song, recording and performance communities. Artists such as Hlamalani Maluleke draw on regional identity while working across acoustic and produced pop settings.
items.description: Sung melodies and recurring refrains interact with chordal guitar or keyboard accompaniment and rhythmic production. Intimate solo songs and fuller dance-oriented arrangements form different parts of the repertoire.

items.name: Kids dance party
items.lineage: Kids’ dance-party music gathers familiar songs and dance routines for shared movement and celebration. Repertoire such as the Hokey Pokey, Chicken Dance and Limbo Rock circulates through family events, recordings and participatory performances.
items.description: Clear beats, repeated phrases and recognizable hooks help dancers follow actions and rejoin the music. Singing, spoken cues and bright chordal accompaniment can support simple repeated movements and group responses.

items.description: Rhythmic vocal lines and repeated hooks interact with programmed drums, bass and sampled phrases. Electronic remixes and live vocal performance draw on the broader funk palette while changing the lyrical and social setting.

items.name: Gospel Amapiano
items.lineage: Gospel amapiano connects South African amapiano production with Christian singing and worship-centered events. Producers and DJs draw on township dance music while foregrounding praise, testimony and communal participation.
items.description: Deep log-drum bass, keyboard chords and programmed percussion support repeated vocal phrases. Gradual changes in layers and rhythmic emphasis create a spacious groove, with gospel expression shaping the repertoire’s devotional purpose.

items.name: Kikuyu Gospel
items.lineage: Kikuyu gospel centers Christian song in Gikuyu-speaking communities and their recording and performance networks. It forms part of Kenya’s wider gospel culture while maintaining a distinct language and community focus.
items.description: Lead and group voices carry praise, testimony and repeated refrains. Guitar, keyboards, bass and percussion can support communal responses and dance-oriented grooves, alongside more intimate devotional settings.

items.name: Música eletrônica gospel
items.lineage: Brazilian gospel electronic music connects Portuguese-language Christian repertoire with electronic production, remix culture and devotional events. DJs and producers such as Noble DJ Remix build networks around gospel songs and dance-oriented ministry.
items.description: Sung phrases and repeated hooks interact with synthesizers, programmed drums and electronic bass. Layering, rhythmic variation and changes in texture support both celebratory dance settings and more reflective passages.

items.name: Norwegian Gospel
items.lineage: Norwegian gospel develops through choirs, church communities and composers drawing on American gospel, hymns and local traditions. Oslo Gospel Choir and Tore W. Aas are prominent examples of this national choral practice.
items.description: Group harmony, lead phrases and communal refrains interact with keyboard accompaniment and rhythm sections. Full choir textures can alternate with individual voices, while arrangements range from intimate piano settings to larger bands.

items.name: Pacific Islands Gospel
items.lineage: Pacific Islands gospel connects Christian hymn and devotional traditions across diverse island communities. Local languages, communal singing and inherited musical practices shape its many regional forms.
items.description: Group harmony, repeated responses and clear melodic phrases support shared worship. Unaccompanied voices remain important, alongside instrumental settings and distinctive local approaches to praise and church music.

items.name: Swahili Gospel
items.lineage: Swahili gospel organizes Christian song through a language shared across several East African national communities. Choirs and solo performers carry worship, testimony and praise through recordings, churches and public events.
items.description: Lead phrases, group harmonies and repeated refrains support participation. Unaccompanied choir textures coexist with keyboard and rhythm-section arrangements, allowing devotional expression to range from restrained to strongly rhythmic.

items.name: Zambian Gospel
items.lineage: Zambian gospel develops through church, choir and popular-recording communities in Zambia and its diaspora. Groups such as Fountain Gates Acappella represent a strong unaccompanied vocal branch alongside other contemporary gospel settings.
items.description: Layered vocal parts and shared refrains create harmonic depth around devotional texts. Contrasts between lead voices and ensemble responses support worship and testimony, with accompaniment varying across projects.

items.name: Turkish reggae
items.lineage: Turkish reggae adapts reggae’s bass-centered grooves within local songwriting and band culture. Groups such as Sattas connect Jamaican-derived practices with Turkish expression and influences from Anatolian music.
items.description: Guitar and keyboard accents leave space around the bass and drum groove. Voices, saxophones and trumpet can add melodic lines and coordinated responses, while repetition and rhythmic placement sustain the music’s forward motion.

items.name: 528 Hz
items.lineage: 528 Hz labels listening releases organized around a nominal 528-hertz tone. The category appears in meditation and frequency-themed sound publishing, spanning pure tones and more layered musical settings.
items.description: A sustained sine tone offers one direct realization, emphasizing continuity, pitch and a largely beat-free texture. Other productions place the frequency within broader soundscapes.

items.name: Bells
items.lineage: Bell music encompasses ringing, chiming and pitched bell repertoire, from tower practices to manually played carillons. Performers such as Arie Abbenes connect composed concert works and arrangements with the resonant sound of large bell instruments.
items.description: Struck metal tones overlap through long decays, creating melodic lines, chords or repeating patterns. Differences in bell size, register and playing action shape the contrast between individual attacks and the surrounding resonance.

items.description: Clear vocal melodies and repeated refrains support shared participation. Guitar and keyboard accompaniment, bass and drums provide flexible band settings, while quieter acoustic and instrumental versions allow more reflective use.

items.description: Fiddle melodies, ornamented dance tunes and song repertoire meet guitar and piano accompaniment. Rhythmic lift, repeating tune forms and small melodic variations support both social dancing and concert arrangements; modern ensembles also explore chamber textures.

items.name: Canadian children’s music
items.lineage: Canadian children’s music grows through family concerts, recordings and educational song traditions. Artists such as Raffi connect everyday experiences, imaginative stories and care for children with memorable, participatory music.
items.description: Clear melodies, repeated phrases and playful changes in rhythm invite listening and singing along. Voices, acoustic guitar and piano support accessible harmonies, while larger arrangements and spoken storytelling vary across performers and settings.

items.name: Caracas indie
items.lineage: Caracas indie connects independent bands, recordings and venues in Venezuela’s capital. Groups such as Los Paranoias draw on alternative rock and pop while participating in a wider Venezuelan independent network.
items.description: Voices and guitar-led arrangements combine melodic hooks with bass and drums. Keyboards, acoustic instruments and contrasting production textures broaden the palette across bands, from direct rock performances to more layered pop.

items.name: Cartoon
items.lineage: Cartoon music accompanies animated characters and stories across television, film and related adaptations. Familiar themes circulate beyond their original programmes through recordings, concerts and family music-making.
items.description: Catchy sung hooks and instrumental motifs establish character and mood. Piano, electronic sounds and rhythmic accompaniment support playful theme songs, while orchestral writing and other ensembles serve the wider range of animated storytelling.

items.name: Chinese manyao
items.lineage: Chinese manyao connects Chinese-language popular songs with dance remixes and continuous DJ programmes. Familiar vocal repertoire is recast through electronic rhythm, repeated hooks and contrasting sections.
items.description: Sampled phrases, synthetic layers and prominent rhythmic patterns reshape songs for dancing. Breakbeat and other club arrangements coexist, with transitions and recurring melodic material linking tracks across a set.

items.name: Chinese Wind
items.lineage: Chinese Wind gathers Chinese wind-instrument repertoire across concert, traditional and recorded performance. Dizi, xiao, hulusi, suona and guanzi contribute distinctive approaches to breath, articulation and melodic expression.
items.description: Sustained phrases, ornaments and contrasting attacks bring out the character of bamboo flutes and reed instruments. Solo lines can be accompanied by plucked strings, as in dizi and guzheng settings, or placed within larger ensembles.

items.name: Christian afrobeat
items.lineage: Christian Afrobeat brings contemporary Afrobeats songwriting and production into gospel communities. Artists such as Annatoria connect faith-centered lyrics with the melodic and rhythmic vocabulary of African popular music.
items.description: Sung hooks and devotional refrains move over syncopated percussion, bass and chordal accompaniment. Acoustic performances sit alongside produced dance arrangements, combining clear melodies with buoyant rhythmic interplay.

items.name: Circuit
items.lineage: Circuit music develops through international LGBTQ dance-party networks, Pride events and touring DJs. Its house foundation connects progressive development, prominent percussion and shared vocal moments within large communal dance settings.
items.description: Steady club pulses, layered percussion and synthesized figures support long builds and transitions. Repeated vocal phrases and changes in density help sustain energy across extended programmes.

items.name: Classic afrobeat
items.lineage: Classic Afrobeat gathers the vintage African funk, highlife, rock and Afrobeat networks associated with pioneers such as Ebo Taylor, alongside later continuations of their sound. Its repertoire extends beyond a single national scene or fixed release-date boundary.
items.description: Repeated bass figures and interlocking drums, guitar and percussion support voices, keyboards and horn lines. Layered groove, melodic responses and contrasting instrumental passages connect dance-oriented song with extended ensemble development.

items.name: Classic anime
items.lineage: Classic anime connects established animation themes with related Japanese television hero-song traditions. Singers such as Hiroko Moriguchi, Isao Sasaki and Mitsuko Horie helped carry memorable screen songs into concerts and later reinterpretations.
items.description: Strong vocal melodies and recognizable refrains meet pop and rock accompaniment, keyboards and varied instrumental arrangements. Dramatic introductions, repeated hooks and contrasting sections reinforce the character and emotional identity of a programme.

items.name: Classic hardstyle
items.lineage: Classic hardstyle is a repertoire and revival branch within hardstyle, sustained through label catalogues, dedicated events and DJ programmes. Artists such as Scope DJ revisit influential releases alongside continuing interpretations of the style.

items.description: Expressive singing and melodic accompaniment move between intimate keyboard-led songs and fuller rhythmic productions. Warm harmonies, clear refrains and flexible vocal phrasing support both reflective and dance-oriented material.

items.name: Brazilian CCM
items.lineage: Brazilian contemporary Christian music includes a substantial Catholic recording and performance community. Artists, ministries and devotional media connect newly composed songs with communal worship and personal reflection.
items.description: Melodic singing and clear refrains often meet acoustic guitar or keyboard accompaniment, with fuller bands in other settings. Intimate delivery, shared responses and accessible harmonies support contemporary devotional expression.

items.name: Britcore
items.lineage: Britcore emerged as a hard-edged branch of British hip-hop, associated with groups such as Hijack, Hardnoise and the Demon Boyz. Rapid rap, forceful breakbeats and turntable technique connect its sound with the UK’s wider sound-system and breakbeat cultures.
items.description: Urgent rhythmic speech meets chopped drum breaks, layered samples and scratch accents. Dense rhythmic attacks and quick verbal exchanges create momentum without requiring a fixed number of rappers or a single production setup.

items.name: Drikkelek
items.lineage: Drikkelek songs belong to contemporary Nordic participatory party-game repertoire. They circulate through local celebrations, recordings and social gatherings, overlapping student-party music while serving a distinct game-oriented function.
items.description: Spoken instructions alternate with memorable sung refrains over repeated electronic accompaniment. Clear verbal cues, communal responses and recurring rhythmic sections organize participation.

items.name: Dunedin indie
items.lineage: Dunedin indie connects the New Zealand city’s independent musicians, labels and venues across generations. The Flying Nun-era Dunedin Sound remains an important inheritance alongside newer guitar, electronic and experimental communities.
items.description: Distinctive vocal melodies and guitar interplay meet bass, drums and varied keyboard textures. Lo-fi intimacy, sharp rhythmic contrasts and exploratory arrangements coexist rather than defining one fixed local sound.

items.name: Dutch moombahton
items.lineage: Dutch moombahton develops within Netherlands club and producer networks that connect Dutch house, reggaeton, bubbling and related dance styles. Producers and MCs bring this local repertoire into international festival and online circulation.
items.description: Syncopated electronic drums, rounded bass and repeated synth or sample hooks support a slower, bouncing dance pulse. Vocal fragments, MC calls and transitions between contrasting rhythmic sections give arrangements their momentum.

items.name: Dweilorkest
items.lineage: Dweilorkesten are Dutch festive wind-and-percussion bands heard at carnival, sporting events and other public celebrations. Local associations sustain a participatory performance tradition with flexible instrumentation and familiar popular repertoire.
items.description: Trumpets, saxophones and trombones exchange punchy melodic phrases over a low brass foundation and percussion. Clear rhythmic accents, communal energy and compact arrangements project into lively public spaces.

items.name: Early avant garde
items.lineage: Early avant-garde music challenged inherited assumptions about composition, sound and performance during the early twentieth century. Chance procedures, Dada experiments, unconventional instruments and new approaches to pitch and form opened paths for later experimental music.
items.description: Independent vocal lines, unusual sound sources and unexpected combinations of gesture and silence can replace familiar harmonic development. Some works organize sound through instructions or chance, while others explore instrumental color and discontinuous musical structures.

items.name: Eastern Bloc groove
items.lineage: Eastern Bloc groove draws together jazz, funk, soul, disco and beat recordings from the former socialist countries of Eastern Europe. Collectors, reissue labels and contemporary musicians connect these varied national recording histories through their rhythmic and instrumental affinities.
items.description: Syncopated bass and drums support electric keyboards and melodic wind lines, with ensemble interplay ranging from concise dance arrangements to exploratory jazz passages. Warm electric textures and repeated grooves connect diverse local repertoires.

items.name: Edo old school
items.lineage: Edo old school centers the recorded popular-music heritage of Benin City and surrounding Edo communities in Nigeria. Highlife, funk and local musical materials met in the work of artists such as Victor Uwaifo, Osayomore Joseph and Akaba Man.
items.description: Repeated bass figures, rhythmic guitar and driving percussion support expressive voices and bright melodic lines. Synthesizers, organs, flute and horns add contrasting colors to arrangements that range from lean grooves to psychedelic textures.

items.name: Egyptian alternative
items.lineage: Egyptian alternative connects independent musicians and experimental communities working across contemporary Egyptian song, rock and electronics. Cairo’s exploratory networks bring inherited melodic materials into dialogue with new production and ensemble practices.
items.description: Voices, guitars, synthesizers and acoustic rhythm sections can combine layered textures, irregular contrasts and improvisatory interplay. Instrument choices and approaches vary widely, from intimate songs to dense electronic and acoustic ensembles.

items.name: Egyptian traditional
items.lineage: Egyptian traditional music encompasses urban art-song, regional folk, devotional and instrumental traditions. Cairo’s takht heritage is one influential strand within a wider landscape that also includes Upper Egyptian, Nubian and Coptic repertoires.
items.description: Ornamented voices and melodic instruments explore modal phrases over recurring rhythmic cycles. Oud and qanun provide plucked detail while hand percussion marks and varies the rhythmic frame; flutes, bowed strings and other ensembles expand the palette in different traditions.

items.name: Eletrônica underground brasileira
items.lineage: Brazilian underground electronic music develops through independent clubs, labels, producers and resident-DJ networks. House, techno, disco and experimental approaches intersect in a community distinct from, but connected to, the larger commercial dance economy.
items.description: Repeated electronic drums and bass patterns support synthesizer movement, sampled textures and gradual transitions. Individual producers vary the balance of rhythmic weight, melodic detail and abstraction across dance-floor and listening contexts.

items.name: EPA dunk
items.lineage: EPA-dunk is associated with Swedish A-tractor youth culture and communal party listening. Producers and singers connect accessible popular-song hooks with bass-heavy electronic arrangements and a repertoire that also circulates beyond the vehicle scene.
items.description: Prominent vocals, repeated refrains and firmly marked electronic beats create an immediate participatory sound. Synthesizer figures and low-end weight reinforce the songs’ rhythmic drive and memorable melodic phrases.

items.name: Epic Collage
items.lineage: Epic collage names a network of experimental electronic music that emerged around surreal combinations of pop fragments, dramatic effects and cinematic textures. Artists connect club-derived materials with abstract narratives and unexpected sonic juxtapositions.
items.description: Abrupt edits, layered samples and contrasting atmospheres form discontinuous musical scenes. Familiar vocal or instrumental fragments may be stretched, interrupted or placed against unrelated sounds, with rhythm serving both dance movement and narrative disruption.

items.name: Epunk
items.lineage: Epunk connects contemporary internet-based punk communities, independent releases and DIY performance. Participants draw on garage punk, power pop and related guitar music while developing local and online networks around shared recordings.
items.description: Direct singing, distorted guitar, bass and drums support concise riffs and forceful song structures. Rough textures and immediate delivery coexist with melodic hooks; electronic production varies rather than defining the category’s name.

items.name: Er ge (Chinese children’s repertoire)
items.lineage: Er ge encompasses Chinese-language children’s songs and associated childhood listening repertoire. Familiar melodies circulate through family, educational and recorded settings, alongside instrumental adaptations and spoken stories.
items.description: Clear sung phrases, recurring rhythms and accessible accompaniment support recognition, memory and participation. Keyboard-led versions offer one common setting, while ensemble, instrumental and narrated formats broaden the listening field.

items.name: Erotica
items.lineage: Erotica is an adult-themed listening field spanning literary readings, songs and atmospheric instrumental material. Publishers and performers connect intimate narrative with a wider repertoire organized around mood and subject rather than a single musical lineage.
items.description: Spoken delivery emphasizes pacing, character and verbal detail in its literary branch. Other recordings use sung melody or instrumental atmosphere, with texture and performance shaped by the work’s intended listening context.

items.name: Escape Room
items.lineage: Escape room is a named discovery community connecting experimental pop, hip-hop and R&B. Its artists blur established genre expectations through independent production, socially engaged expression and unconventional approaches to popular-song material.
items.description: Voices move between direct hooks and rhythmically detailed phrasing over electronic beats, samples and changing synth textures. Arrangement contrasts and distinctive production gestures carry personality without requiring a single shared sound-design technique.

items.name: Ethiopian Traditional
items.lineage: Ethiopian traditional music encompasses inherited repertoires across the country’s diverse communities. Family transmission, poetic performance, regional celebrations and devotional institutions sustain distinct musical languages rather than one national style.
items.description: In lyric-centered traditions, expressive singing and plucked lyre accompaniment carry love poetry, social observation and proverbs. Repeated figures and flexible vocal phrasing coexist with other regional instrumental and choral practices.

items.name: Ethnomusicology
items.lineage: Ethnomusicology connects the study of music in cultural context with documentary recordings, archives and sustained research relationships. Curated listening collections bring distinct local traditions to wider audiences while retaining their separate histories and practices.
items.description: Musical form, voice, rhythm and instrumental color vary across the field’s many communities. Solo instrumental traditions offer one path into attentive listening, alongside ensemble, vocal, ritual and everyday music documented in other settings.

items.name: Euphoric Hardstyle
items.lineage: Euphoric hardstyle is the melodic and emotionally expansive branch of hardstyle, sustained by producers, labels and festival communities. It overlaps rawer approaches while placing particular emphasis on memorable leads, harmonic lift and dramatic releases of tension.
items.description: Heavy electronic kicks and a steady dance pulse support layered synthesizer melodies and broad chordal textures. Breakdowns, rising transitions and returning hooks create contrasts between spacious anticipation and forceful rhythmic impact.

items.name: Eventyr
items.lineage: Eventyr connects Scandinavian fairy-tale traditions with literary collections, oral storytelling and recorded narration. Familiar plots and characters circulate across languages and generations rather than belonging to a single narrator or modern edition.
items.description: Spoken pacing, changes of character and expressive pauses shape imagined scenes. A clear narrative voice can carry the entire tale, with phrasing and emphasis guiding attention through recurring motifs and dramatic turns.

items.name: Experimental Club
items.lineage: Experimental club music brings exploratory sound and rhythm design into dance-floor culture. Independent producers and labels connect unusual timbres and structures with club programming, sometimes preserving steady mixing and sometimes interrupting it.
items.description: Synthetic tones, manipulated samples and shifting rhythmic layers create contrasting textures. Repetition can establish a pulse while edits, changing densities and unexpected transitions reshape the listener’s sense of movement.

items.name: Experimental Indie
items.lineage: Experimental indie connects independent songwriting and guitar-band communities with exploratory arrangement and production. Musicians combine acoustic and electronic resources without requiring a single historical style or technical method.
items.description: Voices, guitars, bass and drums interact with keyboard colors and changing textures. Familiar song material can open into unusual timbres, rhythmic contrasts and flexible ensemble structures.

items.name: Experimental Psych
items.lineage: Experimental psych extends psychedelic rock through exploratory textures, extended performance and unconventional forms. Heavy riffs, improvisatory interaction and altered instrumental colors connect older psychedelic practices with contemporary independent scenes.
items.description: Fuzzed guitar, bass and drums support voices and evolving rhythmic passages. Repeated figures may expand through shifting dynamics, noise and textural changes, moving between concentrated song gestures and open-ended exploration.

items.name: Fantasy
items.lineage: Fantasy music evokes imagined worlds, journeys and characters through instrumental or vocal composition. Standalone concept pieces coexist with music for games, film and other narrative media, crossing acoustic, orchestral and electronic approaches.
items.description: Contrasting themes, changes of register and shifts in harmony suggest places, movement and dramatic events. Piano-led compositions provide one intimate setting, while larger ensembles and electronic textures can create broader imagined spaces.

items.name: Focus Beats
items.lineage: Focus beats connects instrumental beat-making with listening for work, study and everyday concentration. Radio curators and independent producers draw on beat tapes, instrumental hip-hop and related electronic music, creating a functional listening field that crosses individual production styles.
items.description: Repeated rhythmic figures and understated melodic layers maintain continuity while small changes in texture keep the music moving. Sampled fragments and electronic tones can sit within an instrumental arrangement, with occasional vocal fragments rather than a required lead singer.

items.name: Folclore Navarra
items.lineage: Navarre folk music brings together regional song, dance and instrumental traditions in Basque and Spanish. Contemporary groups such as Mielotxin connect locally transmitted repertoire with new compositions and arrangements, maintaining a dialogue between rural traditions and present-day concert life.
items.description: Voices, accordion and traditional flutes combine with rhythmic accompaniment in flexible ensembles. Dance accents, recurring melodic patterns and clear song phrases shape the music, while acoustic strings and percussion support changing textures.

items.name: Future Bounce
items.lineage: Future bounce developed within future-house production and festival culture, with Mike Williams, Brooks and Mesto among its prominent practitioners. It shares house rhythm and electronic production with the wider field while emphasizing buoyant melodic figures and sharply shaped releases of energy.
items.description: Electronic drums and bass support bright, repeating synthesizer figures. Contrasting breakdowns, rising transitions and rhythmically articulated hooks give the music its springy dance-floor character.

items.name: German Hyperpop
items.lineage: German-language hyperpop connects internet-led pop culture with rave, rap and emotionally direct songwriting. Artists including Baby B3ns, Domiziana and Abor & Tynna move between electronic pop, club energy and influences from emo and guitar music. The field extends beyond national borders through its language and online communities.
items.description: Prominent voices, synthetic hooks and electronic drums form a vivid pop texture. Pitch processing, exaggerated timbres and abrupt contrasts can heighten intimacy or intensity, while song melodies remain central through changing production styles.

items.name: Guidance
items.lineage: Guidance recordings connect practical instruction, personal advice and self-help writing with spoken listening. Audiobooks and instructional programmes cover subjects ranging from language and creative skills to everyday decisions and personal development.
items.description: A clear speaking voice organizes explanations, examples and suggestions. Pacing, emphasis and pauses help listeners follow ideas, with the narration able to carry the programme without musical accompaniment.

items.name: Guitarra Argentina
items.lineage: Argentine guitar repertoire brings together concert composition, tango, milonga and folk-derived instrumental practice. Soloists, duos and larger ensembles connect regional dance rhythms with the guitar’s melodic and harmonic resources. Eduardo Falú and Héctor Ayala are among the composers represented in its concert repertoire.
items.description: Fingerpicked nylon strings combine melody, bass and inner voices within a compact texture. Rhythmic accents and changes in register shape dances, lyrical passages and extended compositions, with articulation balancing clear individual notes and resonant chords.

items.name: Gym hardstyle
items.lineage: Gym hardstyle connects hard-dance production with online fitness and Zyzz-associated listening communities. Producers and curators such as Tevvez and Ru-Style draw on melodic hardstyle and harder dance crossovers, bringing festival energy into workout-oriented music circulation.
items.description: Forceful electronic kicks and repeating synthesizer hooks establish a driving pulse. Expansive melodic passages and escalating transitions contrast with dense rhythmic returns, emphasizing intensity without requiring a particular workout or physiological effect.

items.name: Hakkapop
items.lineage: Hakkapop brings Hakka-language songwriting and cultural expression into contemporary popular music. Artists such as Lo Sirong draw on literary texts and mountain-song traditions while engaging with folk, blues and other international influences. The scene overlaps Taiwanese popular music without requiring a single style or ethnic background from every performer.
items.description: Expressive lead singing carries the words over acoustic or amplified accompaniment. Guitar-led arrangements may include mandolin, banjo and harmonica, allowing lyrical phrases and rhythmic instrumental responses to meet in an intimate texture.

items.name: Halloween
items.lineage: Halloween music gathers seasonal songs, theatrical effects and concert repertoire around playful fright and supernatural imagery. Community celebrations and curated listening bring novelty recordings, organ classics, soundtrack material and other styles into a shared seasonal setting.
items.description: Dark contrasts, dramatic pauses and memorable gestures help create suspense or comic surprise. Resonant pipe organ offers one instrumental setting, while voices, bands and electronic effects appear elsewhere in the repertoire.

items.name: Hammond organ
items.lineage: Hammond organ music spans jazz, gospel, rock and experimental performance. Tonewheel sound, drawbar registration and rotating-speaker color connect solo exploration with ensembles, from organ trios to amplified bands and sustained drone-based work.
items.description: Keyboard figures move between melodic lines, chords and repeating patterns, with bass and upper registers available to a single player. Changing registration and rotary movement reshape the tone, supporting both clear rhythmic attack and sustained textures.

items.name: Handpan
items.lineage: Handpan music centers on hand-played tuned steel shells, developing from the Hang and related contemporary instruments. Solo improvisation, composition and ensemble collaboration circulate through maker communities, recordings and live performance.
items.description: Resonant pitched strikes combine melody and rhythm across a small set of tuned fields. Alternating hands, repeated figures and contrasting touches let ringing tones overlap while quieter taps maintain motion.

items.name: Hardgroove
items.lineage: Hardgroove developed within techno through funk-driven rhythm, percussion and layered loop production, with Ben Sims central to its named scene and label. Its connections to DJ culture emphasize movement and interaction between rhythmic layers rather than a single fixed tempo or sample source.
items.description: Interlocking percussion and repeated sampled figures ride a firm electronic pulse. Gradual changes in density, accent and loop combination keep the groove active, combining mechanical precision with syncopated rhythmic movement.

items.description: Voices lead melodic songs over guitar, bass, keyboards and drums in contemporary band settings. Clear hooks and rhythmic accompaniment support the text, while other branches use different local instrumental combinations.

items.name: Lampung Indie
items.lineage: Lampung indie connects local bands, organizers and creative communities within Indonesia’s independent music scene. Pop, folk and rock approaches circulate through regional performances and independently issued recordings.
items.description: Singing and guitar can sit over bass and drums in a light, melodic band texture. Acoustic colors and contrasting instrumental responses support direct songs without prescribing one arrangement for the whole scene.

items.name: Latin Christian
items.lineage: Latin Christian music links Spanish-language Christian artists, churches and ministries across national borders. Worship, gospel, pop, rock and rap coexist within a broad devotional and recording network.
items.description: Voices carry prayers, testimony and praise through familiar song forms. Piano-supported singing provides a reflective setting, while bands, choirs and electronic production give other parts of the repertoire more rhythmic or expansive textures.

items.name: Louisville Underground
items.lineage: Louisville underground developed through connected punk, hardcore and experimental-rock communities, with shared musicians, labels, venues and independent publications. Groups such as Slint, Rodan and Shipping News helped sustain a network that crosses stylistic boundaries.
items.description: Interlocking guitars, bass and drums support vocals through riffs, abrupt contrasts and changing densities. Repetition and tension can matter as much as conventional hooks, with instrumental passages opening space for ensemble interaction.

items.name: Maithili
items.lineage: Maithili music draws on the language and literary traditions of Mithila, spanning devotional poetry, folk song and contemporary repertoire. Vidyapati’s Krishna poetry has also circulated through neighboring devotional singing traditions.
items.description: An expressive voice can carry poetic texts over khol accompaniment in a devotional setting. Melodic phrasing and responsive drum patterns support the words, while other parts of the repertoire use different ensembles and secular themes.

items.name: Malayalam worship
items.lineage: Malayalam worship connects Christian devotional songs with Malayalam-speaking congregations and music ministries. Church repertoire, devotional film songs and contemporary compositions circulate through choral, a cappella and accompanied arrangements.
items.description: Lead singing and supporting voices can weave melody with harmonic and rhythmic accompaniment. Clear text and shared phrases support devotional expression, whether performed by an unaccompanied vocal group or a larger ensemble.

items.name: Meme music
items.lineage: Meme music forms a changing repertoire through online quotation, remixing and humorous recontextualization. Older pop songs, game and film themes, novelty recordings and instrumental tunes can acquire new meanings through repeated reuse.
items.description: Recognizable hooks and abrupt associations help listeners identify a reference. Piano arrangements expose familiar melodies and harmony, while other versions use voices, electronic sounds, edits or intentionally exaggerated performance.

items.name: Middle-earth music
items.lineage: Middle-earth music gathers songs, screen scores and concert works associated with Tolkien’s imagined world. Film adaptations and independent interpretations connect vocal songwriting with large-scale instrumental and symphonic traditions.
items.description: Memorable themes, expansive phrases and contrasting textures evoke places and characters. Voice with piano can present a song intimately, while orchestral, choral and other instrumental settings offer different scales of storytelling.

items.name: Mluvené slovo
items.lineage: Mluvené slovo is the Czech spoken-word publishing field, encompassing literary narration and other recorded voice forms. It includes adult fiction as well as children’s stories, dramatic readings and related spoken repertoire.
items.description: A clear speaking voice shapes narrative through pacing, emphasis and changes of character. Unaccompanied reading focuses attention on language, while other productions may involve multiple voices or supporting sound.

items.name: Mongolian alternative
items.lineage: Mongolian alternative connects contemporary independent and alternative musicians, including Ulaanbaatar’s guitar-oriented scene. Bands and songwriters combine local community ties with varied rock and pop approaches.
items.description: Vocals, guitars, bass and drums create direct songs with melodic hooks and contrasting dynamics. Raw amplified textures can sit beside more intimate passages, without requiring traditional overtone singing or one common instrumental style.

items.name: Chill-Out Trance
items.lineage: Chill-out trance connects trance repertoire with relaxed listening, including reinterpretations of vocal-trance songs. Remixers and labels such as Seven24’s network, RNM and Suanda link melodic dance music with atmospheric listening arrangements.
items.description: Sustained synth harmony and restrained electronic rhythm leave space around melodic material. Layers develop gradually, with softened attacks and spacious production offering an alternative to the pressure of a dance-floor arrangement.

items.name: Indonesian indigenous traditional
items.lineage: Indonesian indigenous traditions encompass many distinct local musical cultures, including communal vocal poetry, instrumental ensembles and dance repertoires. Language, social occasions and inherited performance practices connect music with particular communities.
items.description: A solo voice and responding chorus can shape extended poetic verses, as in Kenyah communal singing. Layered voices and parallel melodic movement offer one texture within a much wider range of regional practices.

items.name: Japanese beats
items.lineage: Japanese beats connects beatmakers, DJs and independent labels through sample-based production and record culture. Networks such as Jazzy Sport bring hip-hop into contact with jazz, soul, house and experimental electronic approaches.
items.description: Layered samples, shaped drum patterns and recurring melodic fragments create compact rhythmic pieces. Texture, timing and variation give instrumental beats their character, while other releases add rap, singing or longer mixed programmes.

items.name: Japanese traditional
items.lineage: Japanese traditional music gathers distinct historical lineages, including court music, theater, vocal repertoire and instrumental schools. Transmission through teachers and communities preserves contrasting instruments, techniques and aesthetic approaches.
items.description: Shakuhachi offers a breath-shaped solo branch, with flexible pitch shading, sustained tones and pauses. Koto, voices and larger ensembles produce other textures across the broader traditional repertoire.

items.name: Japanese VTuber
items.lineage: Japanese VTuber music grows from avatar-mediated streaming performers and their production communities. Virtual idols and independent talents sing original songs and covers, collaborating with songwriters and producers across popular styles.
items.description: Expressive singing, memorable hooks and vivid electronic accompaniment support performances that link music with an on-screen character. Synthesizers and programmed rhythm offer one common pop texture, alongside acoustic and band arrangements.

items.name: Kazakh indie
items.lineage: Kazakh indie connects independent songwriters and bands within Kazakhstan’s contemporary music scene. Kazakh-language songs circulate through intimate performances, recorded releases and collaborations that cross folk, rock and electronic approaches.
items.description: Voice and guitar can place words and melody in the foreground. Restrained accompaniment and shifting dynamics support personal expression, while other arrangements expand into fuller band or electronic textures.

items.name: Lagu Madura
items.lineage: Lagu Madura encompasses Madurese-language song, including community play-songs and later popular or concert interpretations. Regional language and repertoire link varied arrangements without requiring a single ensemble.
items.description: Shared melodies and memorable text support individual or communal singing. Choral settings can distribute phrases across several parts, using imitation, layered harmony and vocal slides to develop familiar material.

items.name: Lagu Timur
items.lineage: Lagu Timur connects contemporary song repertoires across Eastern Indonesia, including Nusa Tenggara, Papua and Maluku. Musicians draw on regional identity and local musical resources while participating in wider Indonesian popular music.
items.description: Singing can blend acoustic guitar and keyboards with programmed sound, percussion and strings. Melodic hooks and layered accompaniment connect contemporary song structures with varied regional colors.

items.name: Latincore
items.lineage: Latincore connects Latin American punk, hardcore and melodic-core communities through touring, independent releases and shared audiences. Argentine, Chilean, Mexican and other scenes overlap within a transnational network of guitar-driven music.
items.description: Emphatic singing and group responses ride over distorted guitars, bass and drums. Driving riffs and melodic passages create contrast, with rhythmic intensity supporting both direct hooks and longer developments.

items.name: Latintronica
items.lineage: Latintronica connects Latin American roots repertoires with electronic production across national borders. Cumbia reworking, Andean materials, folk reinterpretation and ambient approaches circulate through overlapping producer and festival networks.
items.description: Layered samples and electronic rhythms reshape acoustic colors and familiar melodic fragments. Repetition, texture and gradual changes can support dancing or more atmospheric listening, without requiring every piece to follow one regional rhythm.

items.name: Liechtenstein
items.lineage: Liechtenstein’s musical life includes historical composition, contemporary popular groups and national ensembles. Institutions and repertoire traditions connect these contrasting practices, with Josef Gabriel Rheinberger an important figure in its composed-music heritage.
items.description: Romantic organ music offers one branch, combining sustained harmony, contrapuntal lines and broad changes in registration. Other parts of the national repertoire use voices, bands or chamber ensembles and follow different musical forms.
exemplars: Josef Gabriel Rheinberger — complete Organ Sonata No.15, op.168; Carus50.168/00

items.name: Lustrum
items.lineage: Lustrum songs are associated with anniversaries of Dutch student organizations. Commissioned or collectively adopted songs connect association identity, celebration and wider popular-music circulation.
items.description: Lead and group singing carry memorable refrains over energetic popular accompaniment. Piano, bass-synth figures and electronic drums can form a compact foundation, with other arrangements adding brass, strings or sampled effects.

items.name: Malaysian Traditional
items.lineage: Malaysian traditional music encompasses distinct regional and community repertoires, including the oral traditions of Sarawak. Songs and instrumental practices pass between generations while also reaching contemporary stages and new arrangements.
items.description: Voice with sape offers an intimate story-bearing texture, joining melodic singing with plucked resonance. Other Malaysian traditions use different ensembles, languages and ceremonial or social settings.

items.name: Marathi Remix
items.lineage: Marathi remix connects Marathi-language songs with electronic reworking and dance-floor circulation. Producers reinterpret familiar repertoire through house, techno, trance and other club approaches, extending regional songs into new listening settings.
items.description: Repeated samples, electronic percussion and contrasting sections emphasize recognizable hooks and rhythmic movement. Layering and edits can transform a song’s texture while preserving a melodic or vocal reference.

items.name: Montana roots
items.lineage: Montana roots connects regional folk, country, bluegrass and acoustic-song communities. Songwriters and ensembles circulate through local performances and recordings, drawing on shared roots traditions while developing individual approaches.
items.description: Voice and acoustic guitar can foreground stories and melodic phrasing. Strummed harmony and flexible dynamics provide an intimate foundation, while other groups expand the texture with strings, bass and drums.
