items.name: Moroccan traditional
items.lineage: Moroccan traditional music encompasses distinct Amazigh, Arab, Gnawa, Andalusi and Moroccan Jewish repertoires. Community transmission and social or ceremonial settings sustain diverse vocal and instrumental lineages.
items.description: An unaccompanied narrative romance offers one intimate vocal branch, with melodic turns supporting the unfolding text. Other traditions use percussion, strings, wind instruments or larger ensembles with their own forms and occasions.

items.name: Motivation
items.lineage: Motivation connects spoken recordings and readings directed toward encouragement, self-development and practical reflection. Historical self-help writing, contemporary talks and personal testimony offer contrasting approaches to this purpose-based listening field.
items.description: A speaking voice uses pacing and emphasis to organize ideas and address the listener. Reflective narration can be calm and conversational, while other presentations use greater rhetorical intensity or supporting music.

items.name: Multidisciplinary
items.lineage: Multidisciplinary music connects artists whose work crosses composition, visual art, design, performance and other practices. Methods and ideas move between media, producing varied forms rather than one common instrumental style.
items.description: Piano composition can explore space, repetition and changing resonance, while other artists use voices, electronics or sculptural sound. The relationship between musical material and another creative practice shapes each work’s character.

items.name: Música blumenauense
items.lineage: Música blumenauense connects Blumenau’s musicians, venues and independent cultural organizations. Authorial music ranges from rock to MPB and acoustic pop, with regional collaboration supporting varied approaches.
items.description: Voices and guitars can combine with bass, cello and percussion in a melodic song texture. Acoustic and electric colors alternate between support and response, while other local groups develop different ensembles and styles.

items.name: Musica calabrese
items.lineage: Musica calabrese encompasses Calabrian regional repertoire, including dialect storytelling, sentimental song and dance music. Folk revivals and contemporary performers renew songs associated with local history and social life.
items.description: Voice and guitar can bring narrative and language to the foreground through flexible phrasing and direct accompaniment. Dance-oriented branches use stronger repeated rhythms, while reflective songs leave more space around the text.

items.name: Música capixaba
items.lineage: Música capixaba is the cross-style music community of Espírito Santo, connecting popular music, regional scenes and experimental practice. Universities, labels and cultural organizations provide settings for collaboration across these approaches.
items.description: An experimental ensemble can combine processed voices, guitars, bass and electronic sources with live sound manipulation. Sustained textures and changing layers create interaction between performers, while other capixaba branches favor direct song or dance forms.

items.name: Música caririense
items.lineage: Música caririense connects the musical communities of Ceará’s Cariri region, including songwriting, percussion, rock and experimental work. Local artists and independent labels bring these approaches into shared circulation.
items.description: Looped guitar improvisation offers one exploratory branch, using delay and resonance to build changing layers. A foot-played jingle pulse can accompany the guitar, while other regional groups use different acoustic and electric ensembles.

items.name: Música cearense
items.lineage: Música cearense connects Ceará’s cross-style musical community, from acoustic song and popular repertoire to forró and experimental groups. Regional artists, labels and performances link local repertoires with broader Brazilian musical currents.
items.description: Singing with steel-string guitar can present songs directly, using ringing chords and small melodic inflections. Fuller bands and other instrumental combinations expand the range of textures across the regional field.

items.name: Música chiapaneca
items.lineage: Música chiapaneca encompasses the regional repertoires and musical communities of Chiapas. Marimba ensembles, Indigenous-language songs, strings, winds and percussion contribute distinct traditions within this wider field.
items.description: A marimba-led instrumental ensemble can combine interlocking wooden-keyboard lines with bass, bright glockenspiel color and percussion. Song and dance melodies circulate through contrasting arrangements, alongside other regional vocal and instrumental practices.

items.name: Música colombiana instrumental
items.lineage: Música colombiana instrumental gathers instrumental repertoires across Colombia, including piano, string ensembles, harp-associated traditions and orchestral arrangements. Composers and performers reinterpret regional forms alongside concert music.
items.description: Piano can carry melody, harmonic movement and contrasting phrases in a compact instrumental setting. Other ensembles distribute these roles among plucked strings, winds or larger groups, reflecting varied regional and compositional traditions.

items.name: Música moçambicana
items.lineage: Música moçambicana connects Mozambique’s traditional, popular and contemporary musical communities, including artists working across borders. Marrabenta, sung repertoire, electronic collaborations and rap contribute to a broad national and diaspora field.
items.description: Voices and plucked accompaniment can interact with electronic textures in contemporary song arrangements. Shared melodic phrases and changing layers support the text, while dance bands and other regional ensembles offer different rhythmic foundations.

items.name: Música para crianças
items.lineage: Música para crianças encompasses Brazilian children’s repertoire, from lullabies and sung games to contemporary concerts and music theater. Performers and educators adapt both inherited songs and wider popular music for participation and listening.
items.description: A lead singer and responding group can exchange memorable phrases over guitar, bass and drums. Repetition, rhythmic contrast and clear melodies invite participation, while quieter or unaccompanied songs offer other settings.

items.name: Música paranaense
items.lineage: Música paranaense connects Paraná’s varied musical communities, including songwriters, bands and concert performers. Local institutions and artists sustain regional networks within broader Brazilian musical life.
items.description: Voice and acoustic guitar provide an intimate setting for lyrical songs. Melodic accompaniment and flexible phrasing place words in the foreground, while other regional performers work with larger bands or instrumental ensembles.

items.name: Musica per bambini
items.lineage: Musica per bambini connects Italian children’s musical publishing and performance, including songs, lullabies, choral repertoire and narrated musical stories. Educational and cultural institutions bring these forms to different ages and listening settings.
items.description: Spoken narration with piano can shape a story through pacing, musical responses and changes in mood. Other works use singing, repeated refrains or group participation, offering contrasting ways to connect words and music.

items.name: Música piauiense
items.lineage: Música piauiense connects Piauí’s musicians and cultural networks across rock, popular song and rhythmic Brazilian traditions. Artists combine local community ties with influences including samba-rock, funk, baião, soul and reggae.
items.description: A singing voice can lead a guitar, bass and drum ensemble through rhythmic songs. Clean guitar patterns, a firm bass foundation and varied drum articulation support melodic phrases and changes in groove.

items.name: Mùsica piemontèisa
items.lineage: Mùsica piemontèisa encompasses Piedmontese regional-language song and community repertoire, including narratives, rhymes and dance-related traditions. Publications, recordings and performers sustain these materials through revival and contemporary interpretation.
items.description: Voice with guitar can present words directly through melodic accompaniment and changing emphasis. Solo recitals coexist with choral and instrumental settings, reflecting the range of regional repertoire.

items.name: Música pitiusa
items.lineage: Música Pitiusa connects the repertoires of Ibiza and Formentera, including traditional dance music, song and later revival or popular approaches. Island communities and cultural organizations sustain distinct practices within the wider Catalan-speaking musical world.
items.description: In ball pagès, a one-handed flute and drum interact with large castanets to support dance. Repeated melodic fragments and rhythmic elaboration shape the performance, while other island repertoires use voices or different instrumental combinations.

items.name: Música puntana
items.lineage: Música puntana connects the repertoire and musical communities of San Luis, including traditions shared with the wider Cuyo region. Regional songs, poetry and contemporary concert arrangements sustain a varied provincial field.
items.description: Voices and guitars can combine with bass, piano and percussion in a melodic song ensemble. Instrumental responses and shared vocal phrases support regional texts, while other settings favor more intimate accompaniment.

items.name: Música rapa nui
items.lineage: Música Rapa Nui encompasses the island’s inherited and contemporary musical expressions. Artists connect local language and identity with folk, rock, blues and other influences, working across acoustic and amplified settings.
items.description: Lead and supporting voices can ride over electric guitars, bass, drums and percussion. Melodic hooks and rhythmic accompaniment carry contemporary songs, alongside other island practices with different textures and occasions.

items.name: Música sudcaliforniana
items.lineage: Música sudcaliforniana connects Baja California Sur’s regional repertoire, including corridos, campirano and contemporary popular music. Local narratives and community performance link acoustic groups with broader Mexican song traditions.
items.description: A singer with guitar and requinto can be supported by the rounded bass pulse of a tuba. Plucked melodic responses and clear text shape an intimate regional-song texture, with other ensembles offering different arrangements.

items.name: Música tabasqueña
items.lineage: Música tabasqueña gathers Tabasco’s regional repertoire, including the tamborilero traditions maintained through community performance and cultural transmission. Indigenous and mestizo practices meet in ceremonial, social and dance settings.
items.description: Cane flute carries melodies over contrasting small and large drums. Repeating patterns and changes of accent support danza, son and zapateo, with ensemble size and additional instruments varying between contexts.

items.name: Música tradicional cubana
items.lineage: Música tradicional cubana encompasses interrelated Cuban song and dance repertoires, including bolero, son, habanera, guajira and guaracha. Troubadours, trios, larger popular ensembles and other performers sustain contrasting approaches within this broad field.
items.description: Harmonizing voices, guitar, tres and percussion can form a compact traditional-song texture. Plucked responses and repeated rhythmic figures support melody and text, while larger groups add other instrumental colors.

items.name: Musical advocacy
items.lineage: Musical advocacy connects repertoire organized around public causes, collective action and charitable support. Multi-artist projects and community performances bring songs across pop, rock, choral and other traditions into new social contexts.
items.description: Shared singing and memorable refrains can emphasize participation and solidarity. Piano-supported voices offer a direct setting, while larger bands and ensembles expand the musical scale of a performance.

items.name: Músicas espíritas
items.lineage: Músicas espíritas connects Brazilian Spiritist artists, study groups and devotional performance. Songs circulate through concerts, recordings and religious education, engaging with reflection and Spiritist interpretations of spiritual life.
items.description: Voices and acoustic guitar can create an intimate devotional texture. Melodic phrases and responsive accompaniment support the words, with duets, solo singing and fuller arrangements providing different settings.

items.name: Musiqi-ye Zanān
items.lineage: Musiqi-ye zanān gathers Iranian and Persian women’s voices across traditional, popular and contemporary music. Singers connect poetic repertoire, personal expression and varied performance communities without sharing one required style or political position.
items.description: An unaccompanied voice can bring the contour and language of a poem into focus. Other settings add acoustic or electronic accompaniment, while vocal phrasing remains central across contrasting approaches.

items.name: Musique alsacienne
items.lineage: Musique alsacienne connects Alsace’s regional dances, dialect songs and ensemble traditions. Musicians and arrangers transmit repertoire shaped by French and German musical exchange, including polkas, marches and Rhinländer.
items.description: Accordion can carry dance melodies and harmonic support through articulated bellows phrases. Solo and duo arrangements coexist with wind ensembles and sung repertoire, creating different textures around familiar regional forms.

items.name: Musique centrafricaine
items.lineage: Musique centrafricaine encompasses the Central African Republic’s varied communities and contemporary musical life. Aka, Banda, Gbaya, Ngbaka and other repertoires coexist with urban song and popular music.
items.description: A solo vocal line offers one intimate branch, with melodic elaboration shaped by inherited patterns and phrasing. Other practices use interlocking voices, instruments or rhythmic ensembles, reflecting different social settings and traditions.

items.name: Musique mahoraise
items.lineage: Musique mahoraise connects Mayotte’s music and Shimaoré-language song with its wider Comorian and diaspora relationships. Traditional repertoire and contemporary songwriting meet influences such as reggae and other popular styles.
items.description: Lead and supporting voices can combine with guitar, bass, keyboards and hand percussion in an acoustic ensemble. Alternating melodic colors and repeated phrases support songs, while other performers use different local instrumental and vocal textures.

items.name: Musique militaire
items.lineage: Musique militaire encompasses music maintained and performed by military institutions, including signals, ceremonial ensembles, singing and public concerts. Repertoire ranges from functional calls and marches to choral works and wider popular or concert music.
items.description: A choir with piano offers one concert branch, using coordinated phrasing and changing vocal density. Wind bands, percussion and signaling instruments serve other ceremonial and public roles within the broader institutional field.

items.name: Musique tchadienne
items.lineage: Musique tchadienne connects Chad’s varied song traditions and contemporary performers. Local languages and French circulate through national touring and cultural networks, with heritage-rooted material meeting popular influences.
items.description: Voices, guitar and percussion can create a direct song texture with melodic responses and rhythmic support. Duets and small groups offer intimate settings, while other ensembles develop fuller arrangements.

items.name: Musique traditionnelle comorienne
items.lineage: Musique traditionnelle comorienne encompasses inherited practices across domestic, ceremonial, dance and devotional life in the Comorian islands. Songs and instrumental traditions take distinct forms according to community and occasion.
items.description: Voice with firimbi flute can shape an intimate domestic-song texture. Sustained flute phrases and melodic singing provide one setting, alongside larger vocal and percussion practices elsewhere in the repertoire.

items.name: Musique urbaine Kinshasa
items.lineage: Musique urbaine Kinshasa connects contemporary Congolese urban song, rap and electronic dance networks. Artists and DJs circulate between local scenes and wider African club influences, with the named field extending beyond a single city’s residents.
items.description: Layered rhythmic material and electronic percussion support melodies, vocal references and changing club textures. Repetition and edits can connect different styles within a production, while live bands and singers shape other branches of the urban repertoire.

items.name: Muzică bisericească
items.lineage: Muzica bisericească connects Romanian church-music repertoires, including psaltic chant and harmonic choral practice. Regional transmission and institutional publications sustain liturgical material across different vocal approaches.
items.description: Unaccompanied voices shape sacred text through connected phrases and melodic elaboration. Solo, group and choral textures vary by repertoire, with different relationships between sustained lines, rhythm and harmony.

items.name: Muzică creștină
items.lineage: Muzica creștină connects Romanian Christian recording, worship and outreach communities. Contemporary bands, soloists and choirs circulate devotional repertoire through churches, public events and recordings.
items.description: Singing with keyboards can carry familiar praise melodies, while saxophone and other instruments offer responses or instrumental interpretations. Repeated phrases and clear melodic lines support communal and reflective listening.

items.name: Muzica moldoveneasca
items.lineage: Muzica moldovenească connects Moldavian regional song and dance heritage with contemporary circulation. Folk collections, community performance and popular reinterpretations span a field broader than any one ensemble or national pop style.
items.description: Unaccompanied singing can bring melodic phrases and text into focus. Dance-oriented ensembles and other accompanied settings provide contrasting rhythmic and harmonic textures across the repertoire.

items.name: Muzika l’yeladim
items.lineage: Muzika l’yeladim encompasses Hebrew and Israeli children’s musical repertoire, including educational songs, festival material, lullabies and concert arrangements. Songs circulate between family, school, broadcast and performance settings.
items.description: A choir and flute can exchange clear melodic phrases in a composed arrangement. Repetition and expressive word-setting support the text, while other versions use solo singing, instrumental accompaniment or group participation.

items.name: Nederlandse hardstyle
items.lineage: Nederlandse hardstyle connects Dutch-language popular songs, carnival repertoire and communal celebration with hardstyle production. Remixers and event networks bring familiar vocal material into hard-dance contexts.
items.description: Sung hooks and group refrains meet forceful electronic kicks and sharply defined synthesizer figures. Repetition, breaks and changes in intensity connect recognizable songs with an energetic dance pulse.

items.name: Nederreggae
items.lineage: Nederreggae connects reggae performers and audiences in the Netherlands and neighboring Low Countries. Dutch-language songs and multilingual circulation link local bands with the wider reggae tradition.
items.description: Rhythmic guitar chords, bass and drums support voices and keyboards, with horns adding responses and accents. Ensemble phrasing balances repeated accompaniment with melodic and vocal movement.

items.name: NepHop
items.lineage: NepHop connects Nepali-language hip-hop communities in Nepal and the diaspora, including recorded songs, live performance and battle rap. MCs, producers and organizers sustain local networks and exchanges with wider hip-hop practice.
items.description: Rhythmic spoken delivery, wordplay and contrasting flows shape verses over beats. Unaccompanied battles and call-and-response performance provide another branch, emphasizing verbal timing and direct interaction.

items.name: Normal indie
items.lineage: Normal indie connects independent musicians associated with Normal, Illinois, including The Normals and Andrew Osenga. Local roots and collaborations link the community with wider American indie and singer-songwriter networks.
items.description: Acoustic strumming and layered human voices support melodic songs. Intimate solo passages and communal refrains offer contrasting textures within the broader regional scene.
exemplars: Andrew Osenga — complete original Letters to the Editor, Vol.1 EP2007

items.name: Norsk lovsang
items.lineage: Norsk lovsang connects Norwegian church songwriters, worship bands and congregations through local ministries and national networks. Contemporary songs circulate alongside hymn and gospel traditions across denominations.
items.description: Lead singing and congregational refrains rise over keyboards, guitar, bass and drums. Repeated melodic phrases and harmonic support encourage shared participation, with quieter devotional passages providing contrast.

items.name: North Alabama indie
items.lineage: North Alabama indie connects independent musicians around Huntsville, the Tennessee Valley and neighboring northern Alabama communities. Local radio, venues and collaborations support varied rock and song-oriented projects.
items.description: Guitars, bass and drums support voices, while piano and additional percussion can broaden the arrangement. Interlocking accompaniment and contrasting vocal textures connect intimate songwriting with amplified ensemble playing.
exemplars: Dweeby — The Dweepee (2024), complete EP credited ensemble

items.name: Northeast Indian indie
items.lineage: Northeast Indian indie connects independent artists and performance networks across India’s northeastern states. Festivals, venues and collaborations support diverse songwriting and musical identities within a shared regional field.
items.description: Voice and electric guitar can form an intimate song texture, with clear chordal accompaniment supporting melodic phrases. Other branches use larger bands and electronic production, reflecting the scene’s stylistic variety.
exemplars: LOJAL — For Now (2020), complete artist-credited single

items.name: Northern Irish indie
items.lineage: Northern Irish indie connects independent artists, venues, recordings and music institutions across Northern Ireland. Belfast is one important center within a wider regional network that overlaps Irish and British independent music.
items.description: Voices, electric guitar, bass and drums carry melodic songs, with piano adding harmonic weight and contrast. Arrangements move between intimate phrases and fuller ensemble passages across indie-pop and rock approaches.
exemplars: Gareth Dunlop — Welcome To The House Of I Don’t Know (2024), complete album personnel palette

items.name: Northwest China indie
items.lineage: Northwest China indie connects independent musicians and audiences across the region, including Xi’an’s post-punk and psychedelic networks. Local scenes and labels link contrasting regional backgrounds with wider Chinese independent music.
items.description: Guitar, bass and drums establish repeated figures beneath voices and synthesizer textures. Auxiliary percussion and shifting layers can extend the groove, while different artists draw on distinct song and experimental approaches.
exemplars: FAZI — complete Invisible Water album-version track, Folding Story2022

items.name: Norwegian experimental
items.lineage: Norwegian experimental connects artist-run composition and improvisation networks, including the SOFA label and exploratory concert practice. The field overlaps jazz, contemporary composition and other experimental traditions.
items.description: Acoustic twelve-string guitar can create dense resonance through interlocking fingerpicked patterns, repeated figures and changing emphasis. Other performers explore different acoustic and electronic materials, with close attention to timbre and form.
exemplars: Kim Myhr — All Your Limbs Singing, complete solo programme at AngelicA25 (24 May2015)

items.name: Nova música carioca
items.lineage: Nova música carioca connects contemporary songwriters and independent musical communities in Rio de Janeiro. Local venues and cultural programmes bring varied approaches to popular song into dialogue with the city’s musical history.
items.description: Voice, piano and acoustic guitar can support an intimate exchange between songs and spoken poetry. Larger bands and electronic arrangements provide other approaches within this diverse songwriter community.
exemplars: Letrux and Thiago Vivas — complete Alfabeto Sonoro intimate literary show

items.name: Nu gabber
items.lineage: Nu gabber connects a contemporary hardcore revival with techno, punk and electronic crossover communities. Artists and collectives such as Brutalismus 3000, Casual Gabberz and Gabber Modus Operandi reshape gabber’s forceful pulse through contrasting vocal and production approaches.
items.description: Hard electronic kicks and sharply defined synthesizer figures drive repeated patterns. Projected vocals and abrupt changes in texture can add punk-like urgency, while different projects explore other rhythmic and timbral combinations.
exemplars: Brutalismus3000 — complete Prague SaSaZu headlining set, documented May2023

items.name: Nueva ola chilena
items.lineage: Nueva ola chilena emerged as a Chilean youth-oriented popular-song movement shaped by rock and roll, radio, records and television. Artists such as Los Ramblers helped establish a repertoire that continues through revivals and public performance.
items.description: Lead voices ride guitar, piano, bass and drums, with saxophone and brass adding melodic responses and rhythmic accents. Clear song forms and lively ensemble phrasing connect ballads and dance-oriented numbers.
exemplars: The Ramblers — manager-documented current November2019 performing lineup

items.name: Nueva ola peruana
items.lineage: Nueva ola peruana connects Peru’s early Spanish-language popular-rock movement and its continuing repertoire. Groups such as Los Doltons and later revival performers sustain songs associated with the country’s expanding youth and recording culture.
items.description: Melodic lead singing combines with electric guitar, keyboards, bass and drums. Chordal accompaniment and a clear backbeat support contrasting verses and refrains, from gentle songs to more animated rock-and-roll treatments.
exemplars: Alfredo Correa y el show de Los Doltons — documented complete July2022 performing lineup

items.name: NZ Christian
items.lineage: NZ Christian connects Christian artists, recording networks and worship communities in New Zealand. Contemporary bands and songwriters overlap international Christian pop and rock while developing local ministry and performance relationships.
items.description: Lead and group singing combine with guitars, keyboards, bass and drums. Additional percussion can reinforce the pulse, while repeated melodic phrases and harmonic movement support praise and reflection.
exemplars: Thousandfold — complete published nine-person ensemble practice

items.name: Oceania soundtrack
items.lineage: Oceania soundtrack connects screen composers and repertoire associated with Australia, New Zealand and the wider region. Music circulates through films, broadcasts, recordings and concert arrangements, encompassing contrasting eras and production approaches.
items.description: Instrumental themes support dramatic movement through melody, harmony and changes of texture. Piano arrangements bring those themes into a compact acoustic setting, alongside orchestral and electronic approaches in the wider field.

items.lineage: Oktoberfest music connects Munich beer-tent performance and its wider circulation, from repeated toasting songs to folk, schlager and contemporary party repertoire. Live bands and communal singing sustain the festival’s participatory musical setting.

items.name: Pittsburgh indie
items.lineage: Pittsburgh indie connects a varied local independent music community, from guitar bands and songwriters to electronic and sample-based projects. Artists such as Girl Talk demonstrate the field’s reach beyond one rock-band format.
items.description: Layered samples can create rapidly changing combinations of rhythm, melody and recorded voices. Repetition, cuts and transitions shape a collage, alongside other instrumental and song-based approaches in the wider scene.

items.name: Pontianak indie
items.lineage: Pontianak indie connects independent bands, labels and physical-release communities in Pontianak, West Kalimantan. Local events and collaborations support varied pop, rock and experimental approaches within Indonesia’s broader independent field.
items.description: Voices and guitars combine with bass and drums, while synthesizers and trumpet can add contrasting color. Repeated figures, melodic hooks and changing density connect song-oriented passages with fuller amplified textures.
exemplars: Stromberry Blue — See You Darling, full six-song Dirtwave EP

items.name: Popping
items.lineage: Popping music serves the rhythmic needs of a dance practice built around sharply timed muscular hits, controlled isolations and flowing movement. Funk, electro and related recorded repertoires circulate through dancers, DJs and competitions.
items.description: A clear drum pulse and focused bass line support precisely placed accents. Synthesizer textures and repeating figures give dancers room to shape tension, release and changes in movement.
exemplars: Rita Spirit — Popping Delight (2023), complete event-directed DJ mix

items.name: Psytech
items.lineage: Psytech connects psychedelic techno producers, labels and audiences, including the Techgnosis network. It overlaps minimal techno and psychedelic dance music while developing its own patterns of circulation and sound design.
items.description: Electronic drums establish a repeated dance pulse beneath synthesizer figures and gradually shifting layers. Texture, space and recurring motifs create tension through extended development.

items.name: Puglia indie
items.lineage: Puglia indie connects independent artists and musical communities rooted in Italy’s Apulia region. Local bands and songwriters maintain these relationships even as recordings and collaborations take them elsewhere.
items.description: Voices and acoustic guitar meet bass, drums, piano and synthesizer color. Clear melodic phrases and changing accompaniment connect intimate songwriting with fuller indie-pop arrangements.

items.name: Purple sound
items.lineage: Purple sound emerged around Bristol producers including Joker, Guido and Gemmy, combining dubstep-related rhythm and bass with bright melodic synthesizer writing. Its connections with grime and other electronic scenes create an overlapping but recognizable production approach.
items.description: Vivid synthesizer leads and bass figures move over programmed drum patterns. Contrasting registers, melodic hooks and changes in density give the music its colorful, sharply outlined character.
exemplars: Joker — complete RA.962 studio DJ mix (2024)

items.name: Qanun
items.lineage: Qanun music centers on the plucked zither across Arab, Turkish and other regional performance traditions. Improvisation, ensemble accompaniment and newly composed repertoire connect inherited modal practices with contemporary exploration.
items.description: Plucked notes, tremolo and ornamented runs shape melodic lines over the instrument’s resonant strings. Solo compositions and ensemble settings offer different relationships between melody, harmony and rhythmic movement.
exemplars: Firas Zreik — Solo (2021), all four original compositions

items.name: Native American hip hop
items.lineage: Complete Supaman Prayer Loop Song performance filmed by Lloyd Blunk at the Gazette studio in 2014. Original filmmaker identifies a one-person loop-machine performance with live drum and flute layers and scratching an old record of Crow songs; CKUA explicitly identifies beatboxing, singing and rapping in the same video. All six source families are retained: vocal delivery, vocal percussion, Native flute, hand drum, live loop capture/playback and turntable scratching. The sampled old Crow record stays within the turntable source layer; its embedded performers and voices are unknown, not zero or invented live musicians. Authored recording realization of the full documented performance. One live human supplies both vocal cards and instrumental roles; repeated loops do not multiply performer count. Mixed sung/rap delivery and physiology remain source unspecified. The existing beatbox owner requires a gesture: an explicitly authored pulmonic-egressive velar-affricate snare is a compatible representative technique, not a phonetic measurement of Supaman. Ensemble-layer beatbox describes the combined loop texture, not extra people. Scratch/chopped variants realize positive vinyl scratching, not a measured scratch vocabulary or East Coast performer identity. All three isolated owners retain independent physical/workflow controls with unknown options. Room and signal chain are authored; no source hardware model, flute key, drum species or total embedded voice count is invented. Global tuning omitted.

items.name: Seychelles pop

items.description: Singing voices, guitar, bass, drums and keyboards create a flexible band texture. Saxophone responses can enrich a reggae-influenced branch, while the wider field includes other rhythms and arrangements.
exemplars: Grace Barbe and Antoinette Dodin — Mon Loreye (2021)

items.name: Sierra Leonean pop
items.lineage: Sierra Leonean pop connects artists, producers and listeners through local and diasporic networks. Contemporary performers combine popular songwriting with hip-hop, dancehall, Afrobeat and regional rhythmic references.
items.description: A fronting voice can move between rap and melody over bass, drums and keyboards. Saxophone lines add melodic responses in a live-band branch, while other productions use different textures.
exemplars: Drizilik and Freetown Uncut — Jazzlive announced2019 practice

items.name: South African Pop Dance
items.lineage: South African pop dance connects melodic popular songs with dance-oriented production and performance. Groups and singers draw on the country’s diverse rhythmic and electronic-music communities.
items.description: Sung refrains meet keyboards, bass and percussion, with trumpet and saxophone adding melodic hooks in a live-ensemble branch. Repetition and contrasting song sections connect the vocal line to the groove.
exemplars: Mi Casa — complete announced2015 National Arts Festival concert

items.name: Sudanese pop
items.lineage: Sudanese pop brings regional singing, melodic traditions and contemporary popular-song arrangements into dialogue. Local and diasporic artists develop varied ensembles and approaches rather than one fixed national sound.
items.description: Lead and supporting voices can meet oud, bass and percussion. Ornamented plucked phrases and vocal exchanges provide melodic detail, while repeated accompaniment gives songs rhythmic shape.
exemplars: Alsarah and the Nubatones — NPR Tiny Desk2016

items.name: Surinamese Pop
items.lineage: Surinamese pop connects singers and popular-song repertoires associated with Suriname and its diaspora. Artists move among acoustic songwriting, band arrangements and contemporary production across a multilingual musical field.
items.description: Expressive singing and repeated harmonic patterns carry memorable melodies. A voice-and-guitar setting highlights lyrics and phrasing, alongside the wider field’s fuller instrumental arrangements.
exemplars: David van Ooijen — complete solo-guitar arrangement of Kenny B’s Parijs

items.name: T-Pop Girl Group
items.lineage: T-pop girl groups bring Thai vocal ensembles into contemporary pop recording, choreography and fan communities. Group identities develop through songs, performances and collaborations across the Thai popular-music field.
items.description: Shared vocal lines and contrasting individual phrases meet chordal accompaniment and electronic percussion. Repeated hooks, coordinated responses and changing textures shape compact pop songs.
exemplars: Siriporn Yookaew/ploycris — complete four-page4EVE Test Me piano-solo arrangement154077

items.name: Tongan pop
items.lineage: Tongan pop connects Tongan artists and audiences with regional and international popular-music influences. Island and diasporic networks circulate songs that overlap reggae, soul and other contemporary styles.
items.description: Singing voices, electric guitar, bass, drums and electric piano support a flowing band texture. Vocal exchanges and instrumental responses can enrich the groove, with additional keyboards and horns appearing in larger arrangements.
exemplars: Aisea Taimani + Minor Islands — Jahmekya (Live & Direct, 2022)

items.name: Vietnamese Idol Pop
items.lineage: Vietnamese idol pop connects vocal groups, staged performance and fan-oriented song culture in Vietnam. Local groups adapt and develop repertoire within wider East Asian idol-pop networks.
items.description: Group singing, memorable refrains and chordal accompaniment create clear melodic contrasts. Electronic percussion supports the rhythmic drive of a vocal pop arrangement, alongside quieter interpretations of the same repertoire.
exemplars: 松尾 益民 (Matsuo) — Heavy Rotation, complete PTNA piano-solo edition149450

items.name: West Bengali Pop
items.lineage: West Bengali pop connects Bengali-language popular songs, songwriters and audiences in West Bengal. Film music, independent releases and live performances contribute overlapping strands to this regional field.
items.description: Melodic singing and chordal accompaniment foreground the lyric and refrain. Piano supports an intimate song rendition, while band and electronic arrangements give other performances a different rhythmic character.
exemplars: KumarjitDey — Jawl Phoring (Anupam Roy), complete solo piano arrangement26579233

items.name: Sinhala EDM
items.lineage: Sinhala EDM connects Sri Lankan and diasporic producers, DJs and audiences with contemporary electronic dance music. Sinhala-associated songs and regional collaborations circulate alongside wider international club styles.
items.description: Synthesizer phrases and electronic drums create repeated dance sections and changes in intensity. Club-oriented production can combine melodic hooks, bass weight and transitions, with voices appearing in some releases.
exemplars: DJ Mass — whole Bandwagon Mix090 commissioned for MARQUEE resident feature2019

items.name: Ukrainian EDM
items.lineage: Ukrainian EDM connects electronic dance producers, DJs, broadcasters and listeners through Ukrainian and international networks. The field embraces varied club styles rather than a single uniform rhythmic formula.
items.description: Synthesizer patterns and electronic percussion organize repeated dance passages, breaks and returns. Bass and melodic layers change in density as the arrangement develops.

items.name: Rwandan Gospel
items.lineage: Rwandan gospel connects Christian devotional singing, choirs and recording communities in Rwanda. Songs circulate through worship, concerts and media, with both accompanied and unaccompanied approaches.
items.description: Blended group voices carry the text through shared phrases and harmonic movement. An unaccompanied choral branch emphasizes ensemble balance and collective delivery, while other performances add instruments.
exemplars: Ambassadors Of Christ Choir — ABANTU B’UMUKIZA (Acapella Version), whole issued version

items.name: Borneo traditional
items.lineage: Complete Karan Kayu: Sapek Kayan Solo with Male Vocals, issued2016 by Tresno Records from its own June2015 field recordings in West Kalimantan. Exact track title positively identifies one solo sapek Kayan role plus male singing. Retain both complete roles; individual singer count and whether player also sings are not stated. Other compilation tracks with bronze percussion, belikan and nature recordings are not part of this selected full track. DroneModal.string scopes the positively documented melody-and-drone Kayan lute practice. Existing sape owner only offers named datun-julud dance, belian ritual or modern stage-fusion contexts; none is established for Karan Kayu. Isolated credited sapek Kayan owner retains source identity without importing those contexts or a false modern amplified model. Independent firsthand Kayan documentation supports a carved wooden open-backed lute with two strings, one melodic and one drone; no claim the separately described maker or exact specimen is this recording. Unknown source singer count remains unknown; single accompanied lead is an expressly authored realization, not measured number of humans. No anatomical vocal, pitch-system or global tuning claim. Controlled live-room rendition is explicitly authored, not the actual field recording location or equipment. Optional signal chain omitted. Separate physical controls preserve documented wooden open-backed construction, melody/drone string roles, three scalloped frets and plucked excitation; string material and absolute pitches remain unspecified.

items.name: Cantonese Traditional
items.lineage: Cantonese traditional music developed in the Pearl River Delta and through Guangdong and Hong Kong performance networks. Instrumental ensembles, inherited tunes and newer compositions continue a regional tradition shaped by theatre, social performance and recording.
items.description: A bright gaohu melody and struck yangqin patterns can share an ornamented melodic line. Larger groups add other bowed, plucked and wind instruments, creating varied versions of the same tune.
exemplars: Wong Kong-Yu — Eight Cantonese Folk Songs, complete solo-piano collection

items.name: Chill Baile
items.lineage: Chill baile connects Brazilian funk references with relaxed electronic production and overlapping R&B and club communities. Producers reshape rhythmic and melodic material into a more spacious branch of baile-related listening.
items.description: Layered sampled phrases and electronic percussion build compact grooves with room for melodic detail. Repetition, changes in density and softer contrasts provide movement without requiring an unbroken high-intensity presentation.
exemplars: VHOOR with Maffalda/DJ Tonias — full Aquecimento NTS12February2026 programme

items.name: Chinese Electropop
items.lineage: Chinese electropop connects popular songwriting with electronic sound and production across Chinese-language music networks. Bands and producers combine vocal melodies with keyboards, programming and other instruments.
items.description: A singing voice, guitar and bass can interact with electronic keyboards and programmed material. Repeated hooks and contrasting textures connect a band-based sound to electronic pop rhythms.
exemplars: JADE EYES — Baybeats2023 complete announced programme

items.name: Chinese Soundtrack
items.lineage: Chinese soundtrack music serves film and other screen storytelling across a broad range of productions. Composers develop themes and dramatic cues using acoustic ensembles, electronic production and intimate instrumental settings.
items.description: Piano can present a lyrical screen theme through connected melody, harmonic movement and flexible phrasing. Other cues use different instrumental colors and textures to support dramatic pacing.
exemplars: Tan Dun — The Eternal Vow, complete piano-solo edition MN0081073

items.name: Cuban Alternative
items.lineage: Cuban alternative music connects artists and independent creative networks across contemporary Cuban song. It overlaps trova, rock and other popular forms while encouraging varied combinations of instruments and rhythmic references.
items.description: Voices, guitars, bass, drums and percussion can combine in flexible song arrangements. Brass and reeds may add responses and counterlines, with contrasting textures supporting the lyric and refrain.

items.name: Cumbia Sonorense
items.lineage: Cumbia sonorense connects dance bands and audiences in Sonora, Mexico. Regional performers adapt cumbia through amplified ensembles and local performance networks.
items.description: Singing, keyboards, guitar and bass ride over drum kit, güiro and congas. Saxophone phrases and repeated melodic hooks reinforce the dance groove.
exemplars: Los Comandos del Oeste — full June28,2026 La Sauceda ensemble

items.name: Dansei Seiyu
items.lineage: Dansei seiyu connects the musical work of male Japanese voice actors with recordings, concerts and character-related entertainment. The field includes varied popular-song styles rather than one uniform vocal technique.
items.description: Singing voices carry melodic hooks over chordal accompaniment. An intimate piano-led song arrangement emphasizes phrasing, while other releases use bands and electronic production.
exemplars: Yamaha — Mamoru Miyano Selection for Piano, complete ten-song solo-piano edition GTP01086302

items.name: Dansk Lovsang
items.lineage: Dansk lovsang connects Danish-language Christian worship songs with congregational, concert and recorded practice. Hymn traditions and newer devotional songwriting meet through varied musical settings.
items.description: Group singing and chordal accompaniment support shared phrases and clear text. Piano can guide the harmony and pulse, while other performances use larger bands or instrumental hymn reinterpretations.
exemplars: Den Danske Salmeduo — complete announced 30th anniversary instrumental hymn concert, Sankt Lukas Kirke, 20 September 2026

items.name: Dansktop
items.lineage: Dansktop connects Danish popular songs, dance bands and broadcasting traditions. Singers and groups circulate accessible melodies through recordings, social dancing and public performances.
items.description: Lead and supporting voices meet electric guitars, keyboards, bass and drums. Clear refrains and steady ensemble accompaniment encourage familiar, participatory listening and dancing.
exemplars: Kandis — complete presenter-issued2025 band practice used for the2026 Fuglsø dance-evening programme

items.name: Danspunk
items.lineage: Danspunk connects a Nordic popular-music discovery field with dance-oriented songs, humor and regional performers. Its varied repertoire is distinct from treating the name as a direct synonym for Anglo-American dance-punk.
items.description: Singing and guitar can carry humorous observations through memorable refrains. An acoustic song branch emphasizes verbal delivery and rhythmic accompaniment alongside the field’s more amplified performances.
exemplars: Billy Opel — complete Riksteatern solo show, April2, Folkan Örnsköldsvik

items.name: Deep Full On
items.lineage: Deep full-on belongs to psychedelic trance production and its night-oriented dance networks. Artists and DJs develop extended electronic grooves with layered melodic and timbral movement.
items.description: Repeating bass figures and electronic percussion create a continuous dance foundation. Changes in density, accents and phrase patterns shape longer passages and transitions.
exemplars: Archive — complete Live from the basement vol II, 2:04:35

items.name: Draga
items.lineage: Draga connects drag performers, popular songs and performance communities, particularly in Mexican drag culture. Recorded releases and stage presentation overlap dance-pop and other styles without requiring one fixed vocal sound.
items.description: Expressive voices meet electronic melodic layers and percussion. Repeated hooks and contrasting sections support theatrical delivery, with performers choosing varied arrangements and vocal presentations.
exemplars: Pixie Pixie feat.Neiko — PORNSTAR (Acapella), whole issued2023version

items.name: Drama
items.lineage: Dramatic spoken performance gives written characters, dialogue and narration distinct voices. Cast readings and recorded plays present stories through timing, delivery and exchanges between speakers.
items.description: Speech carries the action through changing emphasis, pauses and contrasts between roles. Edited dialogue can form a complete performance without music or effects.
exemplars: LibriVox — The Importance of Being Earnest (version3), complete three-act dramatic reading

items.name: Euroska
items.lineage: Euroska connects European ska bands and audiences with Jamaican-derived rhythms and exchanges with punk and other popular styles. Touring ensembles and independent scenes develop varied local sounds.
items.description: Singing, rhythmic guitar, bass and drums meet keyboards and punchy brass or reed responses. Offbeat figures and short ensemble accents give energetic songs a clear dance pulse.
exemplars: The Busters — complete published current nine-person performing practice

items.name: Fisarmonica
items.lineage: Fisarmonica centers the accordion in Italian instrumental and popular-music traditions. Players draw on dance tunes, songs and concert repertoire, combining melodic playing with the instrument’s own accompaniment.
items.description: Bellows phrasing connects a treble melody to bass and chord patterns. Changes in articulation and register shape both lyrical passages and rhythmic dance material.
exemplars: Carlo Venturi — Romero, complete Novalis/Unione accordion melody-and-chord score

items.name: Folclore extremeño
items.lineage: Folclore extremeño encompasses traditional repertoires and performance practices associated with Extremadura. The tamborilero tradition is a distinctive instrumental strand within that broader regional heritage.
items.description: One musician can play a three-hole gaita and tamboril together, combining a clear melody with a repeated drum pulse. Ornament and rhythmic variation give shape to tunes used in local communal settings.
exemplars: Sierra de Gata tamborilero — complete one-person instrumental practice

items.name: French Worship
items.lineage: French worship connects French-language Christian devotional songwriting with congregational and recorded practice. Solo artists and groups circulate songs through churches, concerts and media.
items.description: A singing voice and piano can lead reflective phrases and repeated devotional lines. Intimate accompaniment supports the text, while other worship settings use larger vocal or instrumental groups.
exemplars: Dan Luiten — Ma Dévotion2021, complete30-song piano/voice edition

items.name: Full On Groove
items.lineage: Full-on groove belongs to psychedelic trance production and dance performance. Producers develop sustained rhythmic drive through repeating figures and changes in melodic and timbral detail.
items.description: Synthesized bass and electronic drums create a continuous foundation for longer passages. Accents, breaks and changes in density provide contrast while preserving the underlying pulse.
exemplars: StarLab — complete2020 Virtual Burning Man Own Spirit DJ programme

items.name: Ghanaian Traditional
items.lineage: Ghanaian traditional music encompasses distinct community repertoires, ceremonies and instrumental practices. Dagomba pressure-drum ensembles form one important strand within this varied national field.
items.description: Lead and responding hourglass drums shape changing pitch and rhythm, with vocal calls or ululations in some settings. Ceremonial meaning and ensemble interaction guide performances, alongside other traditions with different instruments.
exemplars: Three Lunsi Drummers/A.B. Lunnaa — complete Harvest Songs (1), FW04324_101

items.name: Glass
items.lineage: Glass music centers instruments whose vibrating glass produces sustained or struck tones. The glass harmonica forms an important branch, with repertoire ranging from historical compositions to newer concert work.
items.description: Wet fingers set rotating glass bowls into vibration, producing connected, ringing tones. Sustained melody and changes in touch support an intimate solo texture.
exemplars: Thomas Bloch — Mozart Adagio K356, complete solo track6 from Music for Glass Harmonica

items.name: Granada Indie
items.lineage: Granada indie connects independent bands, releases and performance networks in Granada, Spain. Artists continue a varied local history through guitar music and newer electronic colors.
items.description: Group and lead voices meet electric guitars, bass, drums and synthesizer layers. Strong riffs and contrasting melodic passages create a contemporary alternative-rock branch.
exemplars: Tremendo Pinkman — complete festival-documented five-member live configuration after late2024

items.name: Greek Indie
items.lineage: Greek indie connects independent artists and creative networks in Greece across electronic and band-based styles. Songwriting, studio experimentation and local releases contribute to a varied field.
items.description: A singing voice can interact with drums, synthesizer textures, keyboards and programmed material. Spacious arrangements leave room for melodic phrases and changes in density.
exemplars: Hume Assine featuring Anna Paspati — complete Crying(2020)

items.name: Guitarra Andina
items.lineage: Guitarra andina brings Andean repertories and expressive practices into solo-guitar performance. Arrangements can connect regional melodies, dance references and instrumental narratives through distinctive tuning and phrasing approaches.
items.description: Plucked nylon strings carry melody, accompaniment and contrasting sections within one instrument. Variable tuning and changes in articulation can shape resonance and dramatic movement.
exemplars: Camilo Pajuelo — complete Helme solo-guitar film2014, GarcíaZárate adaptation

items.name: Gyerekdalok
items.lineage: Gyerekdalok encompasses Hungarian children’s songs used in family, educational and public musical settings. Familiar melodies circulate through singing, accompaniment and arranged instrumental versions.
items.description: Clear sung phrases and repeated melodies encourage shared participation. Piano can support the tune with simple harmonic patterns, while other versions use different accompaniment or voices alone.
exemplars: Gryllus/Koszorus — whole EMB20120 twenty-song piano-four-hands edition

items.name: Humour français
items.lineage: Humour français connects French-language comic performance with stage, broadcast and recorded traditions. Monologues, character voices and narrated situations give performers varied ways to shape an audience’s response.
items.description: Spoken delivery, timing and pauses carry the humor. Changes in emphasis and character can build contrast without requiring sung melody or instrumental accompaniment.
exemplars: Fernand Raynaud — Le22 à Asnières / Le Plombier / C’est étudié pour (complete Philips8188224 issue,1984)

items.name: Indian violin
items.lineage: Lalgudi Jayaraman with Palghat Raghu and Vinayakram — complete Parvathi Mysore concert (1973). Authored present-day rendition of the complete credited instrumental programme. Lalgudi violin lineage follows the actual featured violinist; Palghat mridangam lineage is positively supported by a first-person fellow musician’s account of Raghu studying with Mani Iyer. Microtonally inflected bowing, seated South Indian posture, tonic/fifth violin tuning and synthetic strings are explicit representative choices, not measured 1973 equipment. Mridangam jackwood/goat-buffalo construction and standard heads are authored. Ghatam Manamadurai denotes an authored clay-temper construction choice, not Vinayakram’s personal pedagogical lineage or identified historical pot; full-bowl strike is an authored default, not an assertion excluding other gestures. Controlled live room and neutral numeric axes are authored; global temperament and capture apparatus omitted. No new instrument owner or source-inferred lineage is introduced.
items.description: The family-supplied venue archive issues the complete 1973 concert with violin, mridangam and ghatam; its fourteen-piece programme includes a raga-tanam-pallavi and closing pieces. Three credited instrumentalists, no separately credited vocal performer. Later concerts with the violinist’s children are explicitly outside this dated programme. Indian violin denotes the Indian violin-performance repertoire field, overlapping broad violin and Indian classical umbrellas without being equivalent to either. The exact creator roster includes Lalgudi Jayaraman alongside Carnatic and Hindustani players and contemporary popular interpretations. Existing indian_classical remains a broad Indian art-music umbrella, not merely its sarangi exemplar; existing violin likewise remains broad instrumental repertoire, not just its Bartok source. The present instrument-and-practice intersection retains a complete Carnatic concert branch, not a claim all Indian violin uses this trio. Jazz/pop/baroque violin categories overlap particular practices but do not cover this named Indian performance field. Queued regional Indian popular/folk categories do not impose a violin-specific repertoire field. Selected concert practice supports artMusic.southAsian, without assigning every creator-list recording to classical music. exemplars: Lalgudi Jayaraman with Palghat Raghu and Vinayakram — complete Parvathi Mysore concert (1973)

items.name: Indie Sudcaliforniano
items.lineage: Indie sudcaliforniano connects independent music networks in Baja California Sur, Mexico. Local bands and releases bring varied rock and popular-song approaches into a regional field.
items.description: Singing, electric guitar, bass and drums create an amplified band foundation. A requinto can add a contrasting melodic voice in arrangements that combine different guitar roles.

items.name: Indonesian Worship
items.lineage: Indonesian worship connects Christian devotional songs and musical communities in Indonesia. Choirs, soloists and groups circulate repertoire through churches, performances and recordings.
items.description: Lead and ensemble singing can share melodic phrases over acoustic guitar. Repeated lines and chordal support create an accessible devotional texture, alongside more extensively arranged versions.
exemplars: JPCC Worship Choir — Bersinar Terang, complete official lyric-video edition2021

items.name: Japanese Boom Bap
items.lineage: Japanese boom bap connects Japanese rap and beat-making with sample-oriented hip-hop production. Artists and producers develop local voices within a wider international network of releases, DJ practice and collaboration.
items.description: Rhythmic verses meet layered samples and recurring beat patterns. Changes in flow, emphasis and loop texture create contrast while keeping the lyric in the foreground.
exemplars: DJ Woodz-N — Japanese Boom Bap MIX Vol.2, complete33:16programme2022

items.name: Japanese Celtic
items.lineage: Japanese Celtic music connects musicians and listeners in Japan with Irish, Scottish and related repertories. Sessions, touring ensembles and local communities sustain varied approaches to tunes and songs.
items.description: Fiddle and guitar can meet singing, piano and bodhran accompaniment. Ornamented melodies and rhythmic variation shape the tune, with supporting percussion adding color in some ensembles.
exemplars: John John Festival — complete current trio practice

items.name: Japanese experimental
items.lineage: Japanese experimental music connects diverse exploratory practices across composition, improvisation and sound-making. Its field extends beyond amplified noise to quieter acoustic work and collective musical exchange.
items.description: Acoustic guitars can build loosely structured dialogue through contrasting gestures, resonance and repeated figures. Listening and response guide changes in texture without a fixed song form.
exemplars: Yousei Umeki — Extra Light, complete sixteen-piece acoustic improvisation release (2019)

items.name: Japanese Jazztronica
items.lineage: Japanese jazztronica connects jazz-oriented musicians and electronic production through releases and collaborative networks. Acoustic playing and programmed rhythm meet in varied instrumental arrangements.
items.description: Saxophone lines, keyboards and bass interact with electronic beat production. Melodic phrasing and rhythmic variation connect improvisatory playing to repeated patterns.
exemplars: Ted Taforo, ddddeeeellllaaa, Emiliano Lasansky — Diavola, whole2024single

items.name: Japanese worship
items.lineage: Japanese worship connects Japanese-language Christian songs with local church and devotional communities. Artists use solo, group and recorded settings to circulate praise and reflective repertoire.
items.description: A singing voice and acoustic guitar can carry prayerful lyrics through repeated melodic phrases. Chordal accompaniment supports the text in an intimate branch alongside fuller ensemble arrangements.
exemplars: Takahiro Tone Nakamine — Ai No Iro, documented regular solo-acoustic performance practice

items.name: Kannada Indie
items.lineage: Kannada indie connects independent Kannada-language artists and Karnataka performance networks. Local originals draw on rock, popular songwriting and varied regional musical references.
items.description: Singing voices, electric guitar, bass and drums create a band foundation, with flute adding melodic contrast. Ensemble changes and memorable phrases shape an indie-rock branch of the wider field.
exemplars: Mysore Xpress — full five-person performing unit documented April2022

items.name: Kompa Chrétien
items.lineage: Kompa chrétien connects Haitian Christian songs and worship audiences with kompa-influenced popular music. Artists and listeners bring devotional texts into recorded and live dance-band settings.
items.description: Sung refrains meet guitar, bass, keyboards and drums. Repeated accompaniment and interlocking rhythmic figures support a flowing groove beneath the devotional voice.
exemplars: DJ H509 — whole MIX GOSPEL KONPA FIN ANNEE 2022

items.name: Korean Musicals
items.lineage: Korean musicals connect theatrical storytelling, composed songs and staged performance in Korea. Original productions and international exchanges contribute to a varied musical-theatre repertoire.
items.description: Singing voices carry character and dramatic action through melody and text. Piano can support an intimate theatrical song, while full productions use larger ensembles and varied orchestrations.
exemplars: Will Aronson / Hue Park — Why Love (James’s Piano Solo), complete MN0309208 edition

items.name: Lagu Aceh
items.lineage: Lagu Aceh connects songs and melodies associated with Aceh to regional performance, education and newer arrangements. Familiar repertoire such as Bungong Jeumpa circulates through singing and instrumental interpretations.
items.description: A singing voice can present the regional melody over chordal accompaniment. Piano offers one arranged setting, alongside other local instruments, ensembles and unaccompanied versions.
exemplars: Ayunia Saputro — Ananda Sukarlan Rapsodia Nusantara no.6, complete4:35 piano-solo video

items.name: Lagu Betawi
items.lineage: Lagu Betawi connects songs associated with Jakarta’s Betawi cultural heritage to community and contemporary performance. Familiar melodies circulate through varied vocal and instrumental arrangements.
items.description: Group voices can share a melody and harmonic responses without instrumental accompaniment. Repeated phrases and clear text give a communal vocal setting its shape.
exemplars: Jamaica Café — Jali-jali at WWF Indonesia Do Better for Earth,31January2010

items.name: Lagu Manado
items.lineage: Lagu Manado connects songs associated with Manado and North Sulawesi to regional and diasporic audiences. Familiar melodies circulate through singing, local performance and new arrangements.
items.description: A singing voice brings the melody and text forward over chordal support. Piano provides an intimate arranged setting, while other versions use different ensembles and textures.
exemplars: Agus Sandjaya — complete Ananda Sukarlan Rapsodia Nusantara no.8, programme12April2019

items.name: Louvor ICM
items.lineage: Louvor ICM connects hymns and devotional singing within the Igreja Cristã Maranata. Congregational practice and the sharing of new songs emphasize the relationship between melody, words and worship.
items.description: Singing can be supported by acoustic guitar and keyboard. Clear melodic phrases and chordal accompaniment make the text audible and encourage collective participation.
exemplars: Igreja Cristã Maranata Department of Praise — complete prescribed new-hymn submission audio practice

items.name: Piratenmuziek
items.lineage: Piratenmuziek connects Dutch-language popular songs with pirate-radio traditions and their listeners. Broadcasters and local communities circulate familiar repertoire across styles and generations.
items.description: Memorable sung melodies and clear refrains meet chordal accompaniment and rhythmic backing. The music’s social circulation includes requests and spoken hosting, while the songs themselves support varied vocal arrangements.
exemplars: DJ Onslow — complete Puike Platenpaleis110 radio programme

items.name: Rhythm Game
items.lineage: Rhythm-game music connects compositions and recordings to games organized around musical timing and player interaction. The repertoire spans electronic production, popular songs and instrumental themes, with independent arrangements extending beyond the game.
items.description: Piano can present a melodic game theme through clear phrasing and harmonic contrasts. Other tracks use voices, ensembles or electronic textures, reflecting the field’s wide stylistic range.
exemplars: Sakuzyo — Altale, complete Yamaha DEEMO piano-solo edition

items.name: Thai OST
items.lineage: Thai television and screen soundtrack songs, closely connected to the country’s pop industry and performers. Romantic drama themes, character songs and series tie-ins circulate both through their productions and as independent pop releases.
items.description: Expressive singing, melodic hooks and chordal accompaniment connect ballads, band-based pop and electronic arrangements. Thai BL soundtrack music forms an overlapping subset; the wider field also covers other television romances and drama franchises.

items.name: Türkçe remix
items.lineage: Türkçe remix connects Turkish-language popular songs with remix production and club circulation. Producers and DJs reshape familiar vocal material through electronic arrangement and rhythmic treatment.
items.description: Sung hooks meet layered samples and electronic percussion. Repeated phrases, changes in density and contrasting sections support a dance-oriented reworking of the song.
exemplars: Emre Çağlar — Türkçe Remix Set2020, complete19-selection mix

items.name: Ugandan traditional
items.lineage: Ugandan traditional music encompasses varied community repertoires and instrumental practices. Singing with adungu is one strand within a wider heritage of vocal, harp and ensemble performance.
items.description: A voice and plucked harp can share an intimate melodic and rhythmic texture. Repeated accompaniment supports expressive text, with sacred and secular contexts varying across communities and repertoire.
exemplars: Michael Mawoni — Hiwumbe Awumba, complete2:34 issued track

items.name: Ülkücü Şarkılar
items.lineage: Ülkücü şarkılar connects songs and performers associated with Turkey’s nationalist movement and its audiences. Bardic and popular-song approaches circulate alongside varied recorded and public performances.
items.description: Voice and bağlama can foreground text through ornamented melody and repeated accompaniment. Changes in vocal emphasis and plucked phrasing shape a lyric-centered bardic branch.
exemplars: Ozan Arif — self-described solo theatre-intermission programmes,circa1970–72

items.name: Underground Boom Bap
items.lineage: Underground boom bap connects rappers, producers, independent releases and listening communities around sample-oriented hip-hop. Recordings and DJ circulation sustain a field that crosses cities and national borders.
items.description: Rhythmic verses meet layered samples and recurring beats. Vocal flow and changes in loop texture provide contrast while the accompaniment maintains a stable rhythmic foundation.
exemplars: DJ King Flow — complete Mixtape Addict86 first hour and interview

items.name: Dark Progressive House
items.lineage: Dark progressive house — brooding, harmonically layered house associated with extended DJ development.
items.description: Dark progressive house emphasizes shadowy atmosphere, gradual builds and intricate harmonic layers over a steady house pulse. Its DJs and producers develop long transitions and evolving textures, connecting progressive-house structure with a darker, immersive club sound. Moshic and related radio and label communities illustrate this strand.
exemplars: Moshic — complete January2022 live DJ mix1:00:26

items.name: Anime Rap
items.lineage: Anime rap — fan-created hip-hop interpreting anime characters, stories and worlds.
items.description: Anime rap turns characters and storylines from Japanese animation into original rap narratives. Performers combine rhythmic verses, hooks and produced hip-hop beats with fan interpretation, sometimes speaking through a character’s perspective. Online video communities support a transnational field that overlaps nerdcore and rap geek while centering anime themes.
exemplars: Juu Rafaela and Hawky — complete O Fim do Clã Zenin (Acapella),2026

items.name: Armenian Hip Hop
items.lineage: Armenian hip hop connects rap production in Armenia and its diaspora, including work concerned with cultural memory, social experience and contemporary life. Diaspora artists also draw on the wider hip-hop scenes in which they work.
items.description: Rhythmic verses, storytelling and wordplay interact with produced beats and, in some songs, sung hooks. Boom-bap-influenced production and unaccompanied protest delivery are among the approaches used within the field.

items.name: Botswana Hip Hop
items.lineage: Botswana hip hop connects local rappers, producers and DJs through national recording, radio and club networks, with close exchanges across southern Africa.
items.description: Rhythmic rap and sung hooks meet beat-led accompaniment and DJ mixing. Setswana-English Motswako intersects this wider national field, while club programmes also cross into electro and house. ATI and DJ Fauz exemplify its vocal and DJ-led branches.

items.name: Classical Drill
items.lineage: Classical drill brings classical themes and orchestral or piano textures into the instrumental production language of drill.
items.description: Piano figures and string textures meet syncopated drill beats. Producers adapt familiar classical themes or write cinematic instrumental material, using contrast between melodic detail and forceful rhythmic foundations. These beats circulate as standalone releases as well as potential settings for rap.

items.name: Detroit Trap Brasileiro
items.lineage: Detroit trap brasileiro — Brazil’s early-2020s adaptation of Detroit rap, marked by punchline-led Portuguese verses, loose placement against the beat and prominent rhythmic bass.
items.description: Detroit trap brasileiro adapts Detroit rap’s playful punchlines and elastic delivery to Brazilian Portuguese. Piano figures, prominent bass and buoyant percussion frame loosely placed verses, often with irreverent humor. The scene expanded in the early 2020s through independent rappers and producers, with sampling and local references giving the imported style new inflections.

items.name: Ethiopian Hip Hop
items.lineage: Ethiopian rap developed through Addis Ababa and diaspora networks, adapting hip-hop rhythms to Amharic and other local languages.
items.description: Ethiopian hip hop combines rhythmic rap with produced beats and local language wordplay. Amharic is prominent alongside Oromo, Tigrinya and English, with themes ranging from everyday life and storytelling to social criticism. Addis Ababa artists and diaspora collaborators connect boom-bap and trap production with Ethiopian cultural references.

items.name: German Viral Rap
items.lineage: A German-language rap community shaped by online video creators, collaborations and rapidly circulating songs. Music, comedy, gaming and choreographed video production intersect within the broader Deutschrap field.
items.description: Rhythmic German-language delivery and memorable refrains ride programmed beats and a defined electronic low end. Vocal character, punchlines and contrasts between rap passages and hooks work closely with the visual presentation, while production draws on contemporary rap and pop.

items.name: Hip hop boliviano
items.lineage: Bolivian hip-hop brings together local and diaspora rap communities, including links between La Paz and São Paulo. Groups such as Santa Mala combine Spanish-language rap and singing with accounts of migration, identity and everyday life.
items.description: Rapped and sung phrases pass between performers over rhythmically grounded DJ accompaniment. Vocal exchanges, repeated hooks and a strong beat support direct lyrical delivery, while styles and production approaches vary across the wider scene.

items.name: Hip Hop Mauritanien
items.lineage: Mauritanian hip hop — a multilingual urban movement shaped by Senegalese and international rap from the 1990s, local production networks and the Assalamalekoum festival.
items.description: Mauritanian hip hop developed through youth networks linking Nouakchott with Senegal and wider international rap. Rhythmic spoken delivery and produced beats carry social commentary, local identity and contemporary concerns across the country’s languages. Independent studios, discovery competitions and Assalamalekoum have helped connect performers, producers and audiences across regional communities.

items.name: Hip Hop Timur
items.lineage: Hip hop timur brings the languages, experiences and local identities of eastern Indonesia into rap and digital beat production.
items.description: Eastern Indonesian hip hop connects local-language rap, rhythmic wordplay and independently produced beats. Communities in places such as Maumere and Ambon develop recordings, collaborations and live events that express regional identity while participating in national hip-hop networks. Delivery and production vary across this diverse field rather than following a single island-wide sound.

items.name: Hong Kong Hip Hop
items.lineage: Hong Kong hip-hop — local rap communities linking Cantonese expression, beat production and performance.
items.description: Hong Kong hip-hop connects local language and city experience with international rap styles. Its artists work across jazz-sampled boom bap, trap and melodic or atmospheric rap. Producers and MCs shape recorded songs as well as live performance and competitive battles, with LMF and later independent crews contributing to the scene’s development.
exemplars: VEEHK 讚美之王 — complete announced two-participant acapella challenge,18 February2026

items.name: Icelandic Hip Hop
items.lineage: Icelandic hip hop developed through an Iceland-based rap recording and live-performance community, with Reykjavík festivals connecting local artists and audiences.
items.description: MC-led verses and melodic hooks combine with DJ and electronic production. Live-band branches can add guitar, bass, drums and piano, as heard in Úlfur Úlfur’s performances. Multiple voices and contrasting acoustic and electronic textures broaden the concert sound.

items.name: Israelite hip hop
items.lineage: Israelite hip hop develops within contemporary Hebrew-Israelite music communities, combining rap culture with biblical themes, identity and devotional expression. Independent artists and community radio networks circulate the music through recordings and shared religious-cultural spaces.
items.description: Rap, melodic vocal delivery and devotional lyrics connect personal testimony with communal identity. Beat-driven productions and unaccompanied vocal releases both occur within the field.
exemplars: Freebrew Elarie — Psalms23(Acapella), complete2021 bonus edition

items.name: Korean Drill
items.lineage: Korean drill — South Korean rap adapting the rhythmic delivery and bass-heavy production of the international drill scene.
items.description: Korean drill develops drill’s sparse, forceful beat language within South Korean hip-hop. Rapped verses ride deep electronic bass, programmed drums and economical melodic textures. Artists including Fleeky Bang draw on Bronx drill while developing local crews, language and performance styles. The sound participates in a shared drill lineage while belonging to Korea’s contemporary rap community.

items.name: Korean underground rap
items.lineage: Korean underground rap connects independent crews, producers, DJs and club audiences within the wider Korean hip-hop scene. Networks such as Daenamhyup and Rock Bottom combine self-organized collaboration with international touring and exchanges with the commercial music industry.
items.description: Rhythmically articulated rap voices work against DJ-selected beats and recorded textures. Crew exchanges, repeated hooks and energetic rhythmic delivery connect local underground collaboration with the live hip-hop stage; reggae and trap influences coexist within the repertoire.

items.name: Lao Hip Hop
items.lineage: Lao hip hop connects rap and beat production in Laos with Lao diaspora communities, combining contemporary expression with local languages and cultural memory.
items.description: Rhythmic verses and memorable hooks ride produced beats in Lao hip hop. Artists in Laos and the diaspora address everyday experience and identity in Lao and English, while some arrangements introduce the khaen mouth organ or draw on lam traditions. Concerts, cultural festivals and online collaborations link these varied approaches.

items.name: Latvian hip hop
items.lineage: Latvian hip-hop connects Latvian-language rap, independent releases and live performance. Artists such as Skutelis place detailed lyrical delivery at the center of a scene that includes solo MC work, collaboration and DJ-led concert practice.
items.description: A foreground rap voice shapes phrases against recurring beats and recorded textures. DJ selection and mixing support the changing emphasis of the lyrics, with clear rhythmic articulation and space for pauses, accents and refrains.

items.name: Magyar Trap
items.lineage: Magyar trap is Hungary’s contemporary trap scene, adapting 808-heavy hip-hop production to Hungarian-language verses, short hooks and playful ad-libs.
items.description: Emerging artists including Lil Frakk, Lmen Prala and the AKC collective connect spacious rap phrasing with heavy electronic low end and programmed rhythm. Personal, ironic and confrontational lyrics coexist, while melodic delivery and pitch processing connect parts of the scene with pop.
