The local network developed through online releases, collaborations and energetic live audiences.

items.name: Maltese Hip Hop
items.lineage: Malta’s hip-hop community brings together rap, DJ practice and beat production, with artists and labels connecting local performance and recording scenes.
items.description: Rap delivery and sung hooks interact with programmed drum patterns and turntable cuts. Guitar accompaniment can add chordal rhythm to the electronic foundation, while Maltese-language expression and local collaborations shape the scene.

items.name: Military Rap
items.lineage: Military rap is a hip-hop community shaped by service members and veterans, with songs addressing service, deployment, family and the return to civilian life. Recordings and performances connect artists with military and veteran audiences.
items.description: Personal narrative and rhythmic spoken delivery lead the music, supported by rap production and recurring beats. Intimate unaccompanied versions also foreground the words; military subject matter does not require marching-band instrumentation or drill cadence.

items.name: Mongolian Hip Hop
items.lineage: Mongolian hip hop brings together rap and beat production within Mongolia’s contemporary music scene. Ulaanbaatar producers connect local releases with international hip-hop networks, including an instrumental sample-based strand.
items.description: Chopped melodic fragments, drum patterns and recorded vocal textures can be layered into instrumental beats. Rhythmic swing and repeated phrases support this production branch, alongside the wider scene’s MC-led work.

items.name: Northeast Indian Hip Hop
items.lineage: Northeast Indian hip hop connects multilingual rap communities across India’s northeastern states. Groups such as Khasi Bloodz bring regional identity, local languages and youth experience into a shared hip-hop network.
items.description: Rhythmic speech and contrasting MC voices meet programmed beats, DJ accompaniment and live-band arrangements. Guitar, bass and drums can reinforce the groove, while language, flow and lyrical perspective vary across the region.

items.name: Norwegian Trap
items.lineage: Norwegian trap connects local rap communities and producers with the international trap economy, including online beat production and collaborations across scenes.
items.description: Rap delivery and produced trap beats meet Norwegian language, regional expression and international influences. Local artist networks coexist with producers making instrumentals for overseas rappers. The scene overlaps with other Norwegian hip-hop and club styles while retaining trap as a particular production approach.

items.name: Persian Underground Hip Hop
items.lineage: Persian underground hip hop grew through independent Iranian and diaspora recording, circulation and performance networks, including the community around Hichkas and Moltafet.
items.description: Forceful, conversational rap places Persian-language writing and social observation over rhythmic beat production. Independent releases and online circulation connect artists across Iran and the diaspora. The field overlaps broader Persian hip hop while emphasizing these independent creative networks.

items.name: Pinoy Alternative Rap
items.lineage: Pinoy alternative rap develops through independent Philippine hip-hop communities that value artistic experimentation, collaboration and self-directed production. Networks such as UPRISING connect rappers and DJs across local languages and styles.
items.description: Individual MC voices and contrasting flows interact with sampled beats, low bass and changing textures. Live performance, turntablism and collaborative production provide room for lyrical and sonic approaches outside a single mainstream formula.

items.name: Polish Drill
items.lineage: Polish drill — Polish-language rap adapting British-influenced drill production and delivery.
items.description: Polish drill brings Polish-language rap into the British-influenced drill sound, with forceful rhythmic verses over sparse melodies, electronic bass and sharply programmed drums. Artists such as Miszel connect local rap communities with international drill platforms. The field shares drill’s production vocabulary while developing its own language, performers and audience.

items.name: Polish old school hip hop
items.lineage: Polish old-school hip hop preserves the foundational practices of the country’s hip-hop communities, linking rap with b-boy culture, DJing and sample-based beatmaking. Earlier scenes and continuing practitioners share an emphasis on breaks, loops and the creative reuse of recorded music.
items.description: Rhythmic rap delivery and loop-based beats sit alongside instrumental productions for breaking. Producers cut and rearrange samples into recurring grooves, drawing on both local and international records.

items.name: Polish underground rap
items.lineage: Polish underground rap developed through independent releases, DIY circulation and local club networks, including Warsaw’s experimental scene. Acts such as TONFA connect rap with turntablism, live percussion and cross-genre collaboration.
items.description: Interacting rap voices work against scratched and cut recorded material and an energetic drum-kit pulse. Rhythmic speech, abrupt transitions and contrasting textures create a confrontational live sound within a wider field of independent production.

items.name: Rap Geek
items.lineage: Brazilian internet rap communities developed character-driven songs across anime, comics, games and films, connecting independent channels, producers and specialist labels.
items.description: Character narratives and personal messages meet rhythmic rap delivery over trap and boom-bap production. Rap Geek developed a Brazilian online community around shared fandoms, collaborative channels and specialist labels, with lyrics moving between fictional worlds and everyday experiences. Its repertoire reaches beyond anime to games, comics and cinema.

items.name: Surinamese Hip Hop
items.lineage: Surinamese hip-hop links rap and DJ culture across Suriname and its diaspora. Its contemporary communities draw on multilingual urban music and local rhythmic traditions, with artists and soundsystems connecting hip-hop to kawina, awasa and other dance styles.
items.description: MC voices interact with DJ-led recorded beats and live percussion. Alternating vocal phrases, layered rhythms and changes in recorded texture create a communal dance setting, with traditional rhythmic colors and contemporary hip-hop delivery reinforcing one another.

items.name: Swedish Drill
items.lineage: Swedish drill localizes drill within Sweden’s contemporary rap scene, with artists such as Dizzy linking it to trap and other club-music currents.
items.description: Rhythmic verses and hook-led passages meet forceful beat production and DJ backing. Live performances can bring several voices into call-and-response with audiences. The scene overlaps Swedish hip hop and trap while retaining a specifically identified drill affiliation.

items.name: Kamba Pop
items.lineage: Kamba pop connects vernacular song in eastern Kenya with benga bands, recordings and contemporary dance audiences. Artists such as Ken Wa Maria and Kativui Mweene carry narrative and topical lyrics through a guitar-driven popular tradition that includes both secular and gospel repertoires.
items.description: Lead and supporting singing interlock with bright electric-guitar figures, an active bass line and a steady drum pulse. Repeated refrains and instrumental passages create room for dancing, with contrasting accents and melodic guitar responses keeping the texture in motion.

items.name: Karbi Pop
items.lineage: Karbi pop connects contemporary Karbi-language song, video and performance communities in Assam, including modern treatments of inherited melodies.
items.description: Sung melodies meet amplified guitar, bass and drums, with some fusion groups bringing bamboo flute, reed instruments and Karbi drums into the band. Arak exemplifies this interplay of local instrumental colors and energetic popular-song arrangement.

items.name: Karen Pop
items.lineage: Karen pop connects contemporary popular music with Karen communities in Myanmar and the diaspora. Artists draw on personal experience, migration and multilingual expression while working across pop and related modern styles.
items.description: Melodic singing can sit over a bass-and-drum foundation with synthesizer, piano and string textures. Softer songs favour connected vocal lines and rounded accompaniment, while other releases draw on more forceful electronic or hip-hop production.

items.name: Kumaoni Pop
items.lineage: Kumaoni pop — Kumaon’s regional-language popular songs, bringing local melodies and folk rhythms into contemporary recorded arrangements.
items.description: Kumaoni pop adapts the Kumaoni language and regional song heritage to contemporary listening and dance settings. Folk-derived melodies and hudka rhythms meet guitar, keyboard or piano accompaniment and modern recording production. Artists connect village traditions, family occasions and regional identity with younger audiences and online circulation.

items.name: Ladakhi pop
items.lineage: Ladakhi pop carries Ladakhi-language song into contemporary recordings, media and live performance. Regional song traditions and neighbouring Himalayan influences meet modern popular arrangements, while intimate acoustic performances sustain the connection between melody, poetry and everyday life.
items.description: Expressive singing is supported by guitar in acoustic settings and by fuller arrangements in recorded pop. Love songs and regional identity remain important threads across these approaches.
exemplars: Rigzin Norbu — Lungspo ju ju, firsthand documented acoustic rendition

items.name: Lao Pop
items.lineage: Lao pop brings contemporary popular-song writing into dialogue with Lao musical heritage and regional Asian pop exchange.
items.description: Prominent vocal melodies can combine familiar Lao inflections with modern harmonic accompaniment. Alexandra Bounxouei exemplifies the field; piano and percussion support an intimate concert branch with solo and shared singing.

items.name: Liberian Pop
items.lineage: Liberian pop connects a national popular-music community spanning Afropop, R&B, soul and rap. Artists such as DenG and Stunna participate in recording, performance and DJ networks that circulate music across Liberia and its diaspora.
items.description: Sung hooks, rhythmic vocal phrases and layered electronic accompaniment support accessible songs and dance-oriented grooves. Melodic synthesizers, programmed percussion and low bass coexist with acoustic and band-based approaches.

items.name: Maluku Pop
items.lineage: Maluku pop grew through Moluccan bands, recordings and diaspora networks linking eastern Indonesia with the Netherlands. Indorock, soul, fusion and contemporary dance music meet regional melodies and multilingual songwriting, with artists such as Massada, Daniel Sahuleka and the Moluccan Moods Orchestra contributing different strands.
items.description: Lead and harmony singing ride a guitar, bass and drum foundation, with keyboards, auxiliary percussion and lyrical wind lines adding color. Memorable refrains alternate with instrumental passages and improvisatory responses, drawing regional song traditions into contemporary popular arrangements.

items.name: Mising pop
items.lineage: Mising pop brings the Mising language into modern recorded song across Assam and neighbouring Arunachal Pradesh. The Anu ni:tom repertoire developed alongside older song traditions, with video albums, regional talent platforms and online acoustic productions carrying love songs and new compositions to younger audiences.
items.description: Melodic singing connects Mising lyrical expression with contemporary accompaniment and studio production. Guitar-led acoustic songs form one strand alongside keyboard, percussion and folk-fusion arrangements. Community events and digital platforms link local performers with listeners throughout the region and its diaspora.

items.name: Mizo pop
items.lineage: Mizo pop centres on popular song in the Mizo language, connecting local poetry and melodic expression with the influence of radio, guitar bands and contemporary recording. Love songs form an important strand, while singers move between secular popular music and the region’s strong gospel traditions.
items.description: Melodic singing and guitar accompaniment have a long-established place in Mizo popular music. Intimate acoustic songs coexist with fuller band and electronic productions, carrying themes of affection, everyday life and regional identity through a growing recorded repertoire.

items.name: Oromo Pop
items.lineage: Oromo pop — contemporary Oromo-language popular song combining local vocal expression with electric-band production.
items.description: Oromo pop brings Oromo-language singing and regional song traditions into contemporary popular-band settings. Electric guitar, bass, keyboards and drum kit support lead and group vocals, with repertoire ranging from love songs to wider social expression. In Jimma, ensembles such as Shenen Gibe Band connect local cultural institutions with this modern electric sound.
exemplars: Shenen Gibe Band — documented Jimma Oromo electric popular-band practice, Sheba Sound2015

items.name: Pahadi Pop
items.lineage: Pahadi pop links contemporary popular-song communities across Himalayan regions, including Himachali and Uttarakhand networks.
items.description: Regional vocal melodies meet modern song accompaniment, with acoustic guitar, piano, flute and hand percussion in unplugged arrangements. Shared singing and flowing phrases connect these popular treatments with local song repertoires; Thakur Dass Rathi exemplifies the Himachali branch.

items.name: Palestinian Pop
items.lineage: Palestinian pop encompasses contemporary popular music shaped by Palestinian communities and their wider regional and diasporic connections. Singers and groups bring Arabic song, inherited melodies, dance rhythms, hip-hop and electronic production into a varied popular repertoire.
items.description: Melodic vocals and rhythmic accompaniment span intimate songs, modern band arrangements and electronic dance music. The live-percussion and synthesizer interplay of Shamstep is one prominent branch of this wider field.

items.name: PNG pop
items.lineage: PNG pop is Papua New Guinea’s contemporary popular-song field, joining local melodies and languages with rock, reggae, country-pop, R&B and other international styles.
items.description: Catchy singing and rhythmic accompaniment connect diverse local communities through recordings, radio and live performance. Electric guitar, bass, drums and keyboards support one widely used band setting, while string bands and electronic productions offer other textures. Island-reggae grooves, pop melody and regional musical traditions circulate together without reducing the country’s many styles to a single sound.

items.name: Polish Viral Pop
items.lineage: Polish viral pop developed through online creators, video channels and fan communities that grew into recording and concert networks. Projects such as EKIPA and Genzie connect pop hooks, rap, trap and R&B with personal stories, collective identities and rapidly shared audiovisual releases.
items.description: Sung hooks, rapped passages and overlapping vocal personalities sit above producer-shaped accompaniment. Repeated motifs, direct refrains and contrasts between reflective and party-oriented sections keep the vocal message at the center of a broad contemporary pop sound.

items.name: Pop Flamenco
items.lineage: Pop flamenco brings flamenco-inflected expression into accessible Spanish popular-song writing and production.
items.description: Melodic hooks and expressive lead singing connect ballads and danceable material. Acoustic treatments may use piano or guitar accompaniment; the popular-song emphasis overlaps the wider Nuevo Flamenco fusion movement without defining a fixed compás for every song.

items.name: Pop Urbaine
items.lineage: Pop urbaine is a contested Francophone broadcasting and industry label for crossings between melodic pop and hip-hop.
items.description: Prominent sung hooks, rhythmic vocal phrasing and beat-led accompaniment connect rap, R&B and dance-oriented pop. Artists such as Aya Nakamura and Bramsito illustrate this broad crossover; the label describes musical circulation rather than ethnicity.

items.name: Sambalpuri Pop
items.lineage: Sambalpuri pop connects the western Odisha regional-language recording scene with older broadcast hits and contemporary popular releases.
items.description: Regional vocal melodies can be recast with electric guitar, bass, drums and keyboards. Shared singing and occasional rap expand the contemporary band sound, while repertoire such as Rangabati links new arrangements to the region’s recorded-song heritage.

items.name: Santali Pop
items.lineage: Santali pop — contemporary popular songs in the Santal language, carried by cassette and video production, regional performers and a newer generation of online musicians.
items.description: Santali pop brings Santal-language melodies, romance and community concerns into contemporary popular-song formats. Cassette and video industries helped build regional audiences, while online performers now revisit earlier songs and make new acoustic and electronically produced recordings. Traditional musical memory, neighboring popular styles and youthful experimentation coexist across this varied field.

items.name: Sorani Pop
items.lineage: Sorani pop centres on contemporary song in the Sorani Kurdish language, circulated through recordings, television and concert performance. Traditional melodies and poetry remain influential as singers and composers develop modern arrangements and collaborate across Kurdish and neighbouring musical traditions.
items.description: Melodic singing leads arrangements ranging from compact popular accompaniment to concert ensembles with plucked and bowed strings, santur, hand percussion and piano. Regional vocal expression connects inherited repertoire with contemporary songwriting.
exemplars: Adnan Karim and Hezaravaz Ensemble — complete announced16May2025 concert ensemble

items.name: Thai Indie Pop
items.lineage: Thai indie pop is the melody-centered popular-song branch within Thailand’s independent music communities.
items.description: Soft guitar textures and clear vocal lines meet bass and a steady drum foundation, sometimes opening into more forceful alternative-rock passages. Chiang Mai’s YONLAPA exemplifies this intimate guitar-pop approach.

items.name: Underground Power Pop
items.lineage: Independent power-pop communities linked by small labels, fanzines, mail-order distribution and festivals, including the International Pop Overthrow network.
items.description: Melodic guitar songs combine bright chordal hooks, lead and harmony vocals, electric bass and a firm drum backbeat. Keyboards can add colour to the compact band sound. The underground field connects independent artists and listeners across countries through specialist labels, publications and shared bills, continuing the wider power-pop tradition.

items.name: Zomi pop
items.lineage: Zomi pop carries contemporary song through Zomi-speaking communities and their diaspora. Singers bring local language and identity into popular arrangements, while community concerts and celebrations help circulate the repertoire across generations and national borders.
items.description: Melodic singing is supported by guitar, bass, drums and keyboards in live-band settings. Solo and group vocals share the stage, joining contemporary popular-song arrangements with community expression.
exemplars: Zomi community bands and popular singers

items.name: Việt EDM
items.lineage: Việt EDM connects Vietnam’s electronic dance producers, DJs, training institutions and club audiences.
items.description: Mixed dance programmes and beat-led electronic production span several club styles, including but not limited to Vinahouse. DJ Hoàng Anh and the 88DNA network exemplify the exchange between local production and international dance repertoires.

items.name: Myanmar gospel
items.lineage: Myanmar gospel brings Christian devotional song into Burmese-language worship, recordings and community music-making. Hymns and contemporary praise songs connect congregational expression with recorded vocal and popular-music traditions.
items.description: Sung testimony, praise and religious narrative shape the repertoire. Unaccompanied vocal music forms one strand alongside accompanied gospel and contemporary worship songs.
exemplars: Church of Almighty God — Joy to Be an Honest Person, Myanmar A Cappella edition (2018)

items.name: 8D
items.lineage: 8D audio is an online headphone-listening practice that makes recorded music appear to move around the listener through binaural spatial processing. It circulates across pop, rap, electronic and other repertoires rather than prescribing a particular band or compositional style.
items.description: 8D versions use spatial processing to create a moving, surrounding impression over headphones. A stereo song mix can be treated as a single moving source, while more elaborate productions position separate instruments in virtual space. HRTF filtering and reflected sound help convey external location beyond ordinary left-right volume panning.

items.name: Cantaditas
items.lineage: Cantaditas is a Spanish dance-music repertoire centered on memorable sung hooks and familiar club anthems. Remember parties and festivals carry late-1990s and early-2000s recordings into contemporary DJ culture, linking vocal dance songs across related electronic styles.
items.description: Foreground vocal refrains and repeating dance rhythms give the songs their immediate appeal. DJs connect familiar melodies and energetic recorded arrangements into continuous sets, with repetition and transitions sustaining the shared dance-floor momentum.

items.name: Cantonese Worship
items.lineage: Cantonese worship is the Christian song repertoire of Cantonese-speaking congregations and music ministries, circulated through church songbooks, recordings and worship resources across local and diaspora communities.
items.description: Cantonese devotional texts are carried by singable melodies and chordal support. Piano-led singing offers an intimate setting, while congregational, choral and larger instrumental arrangements extend the repertoire.

items.name: Cartoni Animati
items.lineage: Italian cartoon-theme music developed through television commissions, theme-song singles and collections such as Fivelandia. The songs connect generations of viewers with performers including Cristina D’Avena and Giorgio Vanni, while festival bands reshape familiar melodies through pop, rock and dance arrangements.
items.description: Clear lead singing and supporting voices project recognizable melodies over electric guitar, bass, drums and keyboards. Short instrumental hooks, emphatic refrains and contrasting verse sections favor direct audience participation and an energetic pop-rock sound.

items.name: Chinese BGM
items.lineage: Chinese BGM connects Chinese-language popular repertoire and instrumental cover publishing with background listening. Café, study and relaxation releases circulate across regional boundaries and include both Chinese songs and wider repertoire.
items.description: Piano and guitar melodies, soft harmonic support and unobtrusive arrangements suit extended listening. Repetition, clear phrasing and restrained textural changes help familiar tunes sit comfortably behind everyday activities.

items.name: Chinese Drama OST
items.lineage: Chinese drama OST covers music commissioned and circulated for Chinese television and web serials. Theme songs, ending songs and character-related releases connect screen narratives with the wider Chinese popular-song industry.
items.description: Memorable vocal melodies and expressive chordal accompaniment give drama songs an identity beyond the screen. Piano-led songs offer one arrangement approach; instrumental themes and larger acoustic or electronic settings also belong to the field.

items.name: Classic bhangra
items.lineage: Classic bhangra revisits the Punjabi bands and repertoire that shaped British Asian dance music during the late twentieth century. Groups such as Anjaana and Achanak link Punjabi folk singing and percussion with the development of UK bhangra, alongside the continuing influence of singers such as Kuldeep Manak.
items.description: Strong dhol rhythms support Punjabi singing, with harmonium and hand drums sustaining the folk-band strand of the repertoire. Larger band arrangements and electronic production also belong to its history and later performance life.
exemplars: Anjaana — separately offered four-piece pure Panjabi folk practice

items.name: Cumbia Ecuatoriana
items.lineage: Ecuadorian cumbia adapts the wider Colombian-derived dance tradition through local orchestras, singers and later electronic production. Don Medardo y sus Players is a major reference within this national tropical-music community.
items.description: Voices and melodic horn lines meet electric bass, keyboards and interlocking percussion. Repeated dance patterns support memorable refrains, with live-orchestra textures and synthesized arrangements both contributing to the evolving sound.

items.name: Cumbia Santafesina
items.lineage: Cumbia Santafesina developed through Santa Fe’s dance bands, establishing local guitar-led and accordion-led strands within Argentina’s cumbia history. Los del Bohío and later regional groups helped shape a recognizable provincial scene.
items.description: Sung melodies ride a steady bass foundation and interlocking percussion, with electric guitar or accordion carrying the melodic identity. Timbales, congas and electronic multipads can combine in contemporary live bands.

items.name: Double Drumming
items.lineage: Double drumming is the use of two drummers within one ensemble, spanning experimental rock, psychedelic music, post-rock and metal.
items.description: Simultaneous drum parts can reinforce weight or create interacting rhythmic layers beneath guitars and bass. The Lumberjack Feedback exemplifies a heavy instrumental branch built around low riffs, sustained texture and collective rhythmic development.

items.name: Ethnotronica
items.lineage: Ethnotronica brings electronic production into dialogue with regional acoustic traditions. The term circulates through international performance and DJ networks, including Indian-classical electronic collaborations and cross-cultural dance production.
items.description: Regional melodic instruments and percussion can interact with repeating electronic phrases, processed textures and dance rhythms. An Indian-influenced setting combines bansuri flute, tabla and electronic layers; other collaborations use different cultural sources.

items.name: Festigal
items.lineage: Festigal — Israeli Hanukkah festival songs and theatrical popular-music productions for children and families.
items.description: Festigal brings celebrity singers, children’s performers and theatrical storytelling together in a recurring Israeli Hanukkah production. Its repertoire uses contemporary popular-song arrangements, ensemble singing, keyboards, guitars and rhythm sections. The festival’s commissioned songs and annual themes connect stage spectacle with widely circulated recordings.

items.name: Focus
items.lineage: Focus brings together music selected for concentration, including contemporary piano, ambient textures and instrumental beats. Streaming-era listening collections connect these different musical practices through a shared use during study and other sustained tasks.
items.description: Even dynamics, recurring patterns and uncluttered textures keep the music in the background. A connected solo-piano setting represents the acoustic branch; other focus music uses electronic layers or regular beats.

items.name: Folklore Peruano
items.lineage: Folklore Peruano encompasses Peru’s diverse regional folk-song and dance traditions, including highland and coastal repertoires. Community performance, regional instruments and recorded folk repertoires sustain this broad national field.
items.description: Vocal melody and patterned accompaniment take different forms across regions. Solo singing with a resonant Peruvian harp offers one intimate highland setting; larger instrumental and dance ensembles provide other textures.

items.name: Frafra
items.lineage: Frafra music belongs to the Frafra-speaking communities of northern Ghana, especially the Upper East region. Local song traditions continue through regional performers and contemporary recording networks connecting acoustic practice with amplified popular music.
items.description: Text-forward singing can be accompanied by the struck and tossed calabash rattle called sinyaka, while other settings use kologo and fuller ensembles. Rhythmic vocal phrasing and recurring instrumental patterns give intimate performances a strong forward motion.

items.name: French Movie Tunes
items.lineage: French movie tunes — French-language film songs and localized screen-musical repertoire.
items.description: French movie tunes brings together French-language songs circulated through cinema, soundtrack recordings and concert performance. It includes French versions of international screen musicals as well as local performers’ interpretations. Memorable melodies and expressive singing are central, with arrangements ranging from voice and piano to bands and orchestras.
exemplars: Libérée, délivrée — Noviscore complete Level1 six-page solo-piano edition

items.name: Grupero Romántico
items.lineage: The romantic-song strand of Mexican grupera, developed through electric groups, radio and dance-concert circuits and continued by acts such as Los Acosta and Grupo Libra.
items.description: Sentimental lead melodies and memorable refrains sit over electric guitar, bass, keyboards and percussion. Ballads alternate with rhythmic dance songs; synthesizer colours and electronic drums are part of the electric-group sound. Romantic lyrics and the group-performance circuit link this repertoire across differing tempos and arrangements.

items.name: Gumbé
items.lineage: Gumbé is a diverse Guinea-Bissau popular-music field that draws local traditions into modern band performance and Lusophone musical exchange.
items.description: Lead and supporting voices move over interlocking guitar, bass, drums and percussion, with keyboard harmony adding colour. Rhythmic dance-song arrangements connect the ensemble, while different local influences produce varied grooves and textures.

items.name: Hyperpop Brasileiro
items.lineage: Hyperpop brasileiro connects Brazilian producers, DJs and pop artists through internet circulation, collaborations and events such as the Hyperpop Festival.
items.description: Exaggerated electronic pop textures meet forceful dance rhythms and crossings with Brazilian funk, pagodão and other club styles. CyberKills exemplifies the DJ-led branch, where contrasting songs and sounds are shaped into continuous mixed programmes.

items.name: İlahiler
items.lineage: İlahiler are Turkish devotional songs setting religious and mystical poetry to composed melodies. They belong to mosque and tekke musical traditions as well as contemporary religious recordings, drawing on the makam and rhythmic practices of Turkish music.
items.description: Solo and collective singing carry devotional poetry through melodic phrases and recurring rhythmic patterns. Both unaccompanied and instrumentally supported performances occur, with differing practices across religious settings and recording traditions.
exemplars: Sedat Uçan and Hasan Dursun — complete En Güzel Müziksiz İlahiler (2015)

items.name: Indie Boliviano
items.lineage: Indie Boliviano is Bolivia’s independent music community, connecting bands, labels and creative networks in cities including La Paz, Santa Cruz and Cochabamba. Its releases extend across alternative rock, electronic music and experimental approaches.
items.description: Guitar-led songs may combine melodic vocals, bass and drums with synthesizer colour and programmed layers. Independent production also supports more electronic or exploratory arrangements beyond the band format.

items.name: Indie Català
items.lineage: Indie Català connects independent labels, artists and festivals across Catalonia. Networks such as Bankrobber and popArb bring together pop, rock, folk, electronica and experimental approaches, with Catalan-language songwriting forming an important part of the scene.
items.description: Lead singing interacts with clean electric guitar, bass and drums, while acoustic piano, keyboard and synthesizer layers broaden the harmonic color. Melodic vocal lines and contrasting instrumental textures support clear song structures within a stylistically varied independent field.

items.name: Indie Cristão
items.lineage: Indie Cristão connects Brazilian alternative Christian songwriters through independent recordings, collaborations and church-adjacent music communities. Artists such as Paulo Nazareth, Marcos Almeida and Os Arrais explore faith alongside everyday experience and poetic storytelling.
items.description: Intimate voices and acoustic guitar support melodic, lyrically focused songs. Indie-pop and Brazilian influences also bring fuller band textures, contrasting arrangements and approaches that extend beyond congregational worship.

items.name: Indie Liguria
items.lineage: Indie Liguria links independent music communities in Liguria, including Genoa’s bands, producers and small-label networks. Songwriting, electronic production and cross-cultural collaborations coexist within this regional scene.
items.description: Guitar-led and vocal music share the scene with producer-led tracks built from digital beats, edited fragments and layered textures. A sample-based production setting represents this electronic strand without defining the whole community as dance music.

items.name: Indie Nica
items.lineage: Indie Nica is Nicaragua’s independent music community, including self-managed songwriters, bands and production networks. Artists work across acoustic song, alternative music and other contemporary styles, both locally and in diaspora.
items.description: Personal songwriting and melodic singing can be carried by piano or guitar, while band and electronic settings broaden the sound. Literary expression and spoken poetry also intersect with the scene.

items.name: Japanese Psychedelic
items.lineage: Japanese psychedelic music — experimental rock, electronic exploration and immersive improvisation.
items.description: Japanese psychedelic music spans guitar-driven rock and electronic or improvised exploration. Repetition, timbral transformation and extended textures connect different strands, from distorted bands to synthesizer-led soundscapes. Artists and collectives including C.C.C.C. and Taj Mahal Travellers illustrate its wider experimental network.
exemplars: Fumio Kosakai — Look To The Light (complete21:31 B-side)

items.name: Japanese VGM
items.lineage: Japanese VGM develops through Japan’s game-production studios, composers and music audiences, from constrained early hardware to streamed and orchestral scores. Concerts, recordings and adaptations carry game themes into listening cultures beyond play.
items.description: Recurring themes, looping patterns and changing instrumental layers connect melody with game worlds and action. Synthesized timbres, piano and orchestral colors span intimate cues, energetic sequences and dramatic scores, with arrangements adapting to both hardware and narrative needs.

items.name: Kabyle Moderne
items.lineage: Kabyle Moderne connects contemporary Kabyle songwriting with international popular styles, including rock, reggae, blues and folk. Artists such as Akli D. and Iness Mezel extend inherited song traditions through new arrangements and transnational performance networks.
items.description: Voices and guitar-led songs meet bass, keyboards, drums and hand percussion. Melodic phrasing, rhythmic contrast and layered accompaniment create a flexible sound that retains Kabyle expression while drawing on varied musical influences.

items.name: Korean Soundtrack
items.lineage: Korean soundtrack music brings original songs and dramatic scores together across film and television production. Composers, singers and studio musicians shape themes that connect characters, settings and emotion, with recordings and arrangements extending their life beyond the screen.
items.description: Expressive vocal melodies, piano, guitar and string textures support themes and transitions. Electronic production and acoustic performance coexist, ranging from intimate song settings to expansive dramatic writing.

items.name: Korean Talent Show
items.lineage: Korean talent-show music grows through televised singing competitions and the careers, collaborations and audiences they foster. Programmes such as Phantom Singer connect classical singers, musical-theatre performers and popular vocalists, creating a substantial vocal-crossover concert repertoire.
items.description: Solo singing, vocal ensembles and collaborative arrangements span art song, arias, musicals and popular song. Piano-supported recitals and larger concert productions extend the music beyond the original broadcasts.
exemplars: David DQ Lee / Haewon Lee / James Jaewon Moon — whole ACC25September2024 AveMaria recital

items.name: Lagu Iban
items.lineage: Lagu Iban encompasses Iban-language songs and recording communities in Sarawak and their wider circulation. Artists such as Masterpiece connect local language and identity with contemporary rock, pop and other popular forms.
items.description: Sung melodies and recurring refrains meet guitar, keyboards, bass and drums. Contrasting lead and backing voices, instrumental responses and changing band textures support songs about relationships, experience and community.

items.name: Lagu Jambi
items.lineage: Lagu Jambi gathers the regional songs and melodies of Jambi, including inherited repertoire and contemporary adaptations. Songs such as Angso Duo, Batanghari and Ketimun Bungkuk connect local memory and identity with continuing performance and publishing.
items.description: Sung phrases and memorable melodic contours carry local texts through traditional and modern accompaniment. Acoustic guitar and bass can support contemporary renditions, alongside percussion and other regional instrumental practices.

items.name: Lagu Maluku
items.lineage: Lagu Maluku encompasses the regional song repertoire of the Maluku islands, sustained through communal singing, recordings and instrumental adaptations. Familiar songs such as Buka Pintu, Sarinande and Rasa Sayange circulate across generations and beyond the region.
items.description: Clear vocal melodies and shared refrains interact with strummed accompaniment. Ukulele is prominent in Ambon’s musical life, alongside guitar, local percussion, wind ensembles and diverse contemporary band settings.

items.name: Lagu Tarling
items.lineage: Lagu Tarling belongs to the song traditions of Cirebon and Indramayu on Java’s north coast. Earlier guitar-and-flute music developed into varied popular-song and dramatic forms, with modern branches incorporating dangdut influences and electronic keyboards.
items.description: Singing carries the regional repertoire over melodic accompaniment and repeating percussion patterns. Guitar and flute remain part of its historical sound; modern organ-tunggal performances use an arranger keyboard to combine those timbres with bass, chords and rhythmic backing.
exemplars: Modern Indramayu Organ Tunggal Tarling — documented singer/arranger-keyboard practice, Rasriy and Wahyudin 2023

items.name: Lo-Fi Brasileiro
items.lineage: Lo-fi brasileiro connects Brazil’s independent beat producers, labels and online listening communities. Lo-Fi Brasil and Tangerina Music support varied approaches linking lo-fi hip-hop, chillhop, ambient texture and local musical experience.
items.description: Relaxed sampled rhythms, repeating phrases and intimate instrumental recordings shape a broad beat-making field. Acoustic guitar can bring a direct melodic and harmonic layer, while deliberately rougher sample textures give the production a handmade character.

items.name: Louvores Pentecostais
items.lineage: Louvores Pentecostais is the Brazilian Pentecostal praise repertoire developed through churches, devotional recordings and gospel ministries. It forms a recognizable strand within the wider Brazilian gospel field.
items.description: Expressive melodic singing carries praise, testimony and biblical themes over chordal accompaniment. Voices may alternate or join together, with arrangements ranging from intimate piano-led singing to fuller gospel bands.

items.name: Magyar Kabaré
items.lineage: Hungarian cabaret and comic performance, connecting theatre sketches, radio comedy, satirical song and later stand-up through a shared Hungarian-language repertoire.
items.description: Wordplay, comic timing, impersonation and social observation shape spoken sketches and monologues. Musical numbers and ensemble scenes also belong to the wider cabaret tradition, while the solo spoken strand places delivery and the performer’s relationship with the audience in the foreground.

items.name: Mapouka
items.lineage: Mapouka — Ivorian coastal dance and its lively youssoumba vocal-percussion accompaniment.
items.description: Mapouka is an Ivorian coastal dance associated with lively youssoumba accompaniment. Lead singing, harmonized responses, drumming and rhythmic bottle playing support its energetic movement; some performers also add spoken toasting. Groups such as Aboutou Roots and Nigui Saff K-Dance helped bring village-rooted practice to commercial recordings and wider stages.

items.name: Mérida Indie
items.lineage: Mérida indie is the independent-music community of Mérida, Yucatán, built through local bands, DIY production, labels and regional festivals. Its varied approaches connect alternative rock, melodic pop and electronic textures within a shared local network.
items.description: Layered singing and clean electric-guitar figures meet a firm bass-and-drum foundation, with keyboards and synthesizers adding harmonic colour. Clear melodic hooks, contrasting textures and dynamic changes connect intimate songwriting with energetic ensemble playing.

items.name: Middle Eastern Traditional
items.lineage: Middle Eastern traditional music encompasses interconnected Arab, Turkish, Persian, Armenian and neighboring regional repertoires, from modal instrumental improvisation to vocal art music and communal songs.
items.description: Modal melodies, ornamented phrases and exchanges between composed repertoire and improvisation connect many of these traditions, while their tuning systems, rhythms and forms remain regionally distinct. Oud, bowed strings, qanun, nay and percussion appear in varied ensembles; instrumental solos and singing provide contrasting settings. The Iraqi oud tradition offers one intimate expression of this wider musical world.
exemplars: William & Mary Middle Eastern Music Ensemble

items.name: Moorish Traditional
items.lineage: Moorish traditional music carries the azawan heritage of Mauritania’s hereditary iggawin musicians. Its codified modal practice encompasses praise, love songs and dance, with contemporary performances also incorporating electric instruments.
items.description: Voices interact with the rippling strings of the ardin and the plucked tidinit, supported by tbal drumming. Electric guitar can extend the melodic accompaniment. Modal development and exchanges between singing and instruments shape a varied professional repertoire.
exemplars: Dimi Mint Abba and Khalifa Ould Eide — Moorish Music from Mauritania (1990)

items.name: Música Aguascalentense
items.lineage: Música Aguascalentense brings together the regional music communities of Aguascalientes, from northern and tropical dance styles to independent rock and hybrid ensembles. Local festivals and musicians such as La Santísima Voladora connect regional identity with wider Mexican popular music.
items.description: Driving guitar and bass, drums, percussion, brass responses and keyboards meet expressive singing in the region’s rock–tropical fusion. Other branches draw on mariachi, norteño and cumbia traditions.

items.name: Música Bautista
items.lineage: Música Bautista encompasses Spanish-language Baptist hymnody, congregational singing and devotional recordings. Shared hymnals, church ministries, choirs and small vocal groups connect local congregations across Latin America and the diaspora.
items.description: Clear melodies and collective singing carry devotional texts, often supported by piano, organ or strummed instruments. Unaccompanied harmony, solo testimony and fuller worship arrangements coexist within the tradition.

items.name: Música Coahuilense
items.lineage: Música Coahuilense connects regional repertoires and popular-music communities across Coahuila. Northern dance traditions, tropical bands and contemporary ensembles circulate through local celebrations, recording networks and migration.
items.description: Singing, rhythmic bass and drums meet guitar, keyboards and melodic wind responses in tropical dance settings. Cumbia grooves and northern regional styles offer contrasting approaches within this wider musical landscape.

items.name: Música Evangélica Instrumental
items.lineage: Música evangélica instrumental connects Brazil’s evangelical instrumental performers, recordings and listening communities. Hymns and contemporary worship melodies are reinterpreted through solo playing, intimate ensembles and fuller popular arrangements.
items.description: Instrumental melody carries devotional repertoire through phrasing, dynamic contrast and familiar song forms. Saxophone and guitar offer one intimate approach; piano, strings and electric-band arrangements broaden a field that remains centered on instrumental interpretation.

items.name: Música michoacana
items.lineage: Música michoacana encompasses the musical communities of Michoacán, including Purépecha song, arpa-grande and valona traditions, and regional brass bands. State archives and local performers preserve a broad repertoire across the state’s regions and generations.
items.description: Guitar-accompanied singing forms one intimate strand of this regional music. Interlocking voices and plucked chordal accompaniment carry lyrical songs, alongside the larger harp ensembles, choirs and wind bands heard elsewhere in the field.
exemplars: Dueto Sïrankua — complete two-person practice documented by Secretaría de Cultura de Michoacán (2026)

items.name: Música Nayarita
items.lineage: Música nayarita connects Nayarit’s musical communities with migrant fairs and audiences abroad.
items.description: Brass bandas and electrified dance groups share this regional circuit. In the electronic dance-band branch, voices, guitar, bass, keyboards and drums build repeating melodic figures and lively rhythmic support; Hechizeros Band exemplifies this approach.

items.name: Música Otavaleña
items.lineage: Música otavaleña connects the musical traditions of Otavalo and surrounding Imbabura with community performance, recording and contemporary reinterpretation. Local Indigenous and mestizo repertoires circulate through celebrations, ensembles and projects that combine traditional material with electronic production.
items.description: Singing, plucked strings, bowed instruments and winds appear in varied local ensembles. Repeated dance figures and familiar melodies link social gatherings with recorded song. Contemporary projects can rework festival recordings and rhythmic fragments alongside live instrumental parts, keeping older repertoire in conversation with new listening and dancing contexts.

items.name: Música Timor-Leste
items.lineage: Timor-Leste popular music — multilingual songs shaped by local repertoire, Lusophone exchange and electric-band dance music.
items.description: Timor-Leste’s popular music connects Tetun and other local song traditions with Portuguese, Indonesian and international pop influences. Guitar-led bands, keyboards, bass and drums have supported social dancing and public song since the late colonial period. Music also carries memories of displacement and national identity, alongside everyday entertainment.

items.name: Música tlaxcalteca
items.lineage: Música tlaxcalteca connects Tlaxcala’s local carnival traditions, bands, orchestras and popular singers. Contemporary groups such as La Murga Xicohtl bring regional and Indigenous-language expression into amplified songs and brass-led ensemble music.
items.description: Voices and electric guitars meet bass, drums and lively horn lines in a contemporary band strand. Carnival influences, recurring refrains and contrasts between singing and brass figures link local performance traditions with rock, reggae and popular song.
exemplars: La Murga Xicohtl — Tlapaxanketl / Viajero, full credited song (2023 official songbook)

items.name: Música Triste Brasileira
items.lineage: Música triste brasileira links Brazilian internet-era sad-pop and rap audiences through vulnerable songwriting and collaborative digital circulation.
items.description: Melancholic lead vocals sit over acoustic guitar and keyboard support in the pop-oriented branch. Connected phrases and reflective lyrics foreground personal emotion; Hiosaki exemplifies this strand without defining all Brazilian melancholy as one style.

items.name: Música Urbana Oaxaqueña
items.lineage: Música Urbana Oaxaqueña develops through Oaxaca’s rap and urban-music communities, including Spanish-language and Indigenous-language expression. Groups such as Juchirap connect local experience, language and cultural memory with contemporary hip-hop performance.
items.description: Rhythmic vocal delivery, recurring hooks and beat-driven accompaniment support storytelling, social commentary and collective identity. DJs, electronic production and regional musical references provide varied settings for individual and group voices.

items.name: Musique traditionnelle congolaise
items.lineage: Congolese traditional music encompasses the country’s diverse regional and cultural repertoires, from lamellophone-accompanied song to choral, ritual and dance traditions. Contemporary ensembles also reinterpret inherited material with amplified instruments.
items.description: Voices and interlocking instrumental patterns shape varied local practices. In an intimate song strand, a singer accompanies personal verses on the lukembi, alternating vocal phrases with resonant plucked-metal-key figures; larger ensembles and communal vocal traditions supply other textures.
exemplars: Abdul Aziz — complete Lukembi and Voice, SFW40401 track12

items.name: Nasheed
items.lineage: Nasheed is a broad Islamic devotional-song tradition and contemporary recording field. Sung poetry, praise and religious reflection circulate through community performance and international media, with both voices-only and instrumentally accompanied approaches.
items.description: Melodic declamation, repeated invocations and responsive phrases place devotional words at the center. Solo and group voices may stand alone, move with frame-drum pulses or join more elaborate contemporary arrangements.

items.name: New Hampshire indie
items.lineage: New Hampshire indie connects independent artists, venues and festivals across the state, including communities around Peterborough and Keene. Acoustic songwriting, indie rock and pop-punk coexist within these local networks.
items.description: An intimate acoustic strand pairs melodic singing with ringing guitar lines and chordal accompaniment. Other bands add amplified rhythm sections and denser textures, while local collaborations and independent recordings connect the varied song styles.
exemplars: Footings — complete Passerine with Timothy Horgan,2014four-song edition

items.name: Norrbotten indie
items.lineage: Norrbotten indie connects independent musicians and regional production networks in northern Sweden. Personal songwriting, folk-informed melody and contemporary pop and rock textures intersect within a community rooted in the region and its wider creative exchanges.
items.description: An exposed sung narrative meets clear acoustic-guitar lines, a steady drum foundation and synthesizer colour. Intimate phrasing and concise melodic gestures remain central as electronic textures and rhythmic energy widen the arrangement.

items.name: NY Roots
items.lineage: NY roots connects New York folk, roots-rock and songwriter communities through local venues, festivals and regional broadcasting.
items.description: Narrative singing and acoustic guitar anchor a solo branch, while the wider network includes varied roots ensembles. Sawyer Fredericks exemplifies the voice-and-guitar approach alongside broader community figures such as Donna the Buffalo and the Mammals.

items.name: Old School Nederhop
items.lineage: Old School Nederhop connects the pioneers of Dutch-language hip-hop with an enduring community of MCs, DJs and listeners. Acts such as Extince and Osdorp Posse helped establish local language, storytelling and identity within hip-hop’s international circulation.
items.description: Direct rhythmic delivery, sampled beats, turntable cuts and recurring hooks shape a sound centered on flow and wordplay. Live MC-and-DJ exchange and boom-bap production remain important reference points.

items.name: Oldschool Deutschrap
items.lineage: Oldschool Deutschrap gathers the foundational generations of German-language hip hop, from the 1990s scenes of Heidelberg, Stuttgart, Hamburg and Munich to early-2000s street rap. Advanced Chemistry, Die Fantastischen Vier, Freundeskreis, Absolute Beginner and Fettes Brot helped shape its varied approaches to language, identity and everyday life.
items.description: Rhythmic verses, boom-bap grooves, sampled phrases and DJ scratching characterize much of the repertoire. Humour, social commentary and street narratives coexist across regional scenes and remain influential in later German rap.
exemplars: Fettes Brot — Echo (Acapella), separately issued2013 full vocal edition

items.name: Otacore
items.lineage: Otacore connects fan-made songs and remixes inspired by games, cartoons and other screen worlds. Newgrounds, YouTube and related fandom networks helped artists circulate character narratives and original pop songs across national and stylistic boundaries.
items.description: Character-led singing meets keyboard melodies, synthesized bass and bright electronic figures, with arranged samples and vocoded color expanding the texture. Direct hooks and contrasting song sections support theatrical or emotionally expressive storytelling across a varied fan-music field.

items.name: Pinoy Praise
items.lineage: Pinoy praise encompasses Philippine Christian praise repertoires and performance communities across languages and denominations. Tagalog and English songs circulate through Catholic and evangelical ministries, choirs and popular recordings.
items.description: Soloists and groups sing devotional melodies and memorable refrains. Unaccompanied choral settings place the voices in the foreground, while piano-led and contemporary band arrangements support other worship and concert settings.
exemplars: Woodrose Chorale — Lead Me Lord, complete remote a cappella rendition2020

items.name: Polish Alternative
items.lineage: Polish alternative music brings independent and experimental approaches into popular song, crossing guitar rock, alternative pop and electronic production. Its varied artists connect melodic songwriting with exploratory textures and arrangements.
items.description: Singing, electric guitars, bass and drums form one band-oriented foundation, with synthesizers adding harmonic or textural colour. Some arrangements expand into organs, electric piano, processed voices and horns, while others foreground electronic production and sparse pop structures.

items.name: Polish Indie
items.lineage: Polish indie is a cross-style independent music network connecting artists, labels and audiences across Poland. Guitar-based rock, electronics, improvisation and folk-informed work share independent production and circulation rather than a single fixed sound.
items.description: In its instrumental alternative-rock strand, clean guitar patterns, electric bass and drums combine with synthesizer colour. Interlocking rhythmic figures and changes in texture build momentum, with a direct ensemble sound emphasizing detail and contrast.

items.name: Portuguese Indie
items.lineage: Portugal’s independent-music networks connect local songwriting, self-directed production, labels and live venues across rock, pop, electronic music and other styles.
items.description: Guitar-led songs, melodic singing and a bass-and-drum rhythm section form an established strand, often expanded by keyboards and electronic textures. Independent production and circulation connect these varied approaches, alongside continuing exchanges with the wider Portuguese popular-music field.

items.name: Prank
items.lineage: Recorded prank-call comedy, developed through character voices, improvised exchanges and edited telephone conversations.
items.description: A caller’s comic persona interacts with another speaker, building a situation through timing, repetition, misunderstanding and changing reactions. Alternating spoken voices carry the form, with recording and editing shaping the listener’s access to the exchange.

items.name: Psybass
items.lineage: Psybass joins psychedelic music communities with contemporary bass-music production and festival DJ practice.
items.description: Bass weight, transformed textures and broken-beat motion cross dubstep, trap and other bass styles. Mixed programmes can overlap psydub and glitch-hop without requiring a single reggae-derived rhythm; Shanti Planti exemplifies this exploratory community.

items.name: Puerto Rican indie
items.lineage: Puerto Rico’s independently organized recording and live-music communities connect alternative rock, pop, experimental music and locally rooted styles.
items.description: A guitar-band strand combines sung melodies with electric guitar, bass and drums, ranging from concise pop structures to rougher and more exploratory textures. Independent releases and shared venues link this strand with a wider island scene that also includes electronic, rap and Afro-Caribbean approaches.

items.name: Québec indie
items.lineage: Québec indie encompasses independent music across the province’s anglophone, francophone and bilingual communities. Bands and songwriters connect local scenes with wider indie-rock, pop and electronic networks, spanning guitar-centred groups and studio-led projects.
items.description: Melodic vocals, guitars, bass, drums and keyboards support a broad range of intimate pop and alternative-rock arrangements. Artists such as Men I Trust, Wolf Parade, Plants and Animals and Land of Talk illustrate the field’s varied approaches to songwriting and texture.
exemplars: Men I Trust — complete Tiny Desk Home concert (2021)

items.name: Raspe
items.lineage: Raspe is a Honduran dance-music current rooted in the north-coast scene. Producers and singers combine electronic melody with dancehall-derived percussion, developing a local name and community through songs, parties and online circulation.
items.description: Electronic melodic hooks, low-frequency support and syncopated percussion frame rhythmic singing. Repeated phrases and changes in instrumental density give the tracks their dance focus, with influences from reggae, dancehall and contemporary electronic production.

items.name: Ringtone
items.lineage: Ringtone music — short recognizable musical signals for telephone call alerts.
items.description: Ringtone music uses concise, recognizable motifs to identify incoming calls. Its sound ranges from synthesized tones and compact melodies to recorded instrumental or vocal excerpts. Composers also write self-contained alert pieces that circulate as phone audio and playable arrangements.

items.name: Ritmo Kombina
items.lineage: Ritmo Kombiná developed in Curaçao in the early 1990s through Gibi Doran and collaborating dance-band musicians. It brings together rhythmic influences from soca and merengue with the bass and keyboard language of cadence and zouk.
items.description: Singing rides over interlocking conga and drum-kit patterns, with bass and keyboards shaping the harmonic groove. Repeating figures, rhythmic accents and changes in arrangement keep the music directed toward dancing. Brass and timbales can expand the band sound, while local radio and diaspora audiences sustain the repertoire.

items.name: Rumba (Spanish popular song)
items.lineage: Spanish popular rumba developed through intersecting Romani, Catalan and urban musical communities, drawing on Afro-Cuban rhythmic exchange and flamenco-related guitar practice. Peret, Los Chichos and the Gipsy Kings helped carry its danceable songs into wider popular circulation.
items.description: Propulsive strummed guitar, expressive singing and recurring refrains drive the music. Hand percussion, bass and contemporary band arrangements can extend its rhythmic foundation, while guitar flourishes and vocal responses maintain a communal, celebratory character.

items.name: Russian CCM
items.lineage: Russian contemporary Christian music connects Russian-language churches, ministry networks and diasporic communities through devotional popular song. Recorded worship and family ensembles circulate across Russia, other post-Soviet countries and communities abroad.
items.description: Melodic singing conveys prayer, praise and testimony through contemporary song forms. Piano-supported performances coexist with band arrangements and congregational singing, linking intimate devotion with collective worship.
exemplars: Note-Store — complete Sharikov Family Band Держи меня Piano.Easy PEA0339990

items.name: Russian Indie
items.lineage: Russian indie develops through independent bands, labels and performance networks, encompassing guitar music, electronic pop and other self-directed approaches. Local scenes and international exchange have shaped diverse Russian-language and instrumental repertoires.
items.description: Melodic vocals, interlocking guitars, bass and drums often support compact songs and contrasting textures. Synthesizers and electronic production open additional directions, ranging from restrained intimacy to forceful rhythmic interplay.

items.name: Russian Plugg
items.lineage: Russian plugg — a Russian-language branch of the airy, minimalist trap sound developed through online producer and rapper networks.
items.description: Russian plugg combines Russian-language rap with soft electronic melodies, spacious harmonic layers and sparse 808-based rhythm. Its understated production developed within online rap networks, sharing roots with Atlanta plugg while acquiring a local vocabulary and audience. Early releases by Big Baby Tape helped bring this relaxed alternative to heavier trap into the Russian scene.

items.name: Russian rave
items.lineage: Russian rave is a Russian-language electronic scene connecting hard dance energy with pop melodies, rap-inflected delivery and youth-club culture. Artists such as GSPD, DEAD BLONDE and Lida span harder rave tracks and melodic synth-pop, bringing the music into both club and concert settings.
items.description: Driving electronic rhythms and prominent vocals lead exuberant dance performances. DJ accompaniment, synthesized production and catchy refrains connect live shows with the scene’s recorded sound.
exemplars: GSPD with Arina Bulanova/Dead Blonde — representative compact vocal/DJ concert practice

items.name: Sound
items.lineage: Sound-centered listening brings environmental recordings, sustained noise and everyday sonic textures into deliberately chosen listening environments. Household appliances, weather and other continuous sources circulate as recordings whose interest lies in texture and duration rather than conventional songs.
items.description: Steady broadband textures, slowly changing layers and gradual fades can create a continuous auditory background. Pitch, pulse and human voices are optional rather than defining elements, and recordings vary widely in source and spectral character.

items.name: Spa
items.lineage: Instrumental music composed or selected for spa reception areas, treatment rooms and relaxation spaces, drawing on ambient, piano and other quiet listening traditions.
items.description: Slow melodic movement, soft dynamics and spacious phrasing maintain a low-intensity listening environment. Sparse piano is one established approach; sustained electronic and acoustic textures offer other possibilities. Programming often follows the character and duration of different spaces and treatments.

items.name: Spanish new wave
items.lineage: Spanish new wave emerged around the transition from the 1970s to the 1980s, connecting punk, pop and electronic influences with new independent scenes and La Movida. Alaska y Los Pegamoides and other formative groups helped establish a style later renewed by bands such as Juanita y Los Feos.
items.description: Direct melodic songs, brisk rhythms, electric guitars, bass, drums and keyboard colours link punk energy with pop hooks. Synth-driven and guitar-led approaches coexist across the field.
exemplars: Juanita y Los Feos — Nueva Numancia (2014), complete12 songs

items.name: Taiwan Graduation Song
items.lineage: Taiwan graduation songs form a student-created school-leaving repertoire, renewed through university projects and interschool collaborations.
items.description: Shared singing carries farewell, memory and anticipation in contemporary Mandarin popular-song forms. Piano accompaniment supports an accessible group-song rendition; annual student writing and performance distinguish this practice within Taiwan’s broader pop field.

items.name: Talent Show
items.lineage: Talent-show music connects the performers, repertoire and audiences formed through televised singing competitions. International formats such as Idol, The X Factor and Got Talent have launched recording careers and sustained concert, broadcast and fan communities across countries.
items.description: Singers interpret familiar songs and introduce original material through solo performances, collaborations and ensembles. Piano-supported songs form an intimate strand alongside band, orchestral and electronically produced arrangements.
exemplars: Musicnotes — complete Piece by Piece [2016 American Idol Performance] instrumental solo MN0163712

items.name: Talentkonkurrence
items.lineage: Talentkonkurrence connects Danish popular repertoire with televised talent competitions, including youth MGP songwriting and performance.
items.description: Clear lead singing and memorable melodic hooks foreground the performer. Voice-and-piano arrangements make competition songs accessible for participatory singing and teaching; Emma Pi exemplifies the Danish youth-pop branch.

items.name: Talentos Brasileiros
items.lineage: Brazilian television singing competitions connect regional performers with national audiences, broadcast bands and commercial recordings. Programmes such as The Voice Brasil draw on Brazilian song, pop, rock and international repertoire, emphasizing vocal interpretation and the transition from televised performances to concert careers.
items.description: Prominent singing leads a flexible pop-band accompaniment of guitar, bass, drums and keyboards. Clear harmonic support and responsive instrumental accents leave room for phrasing, sustained notes, dynamic contrasts and memorable refrains.

items.name: Telugu indie
items.lineage: Telugu indie connects independent Telugu artists through self-authored releases, online circulation, collaboration and local live venues.
items.description: Song-led bands combine shared vocals with guitar, bass, drums and keyboards, while the wider community also embraces rap and other styles. ChowRaasta exemplifies a folk- and reggae-inflected amplified branch alongside independent songwriters and MCs.

items.name: Telugu remix
items.lineage: Telugu remix connects DJs, producers and audiences through remixed Telugu film songs, popular hits and folk repertoire.
items.description: Recognizable vocal and melodic material is recast for dance-floor mixing and mashups. DJ programmes can move between Telugu selections and neighboring repertoires, emphasizing transitions, rhythmic continuity and crowd response.

items.name: Vintage Hollywood
items.lineage: Vintage Hollywood centres on songs and performers associated with the studio-era screen musical, with strong links to stage repertoire and popular standards. Film performances helped circulate these songs beyond their original productions.
items.description: Expressive melodic singing and clearly shaped phrases carry memorable tunes over tonal accompaniment. A voice-and-piano setting brings the song forward; dance-band and orchestral arrangements offer larger screen-musical textures.

items.name: Violão Clássico
items.lineage: Brazilian concert-guitar practice connecting conservatory training, solo recitals and chamber performance with an international classical repertoire.
items.description: Nylon-string guitar combines melody, bass and inner voices through fingerstyle articulation. Scales, arpeggios, chordal textures and contrasting tone colours support works and transcriptions from different periods. Brazilian performers and composers participate in a wider international concert and teaching tradition.

items.name: Volkstümliche Musik
items.lineage: Volkstümliche Musik is a popular entertainment field drawing on folk-song models, regional imagery, marches and Schlager. Radio, television, film and touring performers helped develop its familiar melodies and public sing-along repertoire during the twentieth century.
items.description: Clear vocal melodies, regular dance rhythms and approachable harmonies support songs of home, affection and sociability. Acoustic instruments and modern accompaniment coexist, with fluid connections to Alpine folk music and German-language Schlager.
exemplars: Gerhard Hildner — complete Musikantentreff130-title songbook MVH1000414

items.name: German Dark Minimal Techno
items.lineage: German dark minimal techno developed through a 2010s independent-label network including Klangrecords, Darker Sounds, Subwoofer and Toxic Recordings, linking hard-minimal producers such as Timao with the darker industrial sound of Klangtronik.
items.description: Heavy bass, stark repeating figures and abrasive electronic textures drive club-focused DJ sets and productions. Restrained motifs and sustained rhythmic pressure connect the style to minimal techno, while rougher textures and weightier impacts connect it to hard and industrial techno.

items.name: Malaysian Tamil Rap
items.lineage: Malaysian Tamil rap grew through local recording crews and producers such as Yogi B and Natchatra, connecting Malaysia’s multilingual hip-hop scene with Tamil-speaking audiences abroad.
items.description: Tamil verses and rhythmic flows ride produced hip-hop accompaniment, ranging from personal and social commentary to celebratory tracks. Malaysian crews, producers and platforms such as Rap Porkalam sustain a local scene with strong links to the wider Tamil diaspora. Sung hooks, beatboxing and live-band collaborations also occur within this varied practice.

items.name: Cloud Rap Français
items.lineage: French cloud rap developed through atmospheric rap production and overlapping artist-producer circles in the 2010s, with TripleGo and PNL among its prominent reference points.
items.description: Spacious electronic backgrounds, subdued rhythmic delivery and introspective or escapist moods distinguish this branch of French rap. Rapped verses can alternate with sung passages and instrumental stretches. The production emphasizes atmosphere, connecting French voices and local collaborations with the wider international cloud-rap aesthetic.

items.name: Indian Underground Rap
items.lineage: Indian underground rap developed through local crews, street cyphers, independent releases and online exchanges across cities and languages. Projects such as Hip Hop Homeland brought Mumbai, Kashmir, Punjab, Kolkata, Shillong and other communities into a shared public conversation, while neighborhood identity and everyday experience remained central.
items.description: Rhythmic, text-forward verses work over producer-built beats or circulate through freestyle and battle settings. Local-language phrasing, code-switching, personal testimony and social criticism connect performers to their communities. Beat production ranges across boom-bap, trap and other hip-hop approaches rather than following one compulsory national rhythm.

items.name: Turkmen Hip Hop
items.lineage: Turkmen hip-hop developed through circulated recordings, studio work and internet communities, linking local MCs with musicians living abroad. Rappers combine personal and social themes with pop-facing material.
items.description: Rhythmic verses over produced accompaniment form a core of Turkmen rap, alongside melodic pop-rap and online battle practice. Local language, everyday experience and emerging independent networks shape a scene connected to wider international hip-hop.

items.name: Bouzouki
items.lineage: Bouzouki repertoire connects Greek instrumental performance, dance music and song adaptation with generations of players, composers and teachers. Recordings and published instrumental collections carry this practice beyond its rebetiko and laïkó roots into concert and international settings.
items.description: Bright picked melodies, ringing paired strings and ornamented phrases lead the music. Free introductory taximia coexist with shaped dance tunes and instrumental versions of songs. Solo playing, small ensembles and larger arrangements provide different settings for the bouzouki’s melodic voice.

items.name: Drill Chileno
items.lineage: Chilean drill developed within the country’s rap and urban-music networks as artists adapted an international hip-hop style to local voices and stories. Musicians move between drill, trap and other approaches, with independent beatmakers and online releases connecting the scene.
items.description: Rapped phrases work against producer-built drill beats, giving rhythm, delivery and personal narrative a central role. Chilean vocabulary and local experience shape the verses, while collaborative studio production links performers to a wider urban scene.

items.name: Indonesian Emo Rap
items.lineage: Indonesian emo rap joins the country’s hip-hop communities with the emotional themes and expressive textures of emo. Independent rappers and producers use personal recollection, alienation and regret alongside social criticism, with artists such as Anjar OX’S and Walkingpasttheex representing different approaches.
items.description: Confessional verses and melodic passages meet producer-shaped hip-hop and trap accompaniment. The emphasis falls on emotional directness and atmosphere, while performers move between rapped and sung delivery and draw on rock-related or electronic textures.

items.name: Medimeisterschaften
items.lineage: Medimeisterschaften music grew from the themed songs and fan culture of European medical-student gatherings. University teams write, produce and perform their own annual tracks, tying local identity and playful slogans to costumes, videos and collective festival participation.
items.description: Catchy sung lines, rhythmic slogans and produced beats carry university-specific wordplay and shared refrains. Student teams build melody, harmony and rhythm together, record and edit vocals, and bring the songs from bedroom studios to festival stages. Styles vary with each year’s theme and contributors.

items.name: Tamaulipas Rap
items.lineage: Tamaulipas rap connects local MCs, independent crews, beatmakers and event networks across the northeastern Mexican state. Regional interviews document both shared scene-building and disagreement over its direction, while artists carry local experiences into wider Mexican rap circuits.
items.description: Text-forward rhythmic verses ride producer-built beats. Personal experience, regional identity, protest and everyday life supply varied lyrical material, with independent recording and live events sustaining the community. Production approaches differ across artists rather than following a single compulsory regional instrument set.

items.name: North Moroccan Rap
items.lineage: Northern Moroccan rap links Tangier, Tetouan and surrounding communities through local MC networks and cross-border collaborations. Muslim’s Tangier work is an important reference, while younger and diasporic artists extend the region’s connections to the wider Moroccan scene.
items.description: Rhythmic verses and producer-built beats carry local experience, personal testimony and social commentary. Darija delivery and flexible language use connect neighborhood expression with wider audiences, while the production remains open to different hip-hop approaches.

items.name: Indie campechano
items.lineage: Campeche’s independent music scene grew through local bands, self-organized concerts and regional recording networks. MOROCA connected underground rock musicians in the 2000s; La Caverna and Indie Fest Campeche later linked this history with new pop, alternative and electronic projects. Studios and community radio supported releases, while Ciudad del Carmen developed its own artist-organized concert activity.
items.description: Guitar-led songs, bass lines, drum-kit grooves and sung melodies form a common band foundation, with keyboards adding harmonic layers and electronic colors. The scene encompasses melodic pop, danceable funk and synth textures as well as heavier rock and metal. Independent production and regional collaboration connect these varied sounds.

items.name: Malawian hip hop
items.lineage: Malawian hip hop developed through local rappers, independent producers, labels and collaborations linking urban communities with wider African audiences. Artists such as Biriwiri, Dizzo and Macelba helped establish vernacular rap and studio-made beats alongside English-language and cross-border work. Chichewa expression, local experience and connections with older popular traditions remain important parts of the scene.
items.description: Rhythmic verses sit over producer-built beats, with memorable sung hooks and switches between rapping and singing in some branches. Lyrics move between everyday experience, personal confidence and social reflection. Production varies by artist and producer, from direct hip-hop grooves to arrangements incorporating local melodic and rhythmic references.

items.name: OC rap
items.lineage: Orange County rap developed through local MCs, home studios, independent releases and collaborations across Santa Ana, Tustin and neighboring communities.
