items.lineage: Viet remix circulates Vietnamese songs in remixed dance versions, nonstop DJ programmes and online listening communities. Pop ballads and older sentimental repertoire can acquire energetic electronic arrangements, while Vinahouse club practice forms a prominent overlapping branch.
items.description: Recognizable Vietnamese melodies and recorded vocals ride driving electronic rhythms and repeating dance hooks. Continuous mixes connect remade songs through transitions, while individual remixes range from club-oriented arrangements to faster social-media edits.

items.name: Vintage Chanson
items.lineage: Vintage chanson gathers older French-language popular song from café-concert, cabaret, music hall and early recording culture. Comic portraits, sentimental melodies and dramatic narratives foreground the singer and the text, with accompaniment ranging from piano to small bands and orchestras.
items.description: Text-led solo singing carries humorous scenes, intimate sentiment and social observation. In the piano-accompanied branch, clear declamation and chordal support leave space for verbal inflection and changing dramatic character.

items.name: Deep Deep House
items.lineage: Deep deep house is a discovery label connecting producers and DJs in warm, melodic deep-house networks. Continuous mixes join rounded bass, fluid synth melodies and occasional vocal passages into extended dance-floor sequences.
items.description: Restrained house grooves support flowing melodic phrases and softly layered electronic textures. Long transitions keep the pulse continuous while vocal and instrumental selections alternate.

items.name: Deep Deep Tech House
items.lineage: Deep deep tech house is a discovery label within groove-led house and techno production. Its DJs connect compact rhythmic patterns, low melodic lines and electronic club textures through sustained mixed programmes.
items.description: A recurring club pulse supports clipped rhythmic detail and darker melodic lines. Layered selection and gradual transitions maintain momentum across house, minimal and techno material.

items.name: Hard Minimal Techno
items.lineage: Hard minimal techno connects minimal club producers around economical percussion, prominent bass figures and cut-up vocal material. DJ programmes develop these elements through repeated grooves and transitions between records.
items.description: Clicking percussion and compact bass grooves give the music a direct club pulse. Brief vocal cuts and small changes in texture punctuate extended mixed passages.

items.name: Cosmic Uplifting Trance
items.lineage: Cosmic uplifting trance is a discovery label for melodic trance producers and their remix networks. Euphoric melodies, piano or plucked counter-lines and club-oriented arrangements connect this repertoire to uplifting and progressive trance.
items.description: A DJ-led rendition sequences melodic dance selections through energetic transitions and sustained rhythmic passages. Vocal and instrumental records can share the programme.

items.name: Focus Trance
items.lineage: Focus trance is a discovery label connecting melodic progressive producers and DJs. Its repertoire links trance-inflected melodies with progressive-house sequencing and gradually evolving electronic textures.
items.description: Layered melodic selections unfold over steady dance rhythms, with long transitions and changing atmospheric textures. A continuous DJ programme can include both vocal and instrumental passages.

items.name: Glitter Trance
items.lineage: Glitter trance is a discovery label linking melodic electronic producers and DJs across progressive house, trance and chill-out. Its mixed programmes connect flowing melodies and vocal passages with sustained electronic dance grooves.
items.description: Melodic selections move through quiet introductions, steady dance passages and gently evolving transitions. Vocal and instrumental textures alternate over a continuous mixed programme.

items.name: Classic Pakistani Pop
items.lineage: Classic Pakistani pop revisits the established popular-song repertoire that musicians carry into new concerts and recordings. Guitar-led bands, electronic keyboards and memorable Urdu melodies connect earlier studio pop with later pop-rock, while retrospective productions bring familiar songs to new listeners.
items.description: Sung melodies and recurring guitar figures sit over bass and a steady kit pulse, with keyboards adding harmonic colour. Band renditions balance intimate lyric delivery with fuller rhythmic passages, while the wider repertoire also includes dance-pop and other regional instrumental colours.

items.name: Pop Cristiano
items.lineage: Pop cristiano connects Spanish-language popular songwriting with Christian faith and testimony. Artists and bands circulate melodic songs through churches, independent labels, radio and digital platforms, joining devotional themes to contemporary pop and regional musical influences.
items.description: Memorable sung melodies and recurring refrains carry reflection, hope and personal devotion. Acappella editions foreground the vocal lines, while acoustic bands and electronic production give other songs fuller rhythmic and harmonic support.

items.name: Pop EDM
items.lineage: Pop EDM connects melody-led popular songwriting with electronic dance production. Radio hooks, remixes and club versions circulate between streaming releases, DJ sets and festival stages, bringing recognizable songs into dance-floor arrangements.
items.description: Songful melodies and recurring hooks sit over electronic dance pulses, with transitions and extended arrangements shaping the DJ branch. Performers balance approachable pop phrasing with club momentum; different tracks and live arrangements retain a wide range of vocal and instrumental colours.

items.name: Thai Folk Pop
items.lineage: Thai folk pop brings intimate songwriting and acoustic textures into popular-song settings. Singer-songwriters, small bands and mixed listening programmes connect local lyrics and folk influences with contemporary melodic pop, alongside the wider Thai indie and rural-song fields.
items.description: Clear vocal melodies and recurring song sections often sit against strummed accompaniment and modest band textures. DJ listening programmes also carry this repertoire, connecting whole songs while preserving their recorded vocal and instrumental layers.

items.name: Vintage Cantonese Pop
items.lineage: Vintage Cantonese pop brings older Cantonese popular songs into present-day listening and performance. Film and stage repertories, dance-song arrangements and later television themes connect Hong Kong with audiences across southern China and Southeast Asia, while revivals keep familiar melodies in circulation.
items.description: Memorable melodies and expressive song phrasing link early screen songs with later popular standards. Western dance rhythms and regional melodic traditions meet in varied arrangements; instrumental adaptations carry the tunes into intimate plucked-string performance.

items.name: Vintage Italian Pop
items.lineage: Vintage Italian pop connects older canzone, radio entertainment and popular dance-song repertories with later revivals. Singers and instrumentalists brought regional melodies, swing and other international dance rhythms into records, variety shows and television, leaving a repertoire still performed in new arrangements.
items.description: Tuneful phrasing and memorable refrains range from lyrical songs to witty, rhythmically animated numbers. Swing-inflected harmony and dance accents are prominent in one branch, with piano adaptations retaining the melody while reworking the accompaniment.

items.name: Vintage Norwegian Pop
items.lineage: Vintage Norwegian pop gathers older popular songs, revues, schlager and dance melodies into a continuing listening repertoire. Radio performers and record artists helped these songs circulate nationally, while songbooks and new performances keep familiar melodies active beyond their original recording era.
items.description: Clear melodic lines and recognizable refrains carry affectionate, reflective and humorous texts. Accompaniments range from small voice-and-piano settings to dance bands and orchestras; the default follows the intimate songbook branch with direct singing and chordal support.

items.name: Abstract IDM
items.lineage: Abstract IDM develops the experimental side of electronic listening music through unstable rhythms, resampling and evolving textures. Independent producers and labels connect detailed digital editing with ambience and melodic fragments, treating irregularity and transformation as compositional material.
items.description: Fractured beats and bass patterns interact with granular textures, drifting pads and uncertain melodic phrases. Repetition gives way to small mutations, irregular attacks and changing layers, with studio processing shaping both the rhythm and the surrounding space.

items.name: Canadian Psychedelic
items.lineage: Canadian psychedelic music connects late1960s garage and experimental song bands with electronic, folk-derived and later revival practices. Toronto and other regional scenes developed amplified improvisation, unusual textures and adventurous songwriting within local clubs, record labels and touring circuits.
items.description: Fuzzed guitar figures and a forceful bass-and-drum pulse support intertwined singing and changing keyboard colors. Organ sustain and piano chords give this band branch contrasting weight, while improvisatory passages and shifting song structures open beyond concise garage-rock forms.

items.name: Charva
items.lineage: Charva connects northern English peer identity with bassline rap, party culture and local musical networks. Bradford acts helped carry regional slang and rapid MC delivery into club sets, online videos and pop-facing releases, while the wider audience crosses several northern dance styles.
items.description: Direct, rhythmic verses and shared hooks ride buoyant bassline beats and recurring organ-like figures. MCs and DJs sustain a lively party flow, alternating individual bars with collective vocal energy; local identity and humour connect recordings with live performance.

items.name: Deep Chill-Out
items.lineage: Deep chill-out is a listening-oriented discovery field within ambient and downtempo culture. Its producers and selectors connect spacious electronic production with choral, acoustic and cinematic material in reflective programmes.
items.description: Slow-moving textures and gently joined selections create a spacious listening flow. A curated DJ programme can pass between choral voices, piano, classical music and electronica without reducing them to one fixed studio ensemble.

items.name: Game Mood
items.lineage: Game Mood gathers music circulated through online role-playing communities, especially the NoPixel scene. Performers and producers create songs for fictional identities and venues while releasing them to real listeners beyond the game.
items.description: A rap-led branch places rhythmic verses over produced beats. Recorded songs circulate through streamed in-game performances, while the broader community also includes sung pop and other electronic styles.

items.name: Música Prehispánica
items.lineage: Música prehispánica is a discovery field around the sound heritage of pre-colonial Mesoamerica and its modern reinterpretation. Archaeological instruments, replicas, Indigenous musical continuities and newly composed or improvised works inform a varied repertoire; surviving objects do not establish the original melodies or a single universal tuning system.
items.description: An experimental flute branch explores simultaneous pitches, breath-shaped attacks and changing fingerings on a three-tube ceramic aerophone. Other interpretations combine whistles, shells, percussion, voices or electronic sound, connecting historical inquiry with contemporary performance.

items.name: No Beat
items.lineage: No Beat is a Brazilian producer-and-MC discovery label spanning digitally circulated funk, arrochadeira remixes and trap-funk collaborations. Producer signatures and recurring vocal partnerships connect the releases; the name does not signify music without a beat.
items.description: Rhythmic vocal lines ride producer-built beats, with short hooks and dance-driven repetitions. This profile represents a rap-and-funk production branch within a wider catalogue of remixes and regional dance styles.

items.name: Salsa International
items.lineage: Salsa International is a discovery label connecting singers, orchestras and dance repertoires across the international salsa circuit. Classic son-derived arrangements, harder orchestral grooves and romantic songs circulate together through recordings, touring bands and social dancing.
items.description: Interlocking piano and percussion support sung lines, answering voices and instrumental phrases. Larger horn bands are prominent, while intimate café ensembles preserve the dance pulse with a smaller acoustic palette; the default represents a flute, piano and hand-percussion branch.

items.name: Scottish Hush
items.lineage: Scottish Hush is a discovery label connecting Scottish independent songwriters and bands, from intimate acoustic performances to fuller arrangements. Personal storytelling and collaborations link its folk, pop and independent-rock strands.
items.description: An acoustic branch sets a single singing voice against intricate nylon-string guitar. Percussive fingerwork and flowing melodic figures support reflective words, while the wider field also includes amplified bands and collaborative ensembles.

items.name: Śląskie Piosenki
items.lineage: Śląskie piosenki connects popular songs circulating through Silesian performers, regional entertainment and domestic music-making. Romantic schlager, family songs and dance-oriented refrains appear alongside adaptations and local-language repertoire.
items.description: Recognizable song melodies and clear chord progressions make the repertoire accessible for singing and instrumental play. A domestic piano rendition carries the tune above chordal support, alongside the vocal duos, bands and electronic arrangements heard across the wider field.

items.name: Tallava
items.lineage: Tallava developed among Roma and Ashkali communities in Kosovo and neighboring Balkan regions, spreading through weddings, celebrations and diaspora networks. Extended improvisation and responsive singing link older voice-and-frame-drum practices with electronic keyboard ensembles.
items.description: A singer stretches words into melismatic phrases over sustained keyboard support and a recurring dance pulse. Clarinet motifs and keyboard leads answer and elaborate the line, while the performance expands around guests, dedications and dancers rather than a fixed short-song form.

items.name: Vintage Old-Time
items.lineage: Vintage old-time gathers early rural American song and instrumental recordings, connecting mountain ballads, string-band dance tunes, sacred songs and country blues. Radio, commercial records and later reissues carried local performers to wider audiences and helped transmit repertoire to subsequent generations.
items.description: Story-led singing can stand over a lightly picked acoustic guitar, while other branches use fiddle, banjo and small string-band combinations. The default represents the intimate singer-guitarist branch with a clear melody and space for the narrative.

items.name: Vintage Radio Show
items.lineage: Vintage Radio Show gathers archival broadcast entertainment, including serial drama, comedy, literary readings and spoken storytelling. Network transmission, syndication and later record reissues carried these programmes beyond their original local audiences.
items.description: In the solo storytelling branch, a narrator shapes pacing, diction and character through speech, leaving the story unobscured by accompaniment. The broader archive also contains ensemble acting, comic dialogue, musical interludes and sound effects.

items.name: Wind Symphony
items.lineage: Wind symphonies perform composed concert repertoire with woodwind, brass and percussion musicians. Their institutional programmes connect historical wind-band and Harmonie arrangements with new commissioned music, and may include smaller chamber formations alongside the full ensemble.
items.description: Blended reeds and brass alternate sustained harmony with articulated melodic passages. The default represents a chamber concert branch: paired oboes, clarinets, horns and bassoons are joined by flute and bowed double bass, while larger symphonic programmes draw on additional brass and percussion.

items.name: Deep Soul House
items.lineage: Deep soul house gathers a contemporary house discovery community drawing on deep-house, soul and disco traditions. Producers and DJs connect harmonic warmth and repeated rhythmic patterns with underground dance-floor circulation.
items.description: Continuous house selections develop through track transitions and changing rhythmic or harmonic textures. The DJ branch retains the recorded layers inside its mixed programme.

items.name: Deep Tropical House
items.lineage: Deep tropical house connects melodic, vocal-centered house with the softer textures of the 2010s tropical-house crossover. Producers and DJs link radio-friendly songs with club and festival sets.
items.description: Light rhythmic motion, clear melodic hooks and vocal warmth connect deep-house pacing with tropical-pop arrangements. Plucked synth colors, sampled or recorded instrumental layers and accessible song structures appear across the repertoire. DJ sets may lift the energy beyond the gentler radio versions.

items.name: Soulful House
items.lineage: Soulful house connects house rhythms with soul and gospel singing, jazz-derived harmony and producer-DJ communities. Labels, vocalists and musicians sustain the field through releases, remixes and dance-floor programmes.
items.description: A flowing DJ programme presents layered soulful house selections with a steady dance pulse. Mixing within and between records maintains rhythmic continuity while recorded vocals and instrumental layers remain in the programme.

items.name: Deep German Hip Hop
items.lineage: Deep German hip hop gathers German-language underground and independent rap artists whose careers connect recorded releases, online video battles and live competitive circuits. Performers such as Cashisclay, Twizzy and Punch Arogunz move between these overlapping spaces. Written a cappella events provide one performance branch alongside their wider recorded repertoire.
items.description: Prepared rhymes, rhythmic speech and emphatic phrasing foreground verbal delivery. In the unaccompanied battle branch, two MCs take alternating turns, allowing cadence, pauses and changes of emphasis to shape the performance without an instrumental backing.

items.name: Drill brasileiro
items.lineage: Brazilian drill localizes Chicago and British drill influences within Brazil’s rap scenes, developing through performers such as Vandal, LEALL, VND and L7nnon. MCs and producers connect its heavy beats with Portuguese flows, local street narratives, football culture and exchanges with Brazilian funk.
items.description: Sliding electronic bass, distinctive hi-hat and snare placements, and forceful rhythmic verses form a recognizable production vocabulary. Brazilian artists adapt these patterns to local language and experience, with collaboration and overlap across grime, trap and funk communities.

items.name: Emo Trap Italiana
items.lineage: Emo trap italiana connects Italian-language emotional songwriting with trap and rock influences. Artists move between rap-led and melodic delivery, introspective themes and popular-song arrangements, including instrumental reinterpretations of their repertoire.
items.description: A solo piano rendition carries the song melody over chordal accompaniment. Connected melodic lines and a compact harmonic texture present the repertoire in an intimate acoustic setting.

items.name: New School Türkçe Rap
items.lineage: New school Türkçe rap gathers a contemporary Turkish-language rap cohort shaped by independent crews, producer collaborations and online circulation. Rhythmic verses move across trap, West Coast-influenced beats, grime and other current production styles.
items.description: A foreground MC delivers rhythmically articulated verses over a produced beat. Changes of flow and accent carry the phrasing, with backing textures left open to the chosen production.

items.name: Norwegian pop rap
items.lineage: Norwegian pop rap connects rhythmic verses with melodic hooks and popular-song production. Artists such as Karpe, Madcon and Paperboys helped bring Norwegian rap into radio and mainstream pop, while multilingual and diasporic influences widened its lyrical and melodic vocabulary.
items.description: Rap verses and sung refrains share space over programmed drums, sampled phrases and polished melodic backing. Songs move between personal stories, social observation and broadly accessible hooks. The field overlaps national hip-hop and contemporary Norwegian pop, with artists working across both audiences.

items.name: Outer Hip Hop
items.lineage: Outer hip hop gathers independent rap and producer networks including Canadian prairie musicians and their collaborators. Personal narratives, social observation and inventive wordplay meet producer-built beats through self-released recordings and small-label circulation.
items.description: Rhythmic lead verses sit over a produced beat in a compact studio arrangement. Verbal phrasing and changes of accent remain foregrounded, while the backing texture can vary between productions.

items.name: Deep Melodic Metalcore
items.lineage: Deep melodic metalcore gathers bands that combine heavy hardcore-derived attacks with melodic metal phrasing. Interlocking electric guitars, bass and drums support a foreground vocalist, balancing tightly accented riffs with more open melodic passages.
items.description: A heavy electric band balances palm-muted guitar attacks with melodic phrase development. Picked bass reinforces the low register, while a stick-driven kit joins a foreground lead voice.

items.name: Deep Metalcore
items.lineage: Deep metalcore is a discovery label connecting contemporary heavy bands with metal riffing, hardcore rhythm and contrasting vocal approaches. Amplified guitars and bass lock into forceful drums, with changes between dense attacks and more open phrases.
items.description: Palm-muted guitar figures and picked bass reinforce a heavy stick-driven pulse. Contrasting vocal parts move between compact rhythmic attacks and broader phrases, while electronic textures extend the amplified band sound.

items.name: Deep Happy Hardcore
items.lineage: Deep happy hardcore gathers a contemporary hardcore producer and DJ cohort around fast dance beats, buoyant melodic hooks and energetic vocal refrains. Label mixes and club performances connect established UK hardcore practices with internationally circulating releases.
items.description: An energetic DJ presentation joins melodic hardcore selections through continuous playback and transitions. The whole mixed programme retains its embedded voices and instrumental layers rather than treating them as a new live ensemble.

items.name: Deep Hardcore
items.lineage: Deep hardcore gathers an electronic hardcore discovery cohort with early rave, gabber and experimental club connections. Distorted rhythms, sampled phrases and changes of electronic texture circulate through records and DJ programmes; the field is distinct from hardcore punk instrumentation.
items.description: A continuous DJ programme connects older hardcore selections with contrasting rhythmic weight and atmosphere. This listening-oriented branch keeps the complete mixed repertoire and its embedded sound layers.

items.name: Deep Psychobilly
items.lineage: Deep psychobilly gathers underground and revival bands connecting rockabilly rhythm with punk force, twanging amplified guitars and horror or rowdy rock-and-roll imagery. The scene spans early British bands and later international performers.
items.description: A foreground lead voice rides a percussive slapped upright bass, forceful electric-guitar chords and a stick-driven drum kit. The compact band texture combines rockabilly bounce with a heavier punk attack.

items.name: Deep Soft Rock
items.lineage: Deep soft rock is a discovery label around melodic soft-rock songwriters and musicians whose work often crosses pop, jazz and soul. Piano-led arrangements, expressive sung melodies and supple rhythm sections sit alongside the broader guitar-led and richly arranged repertoire.
items.description: A clear sung melody and chordal piano sit over a relaxed bass-and-drum foundation. The song remains central, with room for rhythmic inflection and brief instrumental elaboration rather than a fixed notion of sonic depth.

items.name: Rebel Blues
items.lineage: Rebel blues is a discovery field connecting forceful rock songs, blues-inflected voices and cinematic pop. Its repertoire includes artists whose work circulates through film, television and promotional soundtracks, alongside quieter arrangements of the same songwriters.
items.description: Memorable melodic hooks and dramatic contrasts link the repertoire across band, electronic and acoustic treatments. Piano arrangements bring out the song melody and chordal support without reproducing the original vocal or production layers.

items.name: Boom Bap Español
items.lineage: Boom bap español gathers Spanish-language rap shaped by beatmaking traditions and a foregrounded MC. Producers and rappers sustain an underground network through collaborations, releases and performance, with recurring rhythmic backings supporting narrative, wordplay and confrontational delivery.
items.description: A single rhythmic rap lead works against a produced beat. The representative arrangement emphasizes sharply articulated phrases and a steady rhythmic foundation, leaving the backing’s specific sampled or synthesized architecture open.

items.name: Classic Bollywood
items.lineage: Classic Bollywood gathers the enduring playback-song repertoire associated with Hindi cinema and its established singers and music directors. Romantic melodies, memorable refrains and contrasting instrumental passages circulate through recordings, film revivals and new instrumental arrangements.
items.description: Melody remains prominent across intimate ballads and larger film arrangements. Piano adaptations carry the tune over chordal support, preserving the song while allowing a smaller acoustic presentation.

items.name: Classic Cantopop
items.lineage: Classic Cantopop brings enduring Hong Kong popular songs and television and film themes into renewed listening and performance. Cantonese songwriting developed alongside Western pop and rock influences, with singers and songwriters such as Sam Hui helping establish its local voice.
items.description: Lyrical tunes, familiar refrains and expressive contrasts connect ballads, film themes and more rhythmic songs. Piano adaptations let the melody and harmonic accompaniment carry this repertoire in an intimate instrumental setting.

items.name: Covertrance
items.lineage: Covertrance gathers dance-oriented cover versions and reinterpretations of familiar songs and themes. Trance and club producers recast recognizable melodies through electronic arrangements, vocal versions and instrumental mixes, with lounge adaptations also circulating in the wider catalogue.
items.description: Recognizable hooks meet repeating electronic bass, synthesizer figures and a steady programmed club pulse. Sung versions and extended instrumental treatments can reshape the same material for different listening and dancing settings.

items.name: Covertronica
items.lineage: Covertronica gathers electronic dance reinterpretations of familiar songs, connecting vocal remakes and remix production with club and streaming circulation. Producers rebuild recognizable hooks for contemporary dance arrangements, while DJs bring those records into continuous programmes.
items.description: In the club-programming branch, a DJ blends electronic cover records into a continuous dance sequence. Recorded voices and instrumental layers remain embedded in the tracks, with transitions shaping momentum between familiar songs.

items.name: Deep Chill
items.lineage: Deep chill connects relaxed electronic listening with lounge, Balearic and chill-house repertoire. Producers and selectors circulate melodic recordings through albums, compilations and continuous radio mixes, balancing gentle rhythmic movement with spacious textures.
items.description: Unhurried transitions and contrasting recorded selections sustain a relaxed listening flow. Instrumental colors and occasional vocals share the programme, while restrained grooves support rather than dominate the atmosphere.

items.name: Deep Comedy
items.lineage: Deep Comedy gathers recorded stand-up and comic monologues circulated through comedy clubs, specialist labels and streaming discovery. Personal stories, social observation and topical jokes depend on speech rhythm, pauses and audience address rather than a sung melody.
items.description: A solo comic shapes a spoken monologue through conversational emphasis, pauses, character and punchline timing. Dark social observation and everyday storytelling coexist within this recorded-comedy discovery field.

items.name: Deep Rai
items.lineage: Deep rai is a discovery label connecting Algerian and wider Maghrebi popular-song repertoires with diaspora producers and DJs. Its listening network includes singers such as Zahouania and Cheb Faycal alongside producers including DJ Kim, keeping older raï songs in circulation through contemporary records and dance programmes.
items.description: Expressive song melodies and recurring dance rhythms connect vocal recordings with electronic performance. In a club branch, mixed records interact with live keyboard-synthesizer lines; other parts of the repertoire retain different acoustic and electric accompaniments.

items.name: Deep Talent Show
items.lineage: Deep talent show gathers a deeper discovery cohort of televised singing-competition performers and their later recordings. Acoustic pop, close vocal harmonies and familiar song interpretations sit alongside fuller studio productions, connecting televised performances with independent releases and concert careers.
items.description: Blended lead and harmony voices carry a popular-song melody above acoustic-guitar chords and melodic fills. The compact acoustic branch highlights ensemble phrasing and song structure, while the broader discovery field also includes amplified bands and electronic production.

items.name: Downtempo Fusion
items.lineage: Downtempo fusion gathers artists combining relaxed electronic rhythms with song, jazz, soul and atmospheric production. Its discovery repertoire ranges from vocal-led groups to instrumental producers, with DJ programmes connecting these materials across listening and dance settings.
items.description: Layered selections unfold with relaxed pacing and gradual transitions. This DJ branch preserves recorded vocal and instrumental textures inside a continuous programme, alongside the field’s separately documented live-band and studio-production approaches.

items.name: Electropowerpop
items.lineage: Electropowerpop connects catchy pop-rock songwriting with electronic production, tuned vocal textures and dance-oriented rhythms. Its online discovery cohort includes bands and bedroom projects from the late-2000s alternative-pop scene, spanning electronic arrangements and expanded live guitar bands.
items.description: A tuned sung lead moves through compact pop hooks above electronic textures and a guitar, bass and drum foundation. Clean guitar figures and a locked bass pulse leave space for the electronic layers, while the live rhythm section gives the arrangement physical drive.

items.name: Emoplugg
items.lineage: Emoplugg is an online melodic rap label linking emotional vocal expression with plugg-related electronic beat production. Its discovery community overlaps emo rap and melodic internet rap, with processed sung phrases and intimate lyrics carried by producer-built rhythms.
items.description: A melodic lead rides a produced beat, with vocal treatment shaping the intimate sung phrases. The arrangement leaves the beat mechanism open while keeping the singer and rhythmic production separately controllable.

items.name: Flick Hop
items.lineage: Flick hop is a discovery label connecting underground rap producers and MCs across North American and European networks. Its artist corpus includes Snowgoons, Sicknature, Virtuoso, Chief Kamachi and related independent collaborators, with sample-based production and MC-led songs forming a prominent branch.
items.description: Rhythmic verses ride recurring sampled phrases and programmed drum patterns. Producers build a groove around the character of a chosen loop, adjusting drum weight and layering to its mood; other artists and releases extend the palette with keyboards, scratches and different vocal arrangements.

items.name: Groove Room
items.lineage: Groove Room brings together a contemporary network of melodic house producers and remixers. Labels and online DJ programmes connect rounded dance rhythms, tuneful electronic textures and vocal material with both club and relaxed listening.
items.description: Steady house pulses support smooth melodic phrases and recurring vocal or instrumental hooks. Mixed programmes extend the groove across tracks, balancing dance momentum with spacious transitions and polished electronic sound.

items.name: Muzică copii
items.lineage: Romanian music for children encompasses play songs, educational singing and purpose-composed instrumental repertoire. Composers and educators draw on folk idioms and contemporary popular material alongside graded pieces for young listeners and learners.
items.description: Clear melodic figures, compact forms and accessible contrasts support listening, singing and early musical learning. In the composed piano branch, connected lines and modest harmonic textures develop from simple ideas toward richer interplay.

items.name: Novos Talentos Brasileiros
items.lineage: Novos talentos brasileiros is a discovery label centered on emerging Brazilian singers, including a substantial cohort associated with televised youth singing competitions. Their repertoire crosses MPB, pop and regional song, and extends into independent releases and local concert appearances.
items.description: A small vocal ensemble shares popular-song melodies over acoustic-guitar figures and percussion. This intimate stage branch gives familiar repertoire a flexible group presentation, alongside the broader field’s larger television and studio arrangements.

items.name: Nubian Traditional
items.lineage: Nubian traditional music connects Nile Valley heritage with the musical lives of communities in Egypt, Sudan and their diasporas. Song, poetry and dance sustain local memories, while twentieth-century oud interpreters and amplified ensembles have developed contrasting concert and popular-song branches.
items.description: An intimate song branch pairs an expressive lead voice with ornamented, fretless oud lines. Other practices use group responses, frame drums and dance rhythms, and modern ensembles add amplified instruments. The repertoire carries memories of place and community across the Nile Valley and its diasporas.

items.name: Polka Norteña
items.lineage: Polka norteña is the northern Mexican adaptation of the European polka, developed through local dance, instrumental ensembles and commercial recordings. Its lively melodies and duple dance pulse circulate through accordion conjuntos, wind and string groups, and piano interpretations.
items.description: Clear melodic strains and a buoyant duple pulse shape this dance repertoire. A composed solo-piano interpretation carries melody and accompaniment within one instrument, alongside the more widely heard accordion and ensemble branches.

items.name: Proto-hyperpop
items.lineage: Proto-hyperpop gathers electronic-pop experimenters in an online discovery cohort spanning PC Music associates, digital pop producers and newer internet artists. Its repertoire connects exaggerated pop textures, electronic sound design and club mixing, with substantial overlap with hyperpop.
items.description: In the DJ branch, contrasting pop fragments and club tracks are joined through quick transitions, edits and playful changes of direction. Recorded voices and instrumental layers remain within the mixed programme.

items.name: Punjabi Lo-fi
items.lineage: Punjabi lo-fi connects Punjabi popular-song repertoire with online remix and bedroom-production communities. Producers such as MixSingh and Swattrex circulate new songs alongside softened, slowed and reverberant versions of existing recordings. The discovery field also overlaps bilingual South Asian pop and international lo-fi remix culture.
items.description: Sung melodies and existing instrumental layers can be retained within complete recorded-song reworkings. Slower pacing, extended reverberation and softened bandwidth reshape the listening texture, while the broader field also includes newly produced bedroom songs.

items.name: Remix Product
items.lineage: Remix product is a discovery label gathering commercial dance remixes, cover versions and edited club tracks. Its documented repertoire connects familiar vocal hooks with hands-up, hard-dance and other electronic club treatments, circulating through releases and mixed compilations.
items.description: An energetic DJ mix connects edited dance selections, contrasting melodic hooks and rhythmic drops. The playback-and-mixing branch retains recorded vocal and instrumental layers without pretending to identify every original production instrument.

items.name: Sky Room
items.lineage: Sky room is a discovery label connecting festival-oriented electronic dance producers. Its documented listening cohort brings together big-room, progressive and electro-house repertoire, with forceful rhythmic passages, melodic hooks and large-scale builds.
items.description: A DJ-led club presentation moves between melodic rises, rhythmic drops and contrasting recorded selections. Vocal and instrumental material can share the mix; the default preserves playback and mixing without inventing the original tracks’ instruments or hardware.

items.name: Slow Game
items.lineage: Slow game is an online discovery label connecting contemporary R&B singers, melodic rap collaborations and club-oriented DJ productions. Its cohort includes West Coast radio and mixtape networks alongside artists from other regions, with romantic hooks, rhythmic vocal exchanges and polished electronic backing.
items.description: The DJ branch presents sung hooks and rap passages within mixed recorded tracks, connecting R&B intimacy with club energy. The broader field also includes original songs and producer-led collaborations; the label does not prescribe a single tempo or a uniformly slow performance.

items.name: Speed Up Brasileiro
items.lineage: Speed Up Brasileiro gathers accelerated versions of Brazilian popular recordings circulating through streaming and short-video platforms. Singers and producers rework their own songs alongside remixers, shortening their temporal scale while retaining recognizable vocal hooks and backing tracks.
items.description: Accelerated sung phrases and a produced beat compress a familiar song into a brisk remix. Melody and accompaniment move together through continuous phrases, with pitch treatment varying between versions.

items.name: Twin Cities indie
items.lineage: Twin Cities indie encompasses independent music rooted in Minneapolis and Saint Paul. Its regional networks bring together guitar rock, pop songwriting and folk-influenced approaches, with electronic production also entering contemporary bands.
items.description: A vocal-led electric band combines strummed guitar, bass and acoustic drums with synthesizer layers and programmed percussion. This electronic indie-pop branch sits within a wider metropolitan community of contrasting sounds.

items.name: Voidgrind
items.lineage: Voidgrind groups underground extreme-metal discoveries, including death-metal bands with dense riffs and forceful rhythmic interplay. The listening cohort overlaps cavernous, technical and grinding metal practices rather than requiring a single playing technique.
items.description: Electric guitars move between accented riffs and lead phrases above picked bass and a forceful drum kit. A foreground voice joins the amplified band, with changes of density and articulation shaping its momentum.

items.name: Westcoast Flow
items.lineage: Westcoast flow gathers contemporary West Coast rap and melodic vocal production. The named discovery cohort includes Los Angeles artists who combine conversational rhythmic delivery, sung hooks and producer-led beats, with connections to local R&B and club music.
items.description: An alternating rap-and-sung foreground sits over layered sampled rhythmic and melodic phrases. This representative studio branch leaves vocal register and the balance of speech and melody open, while supporting a clear groove and compact hooks.

items.name: Deep Turkish Pop
items.lineage: Deep Turkish pop is a discovery grouping within Turkish popular song, spanning dance-oriented releases, melodic ballads and acoustic reinterpretations. Its repertoire circulates through recordings, remixes and published instrumental arrangements, with no single production style implied by the word deep.
items.description: In a solo-piano rendition, the song melody remains in the foreground above a light harmonic accompaniment. Connected phrasing carries the tune without reproducing the vocal timbre or studio backing of the original pop recording.

items.name: Carnaval de Cádiz
items.lineage: Cádiz Carnival sustains a civic tradition of topical songs, parody and costumed street performance. Neighborhood associations, rehearsals and the official competition connect coros, comparsas, chirigotas and cuartetos, each with its own vocal organization and repertoire. The tango, pasodoble, cuplé and comic sketch give these groups distinct ways to comment on public life.
items.description: Comic dialogue, topical verses and sung cuplés share the stage in the cuarteto branch, with buzzing carnival pitos providing pitch cues. Cádiz also sustains harmonized comparsas, guitar-and-percussion chirigotas and plucked-string coros, each with its own repertoire and ensemble practice.

items.name: Pop Electrónico
items.lineage: Pop electrónico connects Spanish-language songwriting with synthesized textures, programmed accompaniment and electronic performance. Its Latin American and diaspora scenes span intimate trip-hop-influenced songs, dance-oriented pop and more expansive live arrangements.
items.description: A melodic vocal line moves through synthesized layers and programmed accompaniment. Textured electronic layers connect intimate singing with the movement of dance-oriented pop.

items.name: Dark minimal techno
items.lineage: Dark minimal techno develops sparse, ominous club music through independent production and label communities. Plazma Records and related artists combine restrained rhythmic repetition with unusual recorded sounds, dissonant details and carefully spaced electronic figures.
items.description: Small loops, sampled transients and synthesizer patterns leave pronounced spaces between events. Gradual changes in filtering, repetition and placement sustain an uneasy atmosphere without requiring a dense wall of distortion.

items.name: Dutch Drill
items.lineage: Dutch drill developed through local rap networks and exchanges with British and American drill. Amsterdam and Rotterdam performers use neighborhood references, Dutch speech and varied personal subjects, with direct street rap and more melodic crossover approaches coexisting.
items.description: Rhythmic verses ride ominous produced beats, with sharply placed drum attacks and spaces that emphasize the rapper’s cadence. Local slang and neighborhood references shape the delivery; some artists favor melodic hooks or dance-oriented crossover arrangements.

items.name: Polish Trap
items.lineage: Polish trap connects local MCs and producers with international trap production and contemporary Polish rap. Online circulation and collaborations support a broad field, from direct verse-led delivery to melodic hooks and crossover songs.
items.description: Rap cadence and repeated phrases move against produced rhythmic and tonal backing. Direct verses coexist with melodic delivery and electronic textures; producers vary the density, mood and placement of the beat around the voice.

items.name: Soda Pop
items.lineage: Soda pop gathers romantic vocal-group pop and its revival performers, drawing especially on doo-wop and early rhythm-and-blues harmonies. Lead melodies, answering voices and repeated backing syllables carry compact songs; contemporary vocal ensembles keep this repertoire in circulation alongside historical recordings.
items.description: Interlocking lead and backing voices shape tuneful, harmony-led songs with rhythmic vocables and recurring refrains. A cappella groups emphasize the blend and conversational exchange of the voices, while related recordings also use instrumental rhythm sections.

items.name: Deep Pop EDM
items.lineage: Deep Pop EDM is a melodic dance-pop discovery field connecting electronic producers, songwriters and featured singers. Catchy melodies and relaxed house-inflected movement coexist with acoustic instrumental colors and radio-oriented arrangements.
items.description: A clear vocal melody sits among gentle piano figures, lyrical saxophone lines and electronic accompaniment. The balance favors memorable melodic phrases and an approachable dance pulse, while other artists emphasize different acoustic and electronic colors.

items.name: Twee Indie Pop
items.lineage: Twee indie pop links small-label guitar-pop songs, understated vocals and bright melodic hooks across international independent scenes. Its discovery repertoire connects older DIY releases with later bands and collaborations, sharing the intimate scale and melodic directness associated with twee pop.
items.description: Clear guitar figures, bass and a modest drum backbeat frame an unshowy lead vocal. Melodic details and concise song forms take priority over spectacle, while the wider field also includes acoustic collaborations and richer studio arrangements.

items.name: Deep Big Room
items.lineage: Deep big room gathers a deeper discovery cohort of festival-oriented electronic producers. Strong melodic hooks, staged builds and forceful drops connect big-room house with trance and progressive-house influences, circulating through releases, remixes and mixed programmes.
items.description: Bright leads, emphatic kick patterns and build-and-release phrasing give the repertoire its large-scale dance energy. Recorded mixing links selections into longer programmes, including club and exercise settings.

items.name: czsk electropop
items.lineage: CZSK Electropop connects Czech and Slovak electronic-pop artists, from independent synthesizer projects to singer-led productions. Local radio, clubs and cross-border collaborations bring together Czech, Slovak and English-language songs.
items.description: A sung melody moves against synthesizer hooks and programmed rhythm. Retro electronic colors coexist with contemporary production, visual presentation and varied song forms; acoustic and more experimental approaches also appear within the field.

items.name: Melanesian Pop
items.lineage: Melanesian pop connects popular-song communities across Papua New Guinea, the Solomon Islands and neighboring Pacific networks. Touring singers and bands combine local languages and melodies with reggae, R&B and other contemporary song styles.
items.description: Lead and supporting voices meet guitar, bass, keyboards and percussion in a dance-oriented band setting. Repeating song phrases and relaxed or lively grooves carry local language and identity across an active regional touring circuit.

items.name: Marathi hip hop
items.lineage: Marathi hip hop gives Maharashtra’s regional language and local experiences a place within Indian rap. Artists such as Sambata build on international hip-hop influences while using Marathi vernaculars to express neighborhood identity, personal ambition and social criticism.
items.description: Rhythmic verses and emphatic phrasing move over producer-built beats. Repeated drum patterns, edited samples and contrasting backing textures support rhyme, flow and narrative, while collaborations connect local voices to wider Indian hip-hop production.

items.name: Study Beats
items.lineage: Study beats developed within online instrumental hip-hop listening, where beatmakers, labels and streaming channels connect relaxed grooves with studying and everyday concentration. Chillhop and its collaborators helped circulate this listening culture through curated streams, compilations and producer exchanges.
items.description: Repeating sampled phrases and carefully spaced drum patterns create a steady instrumental backdrop. Jazz and soul colours, soft melodic fragments and restrained changes are common, while producers also develop original compositions. The music can reward attentive listening as well as accompany study.

items.name: Greek Fem Rap
items.lineage: Greek fem rap brings women-led rap and feminist organizing into Greece’s wider hip-hop communities. Independent recordings, collective performances and local networks connect personal testimony, social criticism and changing approaches to beat-making.
items.description: Rhythmic verses, punchlines and repeated vocal phrases move over produced beats. Direct speech-like delivery can open into melodic hooks, while arrangements range from sparse rap backing to more elaborate electronic and traditional influences.

items.name: Deep Discofox
items.lineage: Deep discofox is a discovery label within German-language party and Schlager music. Familiar vocal hooks, recurring dance rhythms and festive refrains connect its performers to discofox dancing, party releases and club DJ programmes.
items.description: Direct melodies and steady dance patterns keep the repertoire accessible for communal celebration and partner dancing. DJs connect songs through mixed sets, while party-oriented recordings share space with Schlager and popular dance music.

items.name: Dutch Indie
items.lineage: Dutch indie connects independent musicians, small labels and live venues across the Netherlands. DIY collaboration links guitar bands with folk, electronic pop and more experimental songwriting; labels such as Snowstar and international showcases help these overlapping local networks reach listeners abroad.
items.description: Interlocking guitars, bass and drums can support conversational vocals, melodic refrains and deliberately rough edges. Other branches favor intimate folk or electronic textures. Collaboration and independent circulation connect the field without imposing one language, ensemble or production style.

items.name: Hjemmesnekk
items.lineage: Hjemmesnekk is the participatory song-making strand of Norwegian russetid. Graduation groups write and record their own identities into songs, sometimes making the backing themselves and often collaborating with professional producers. The finished recordings circulate at celebrations and through streaming platforms.
items.description: Catchy sung refrains, personal group lyrics and a produced rhythmic backing connect collective participation with studio songcraft. Singers record repeated takes and producers shape the vocal balance, pitch and arrangement; the music can borrow from dance, pop and rap rather than requiring a single beat style.

items.name: Belarusian Hip Hop
items.lineage: Belarusian hip hop connects local and diaspora rap communities through Belarusian- and Russian-language writing. International hip-hop influences meet neighborhood experience, personal reflection and changing social contexts, with artists moving between underground releases and wider popular circulation.
items.description: Rhythmic spoken verses ride producer-built beats, leaving space for rhyme, accent and personal narrative. Some artists emphasize Belarusian vernacular expression, while melodic collaborations and live-band experiments widen the field.

items.name: Rap Regio
items.lineage: Rap regio connects Monterrey and its surrounding communities through local MCs, studios, producers and independent releases. Neighborhood networks and collaborations have sustained both lyrical rap and changing electronic production practices.
items.description: Rhythmic verses, personal narratives and local expressions move over producer-built beats. Repetition and contrasting backing textures support rhyme and flow, while the regional scene embraces multiple production approaches.

items.name: gothic alternative
items.lineage: Gothic Alternative brings together alternative-rock and metal artists whose songs combine emotive singing with heavier guitar textures. The discovery field overlaps gothic rock and gothic metal while also including melodic hard-rock, acoustic and electronically produced branches.
items.description: A melodic lead voice contrasts with overdriven guitar lines, a grounded bass pulse and a firm drum backbeat. Piano chords can support quieter passages or reinforce the harmony as the band builds in intensity.

items.name: Aesthetic Rap
items.lineage: Aesthetic rap developed through online rap communities, SoundCloud releases and collaborative Discord networks. Its artists connect internet imagery and short, memorable tracks with varied approaches to sample-based production.
items.description: Restrained rhythmic voices contrast with bright sampled melodies and hard drum patterns. Other branches favor hazy production and reverberant vocals; internet circulation links these approaches without making every recording sound alike.

items.name: Libyan Hip Hop
items.lineage: Libyan hip hop joins local MCs and producers with diaspora collaborators. Rhythmic Arabic writing has carried personal experience, public criticism and changing hopes, while studio networks connect artists in Libya with the wider North African scene.
items.description: Direct rap phrasing rides producer-built beats and repeating rhythmic foundations. Language, flow and lyrical viewpoint shape the delivery; some projects also bring local instruments into the production, widening the field without prescribing one ensemble.

items.name: Russian Trap Metal
items.lineage: Russian trap metal connects aggressive rap delivery and metal-influenced vocal intensity with producer-built beats. Artists in Russia and the diaspora use online releases and collaborations to move between trap, heavy electronic music and metal aesthetics.
items.description: Forceful bars and screams sit above hard rhythmic production. Vocal distortion and abrupt changes can heighten the tension, while beatmakers shape the backing through varied electronic methods; individual tracks may add guitars or other layers.

items.name: Glitch Beats
items.lineage: Glitch beats brings finely edited rhythms and synthetic sound design into experimental electronic production. Its discovery community spans intimate studio composition, beat-oriented pieces and manipulated digital textures.
items.description: Short synthesized tones and intricately placed rhythmic events create patterns that shift between groove and interruption. Detailed software editing lets small attacks, pauses and timbral changes shape the arrangement.

items.name: Taiwanese Indie
items.lineage: Taiwanese Indie is an overlapping independent-song discovery category spanning rock, folk and experimental band practice. The selected Sorry Youth approach brings three singing members together with electric guitar, bass and drums; regional-language song is one documented practice within the broader independent scene.
items.description: Independent songs combine personal expression, everyday imagery and varied rock, folk and experimental textures. This representative live-band arrangement retains group singing, clean electric guitar, bass and drums. Taiwan Indie and Taiwanese Indie overlap as scene terms and named discovery cohorts; no exclusive language or universal stylistic boundary is asserted.

items.name: Flamenco Fusion
items.lineage: Flamenco fusion extends flamenco singing, guitar and dance through contemporary composition and cross-cultural collaboration. Acoustic companies and larger amplified ensembles coexist, connecting Andalusian musical vocabulary with new theatrical and popular-music settings.
items.description: Ornamented singing and sharply articulated guitar interweave with percussion and the dancer’s rhythmic footwork. Contrasting vocal passages and instrumental responses create a theatrical dialogue, while contemporary arrangements can draw on a wider palette.

items.name: Redneck
items.lineage: Redneck is a discovery label connecting rural Southern rap, country crossover and related rock performers. Storytelling about backroads, working life and outdoor gatherings links much of this repertoire, while MC-and-DJ performances coexist with expanded live bands.
items.description: In the MC-and-DJ branch, rhythmic storytelling is carried by recorded beats and country-inflected backing. The live lead remains separate from the mixed accompaniment, preserving its embedded instrumental and vocal material.
